# Batch C: the complete Brownian motion paper

**Type:** epic · **Batch:** batch-c · **Priority:** P1 · **Plan sections:** §3.4, §3.9, §7.6, §7.9, §8.2, §9.3, §10.2, §17.7, §19.3 (traceability only)

## Background

Batch B proved the architecture on §§4–5. Batch C completes the paper: the introduction and its stated uncertainty, §1 on the osmotic pressure of suspended particles, §2's statistical-mechanical justification in full, §3's drag-and-equilibrium route to the diffusion coefficient, the closing, the honest inference route from displacements to the molecular number, measurement bias, the kitchen real-data mode, and complete source review. The statistical-mechanical foundation of §2 is not an optional omission merely because a reader can proceed without it; both the direct route and the full derivation are provided. Batch C's exit evidence is that all five sections and the surrounding text are covered, the historical inference exercise contains no modern-constant circularity, and the §17.6 acceptance scenario passes.

## Scope and Children

- `am-bm-readings-intro-s1-s3-l3tp`: R0–R3 for the introduction, §§1–3, and the closing.
- `am-bm-equations-s1-s3-u6j7`: equation records and Route A derivation chains.
- `am-bm-margin-entries-7fa4`: the seven required historian's-margin records.
- `am-bm-02-osmotic-partition-n13x`: BM-02 osmotic partition.
- `am-bm-03-configuration-integral-e84v`: BM-03 configuration integral.
- `am-bm-04-drift-diffusion-balance-fpow`: BM-04 drift–diffusion balance with the kicks-off Nägeli branch.
- `am-bm-07-infer-molecular-number-frf9`: BM-07 inference with synthetic and historical modes.
- `am-bm-08-measurement-bias-h1ye`: BM-08 localization noise, drift, and exposure models.
- `am-bm-07-kitchen-mode-mays`: the reader's own microscope video, calibration, and interval.
- `am-bm-kitchen-page-ny2o`: the `/kitchen` protocol and worksheet.
- `am-bm-misconceptions-2hk1`: the Brownian misconception ledger.
- `am-bm-results-cards-ft8k`: the results-face cards.
- `am-bm-e2e-complete-gmdb`: browser acceptance for the whole paper.
- `am-bm-review-physics-arfv`: physics review of every derivation (human gate).
- `am-bm-review-reader-x77h`: non-physicist R2 review and fifteen-minute tour test (human gate).
- `am-dod-brownian-2k4y`: the per-paper definition-of-done audit.

Related work owned elsewhere: the German review (`am-edn-review-german-brownian-cfh`), Journey II (`am-disc-journey-ii-shelf-zbli`, `am-disc-journey-ii-chain-pl6u`), the tour (`am-tour-15min-brownian-z034`), Perrin's data (`am-data-perrin-1909-p7ku`), inference primitives (`am-ref-inference-2w9`).

## Success Criteria

- [ ] All five sections, the introduction, and the closing have source blocks, reviewed translation, four readings, equation records, and anchors.
- [ ] BM-02, BM-03, BM-04, BM-07, and BM-08 meet the full instrument contract; the kitchen mode yields an interval from a test video.
- [ ] The historical inference exercise never lets a modern exact $k_B$ or $N_A$ enter data generation or inference.
- [ ] Identifiability of radius and molecular number is shown before any narrow interval.
- [ ] The seven margin records and at least six misconception entries exist with sources and instruments.
- [ ] The §17.6 scenario passes and the nine definition-of-done items are verified in `am-dod-brownian-2k4y`.

## Sequencing

1. After `am-bm-slice-retrospective-pp09`: readings and equations for §§1–3 in parallel; BM-02, BM-03, BM-04 in parallel.
2. `am-ref-inference-2w9` and `am-data-perrin-1909-p7ku` enable BM-07 and BM-08; both enable the kitchen mode, then the kitchen page.
3. Margin records, misconceptions, and results cards follow readings and equations.
4. Browser acceptance follows the instruments; the human reviews follow content completion; the tour and Journey II finish in the discovery epic; the DoD audit closes the batch.

## Considerations

- Synthetic trajectories stay labeled until a licensed real sequence exists (`am-later-real-brownian-sequence-o6l3`).
- The kitchen mode reads video locally and uploads nothing.
- Einstein's velocity warning: verify whether the 1905 text states it; otherwise attribute it to the 1906 and later papers.
- The 1911 viscosity correction belongs to the dissertation; this paper's margin links to the companion record rather than absorbing it.

title: Batch B reference slice: Brownian motion sections 4 and 5 end to end
description:
# Batch B reference slice: Brownian motion sections 4 and 5 end to end

**Type:** epic · **Batch:** batch-b · **Priority:** P0 · **Plan sections:** §7.4, §8.2, §9.3, §14.3, §17.6, §19.2, §19.7 (traceability only)

## Background

The first thing Annus Mirabilis builds end to end is **the distribution argument and the measurable displacement** of the Brownian motion paper (Ann. Phys. (4) 17, 549–560, received 11 May 1905), sections 4 and 5, with the required explanation of the diffusion coefficient and links back to sections 1–3. This slice was chosen because it exercises almost everything the architecture must prove at once:

- German and English alignment on a real source passage;
- probability and calculus drill-downs through the foundation library and the return stack;
- semantic equations with derivation chains and a marked move;
- a real seeded numerical owner (the FrankenSim `brownian_frames` and `diffusion1d_frames` exports in the slim WASM artifact, plus the audited TypeScript reference evaluator as a labeled fallback);
- a graph and a microscope view of **one accepted snapshot**;
- units across microscopic scales (micrometers, seconds, mPa·s);
- model limits and typed non-numeric results (the point distribution at $t = 0$);
- mobile operation at 320 px, the no-algebra entrance, equivalent nonvisual actions, and a discovery path.

The governing rule for this epic: **do not generalize the framework until this slice exposes which abstractions help.** The slice is a proving ground. Abstractions that turn out to help are recorded in the retrospective and only then generalized for the other papers; abstractions that do not help are dropped.

The slice also delivers the P0 row of the innovation sequence: the no-algebra Brownian entrance plus a complete advanced explanation of the same step; equivalent nonvisual actions and the reading-only path; and typed results, exact identities, command classes, and safe snapshot ownership. P0 work is not a license to postpone the other papers.

## Scope and Children

- `am-bm-readings-s4-s5-uqbb`: R0–R3 readings for §§4–5 and the explanation of $D$ with links back to §§1–3.
- `am-bm-equations-s4-s5-6r81`: equation records and derivation chains for §§4–5 (variance of a sum, the transition-kernel expansion, the diffusion equation, the Gaussian, $\lambda_x = \sqrt{2Dt}$, the inversion for $N$).
- `am-bm-slice-foundations-f5z9`: the foundation nodes and zero-algebra bridges the slice calls.
- `am-bm-01-tracer-ensemble-hdly`: BM-01 tracer ensemble and observable selection, including the velocity trap.
- `am-bm-05-random-steps-ntzl`: BM-05 random steps to diffusion.
- `am-bm-06-gaussian-spread-982y`: BM-06 Gaussian spread, point distribution at $t = 0$, radial law, FTCS comparison.
- `am-bm-first-encounter-fjvh`: the no-algebra first encounter "zero average is not no movement."
- `am-bm-slice-discovery-route-tias`: the observable, Route B, the Exner fork, and the check against Einstein's printed numbers.
- `am-bm-slice-a11y-codesign-3xuq`: disabled readers run the slice's reasoning actions with their own tools (human gate).
- `am-bm-slice-e2e-sbqu`: the continuous browser acceptance journey with JSONL logs.
- `am-bm-slice-exit-demo-5922`: the recorded Batch B exit demonstration.
- `am-bm-acceptance-scenario-vjn4`: the full acceptance scenario with a reader unfamiliar with algebra plus a nonvisual check (human gate).
- `am-bm-slice-retrospective-pp09`: which abstractions helped; freeze of the shared reader and equation architecture.

Out of scope: §§1–3, the introduction, and the closing (Batch C, `am-ep-brownian-complete-6xe`); BM-02, BM-03, BM-04, BM-07, BM-08; the kitchen mode.

## Success Criteria

The Batch B exit demonstration, recorded against the running site:

- [ ] A reader opens the original passage about displacement (§5) on the German and English faces.
- [ ] The reader understands why the mean displacement can vanish while its square grows.
- [ ] The reader predicts the effect of changing viscosity and then sees the admitted comparison: doubling $\eta$ halves $D$ and multiplies the RMS displacement at fixed time by $1/\sqrt{2}$, not by $1/2$.
- [ ] The trace view and the distribution view show the same accepted snapshot (identical `instanceId`, `runId`, `snapshotVersion`).
- [ ] The reader opens the derivation of the square-root time dependence with the move marked.
- [ ] The reader returns to the source without losing position.
- [ ] The page remains intelligible when the simulation is unavailable (no WASM, no worker, JavaScript disabled).
- [ ] An assistive-technology user runs the same comparison (`am-bm-slice-a11y-codesign-3xuq`).
- [ ] The full derivation and the analytical and stochastic checks pass (historical fixture, modern golden scenario, adversarial fixtures, statistical tests).
- [ ] The §17.6 acceptance scenario has been run and recorded (`am-bm-acceptance-scenario-vjn4`).
- [ ] The retrospective records which abstractions helped and freezes the shared reader and equation architecture (`am-bm-slice-retrospective-pp09`).

## Sequencing

1. **Content track:** `am-edn-translation-brownian-s4-s5-jr4` then `am-bm-readings-s4-s5-uqbb` and `am-bm-equations-s4-s5-6r81` in parallel; `am-bm-first-encounter-fjvh` after the readings.
2. **Instrument track:** `am-ref-diffusion-lr3`, `am-fs-slim-artifact-0yh`, the runtime beads, and the view kit, then `am-bm-01-tracer-ensemble-hdly`, `am-bm-05-random-steps-ntzl`, `am-bm-06-gaussian-spread-982y` in parallel.
3. **Foundation track:** `am-found-library-infra-002t` then `am-bm-slice-foundations-f5z9`.
4. **Discovery track:** `am-disc-journey-framework-umbg` and `am-disc-knowledge-cards-iw8j`, then `am-bm-slice-discovery-route-tias` once the three instruments exist.
5. **Closure:** `am-bm-slice-e2e-sbqu` and `am-bm-slice-a11y-codesign-3xuq`, then `am-bm-slice-exit-demo-5922`, `am-bm-acceptance-scenario-vjn4`, `am-bm-slice-retrospective-pp09`. The retrospective gates the readings, equations, and instruments of Batches C through G.

## Considerations

- Human gates can stall the chain. Start recruiting disabled readers and a reader unfamiliar with algebra early, using `am-edit-comprehension-protocol-ouih`.
- No reviewed, licensed real Brownian observation sequence exists yet. Every demonstration trajectory is conspicuously labeled synthetic.
- Transcribe Einstein's printed numbers from the facsimile. With his printed constants ($R = 8.31\times10^{7}$ erg mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, $N = 6\times10^{23}$, viscosity $1.35\times10^{-2}$ poise, $T = 290.15$ K, $P = 0.5\,\mu$m) the kernel gives $\lambda_x \approx 0.795\,\mu$m at 1 s and $6.16\,\mu$m at 60 s; with the modern $k_B$ and the printed viscosity it gives $0.794$ and $6.15\,\mu$m. Einstein printed "about 0.8 μ" and "about 6 μ."
- The plan attributes to the 1905 text a warning that the observable is not a mean velocity. Verify it against the facsimile; the explicit apparent-velocity discussion appears in Einstein's 1906 "Zur Theorie der Brownschen Bewegung" and 1907–1908 notes, and if the 1905 text lacks it, the site presents it as a dated later Einstein statement.
- §§1–3 are not complete in this batch. The slice explains $D = k_BT/(6\pi\eta a)$ as an available result and links forward, without claiming the Route A derivation is done.

title: Typed content model, stable ids, and the content compiler
description:
# Typed content model, stable ids, and the content compiler

**Type:** epic · **Batch:** A–B (checks mature through H) · **Priority:** P0 · **Plan sections:** §3.2, §4.8, §5.1–5.3, §6.5, §6.6, §6.9, §10.4, §11, §17.3, §22.5 (traceability only)

## Background

The site is "one corpus, several ways through it." The German source face, the English translation, the gloss, four authored readings per paragraph, semantic equations, instruments, discovery journeys, foundations, misconceptions, knowledge cards, and datasets are projections of **one underlying content model**, not separately maintained websites (§1.2). That only works if the corpus is declarative and reviewable: structured records in JSON or YAML plus constrained Markdown for long prose, validated by schemas and joined by a build-time compiler into small route-local payloads (§11.1). Executable MDX, functions, runtime objects, and untrusted JavaScript never live in content files, and no client component imports a giant aggregate module.

Two ideas make the model trustworthy. First, **completeness is measured against a source manifest**, block by block, never by a hand-maintained percentage (§3.2). Second, **the compiler rejects** the specific failures that would quietly corrupt a scientific edition: duplicate ids, broken alignment, unresolved symbols, dimension mismatches, cycles in a proof, a discovery step that cites a premise from after 1904 without a flag, a missing `notModeled`, an English equation block that differs from its German block, a paper marked complete while blocks are missing (§11.7). It **flags rather than resolves** translation ambiguity, influence claims, approximation claims, and source disagreements, because passing a schema is not evidence of a correct translation or good teaching.

## Scope and Children

- `am-cm-id-scheme-8bn`: stable id, anchor, alias, and revision scheme with validators.
- `am-cm-schemas-source-1en`: Paper, SourceAsset, SourceBlock, TranslationUnit, Alignment, GlossUnit, EditorialNote, Citation.
- `am-cm-schemas-argument-llm`: HistoricalPremise, ArgumentNode, Quantity, Equation, Foundation, Misconception, readings, the four kinds of meaning.
- `am-cm-schemas-experiment-fuu`: Experiment manifests, Scenario, HistoricalDataset, Tour, constant-set references.
- `am-cm-compiler-core-oa7`: load, validate, join, route-local payloads, JSONL diagnostics.
- `am-cm-source-manifest-6qa`: the source manifest compiler and locator validator.
- `am-cm-checks-structural-lq0`: structural rejections.
- `am-cm-dimension-validator-aoz`: exact rational-exponent dimensions and semantic-kind distinctions.
- `am-cm-checks-semantic-lic`: symbol, quantity id, owner, and math-command rejections.
- `am-cm-checks-epistemic-o7n`: proof acyclicity, edge types, shelf dates, `notModeled`, accessibility alternatives, ledger minimums, review flags.
- `am-cm-anachronism-lint-dl2`: unlabeled anachronisms in discovery and 1904 content.
- `am-cm-audit-scripts-d34`: `verify-content.ts` and the audit scripts.
- `am-cm-coverage-ledger-0ip`: the executable coverage ledger with never-aggregated dimensions.
- `am-cm-i18n-readiness-b2g`: language, direction, and locale-aware numbers from the start.
- `am-cm-machine-readable-exports-xgy`: stable JSON and Markdown exports.

## Success Criteria

- [ ] Every entity in plan §11.2 has a schema, TypeScript types, valid and invalid fixtures, and readable validation errors.
- [ ] Ids and anchors are content ids, never array positions, identical across faces, with aliases for retired or split ids and explicit revisions.
- [ ] `bun run build` runs the compiler; it produces deterministic route-local payloads and no client-side aggregate import.
- [ ] Every rejection listed in §11.7 has a fixture that triggers it with an actionable message naming the record and field.
- [ ] Flags (translation ambiguity, influence claims, approximation claims, source disagreements) appear in a review queue and never fail silently or auto-resolve.
- [ ] Paper completeness comes only from the source manifest.
- [ ] The coverage ledger reports source completeness, translation review, argument coverage, instrument availability, accessibility equivalence, and numerical validation as separate dimensions.
- [ ] `scripts/verify-content.ts` runs every check plus Rules 0–2 and is part of the quality gate chain.

## Sequencing

1. `am-cm-id-scheme-8bn` (needs `am-scaf-nextjs-app-bu2`).
2. The three schema beads in parallel.
3. `am-cm-compiler-core-oa7`; `am-cm-dimension-validator-aoz` can start right after `am-cm-schemas-argument-llm`.
4. After the compiler core: `am-cm-source-manifest-6qa`, `am-cm-checks-structural-lq0`, `am-cm-checks-epistemic-o7n`, `am-cm-machine-readable-exports-xgy`. `am-cm-i18n-readiness-b2g` follows `am-cm-schemas-source-1en`.
5. `am-cm-checks-semantic-lic` waits for `am-eq-expression-tree-8kl` and `am-not-quantity-registry-2f7`.
6. `am-cm-audit-scripts-d34` after all checks and `am-scaf-architecture-gate-l1p`; `am-cm-coverage-ledger-0ip` after the manifest and `am-scaf-extract-runtime-utilities-99y`; `am-cm-anachronism-lint-dl2` after the epistemic checks.

Source inventory beads (`edn-inventory-*`) depend on the manifest compiler, so steps 1–4 are on the Batch A critical path.

## Considerations

- Keep records small enough for precise review and parallel work; one paragraph's readings should not live in a file shared by a whole paper.
- The compiler is an editor's tool as much as a gate: messages must name the record, the field, the rule, and a repair.
- Do not build a general computer algebra system; authored derivation graphs with a small tested rule set are more auditable (§11.4).

title: Typed, cited historical datasets for overlays and inference
description:
# Typed, cited historical datasets for overlays and inference

**Epic** · **Batch:** C–H · **Priority:** P1 · **Plan sections:** §5.2, §8.1, §8.2, §10.7, §13.1, §22.1 (traceability only)

## Background

The site never manufactures a convincing "1904 measurement" by sampling a modern formula and adding noise. Historical measurements appear only as typed `HistoricalDataset` records with a full citation (including the table or figure number), the digitizer, the digitization date, columns with units, rows, uncertainty, and notes. If a dataset cannot be sourced and cited, it is absent.

Datasets serve three purposes: overlays that compare a model curve with dated evidence (Millikan's 1916 sodium line on the photoelectric apparatus), historical inference (Perrin 1909 displacements in BM-07), and the timeline and "check it against the world" steps of the discovery journeys. A later measurement is excellent evidence while being unavailable on the 1904 shelf: every overlay carries its date and, where shown beside a pre-1905 reconstruction, the label "later evidence."

The launch set named by the plan is: Millikan 1916 sodium, Perrin 1909, Bucherer 1908, Bancelin 1911, Lummer–Pringsheim and Rubens–Kurlbaum 1899–1900, Kaufmann 1902–1906, Ives–Stilwell 1938, and Fizeau 1851.

## Scope and Children

- `am-data-perrin-1909-p7ku`: Perrin's Brownian displacement and sedimentation measurements (BM-07 historical mode).
- `am-data-bancelin-1911-94um`: Bancelin's suspension viscosity measurements (Avogadro lab third panel, companion record).
- `am-data-millikan-1916-zh2q`: Millikan's sodium stopping potentials (LQ-08 overlay).
- `am-data-blackbody-1899-1900-1193`: Lummer–Pringsheim and Rubens–Kurlbaum spectra (LQ-03 points).
- `am-data-kaufmann-1902-1906-52ya`: Kaufmann's beta-ray deflections (SR-13 overlay, presented as ambiguous in 1905–1906).
- `am-data-bucherer-1908-w3mf`: Bucherer's 1908 comparison (SR-13, dated later evidence).
- `am-data-ives-stilwell-1938-61lp`: the transverse-Doppler measurement (SR-09 timeline and overlay).
- `am-data-fizeau-1851-tgl8`: moving-water drag (Fizeau shelf instrument and SR-06).

The loader, schema validation, digitization pipeline, and overlay component belong to `am-inst-dataset-overlay-ra9r`. Rights determinations follow `am-src-rights-policy-1dp`.

## Success Criteria

- [ ] Each dataset exists as a validated `HistoricalDataset` record with CSV data, full citation with table or figure number, digitizer, digitization date, columns with canonical units, uncertainty, and notes.
- [ ] Each dataset has a validation test that checks schema, units, row counts against the source table, and a documented spot-check of at least three rows against the scan.
- [ ] Each dataset's source scan and rights status is recorded; data values are facts, but any reproduced figure image needs its own rights status.
- [ ] Only datasets published on or before the end of 1904 (Fizeau 1851, the 1899–1900 spectra, Kaufmann's 1901–1903 results) may appear on a 1904 shelf; later datasets never do, and every overlay shows its publication date.
- [ ] Digitized-from-figure values carry a digitization uncertainty separate from the reported measurement uncertainty.

## Sequencing

Blocked by `am-inst-dataset-overlay-ra9r` and `am-src-rights-policy-1dp`. Then per batch: Perrin (C) before BM-07; blackbody spectra and Millikan (F) before LQ-03 and LQ-08; Fizeau (E) before the shelf instrument; Kaufmann and Bucherer (G) before SR-13; Ives–Stilwell (G) for SR-09 and the timeline; Bancelin (H) for the Avogadro lab.

## Considerations

- The plan's primary-source list gives full citations for Perrin 1909, Bancelin 1911, Millikan 1916, Kaufmann 1906, Bucherer 1908, and Ives–Stilwell 1938. It does not give citations for Lummer–Pringsheim, Rubens–Kurlbaum, the earlier Kaufmann papers, or Fizeau 1851; child beads list candidate citations that must be verified against the originals before digitization.
- A dataset records what was reported, including the author's own reduction choices. Modern reanalyses are secondary sources and are cited as such, never silently merged.
- Some historical papers report derived quantities rather than raw measurements. Record which is which in the column metadata.

title: Visual design system, themes, semantic color, and top-level pages
description:
# Visual design system, themes, semantic color, and top-level pages

**Epic:** this bead · **Batches:** batch-a (themes), batch-b (color, papers index), batch-c (home, sources, about), batch-h (share cards) · **Priority:** P1 · **Plan sections:** §1.7, §3.8, §4, §15.1, §15.3, §15.5, §16.3, §16.4 (traceability only)

## Background

The site should look like "an unusually beautiful scientific book that happens to be alive": a bright, warm paper background, dark readable body text, generous margins, fine rules, restrained archival accents, and vivid but controlled scientific color. Design here is not decoration. Typography decides whether German diacritics, Greek letters, primes, and long equations are legible; semantic color decides whether a reader can follow one quantity across an equation, a legend, a graph, a scene, and the kernel source; top-level pages decide whether the first screen invites a scientific question or gatekeeps.

The first screen asks a scientific question and offers "Show me with an example" and "Take me to the paper." It never asks whether the visitor is clever enough to enter and never promises that four difficult papers can be mastered in minutes.

## Scope and Children

- `am-design-themes-typography-288q`: the Annalen, Kramgasse Night, and Slate themes; self-hosted, subset Newsreader, Plus Jakarta Sans, JetBrains Mono, and KaTeX fonts with glyph coverage tests; AA contrast checks for every text color pair.
- `am-design-semantic-color-8vbq`: the role palette inherited from the donor's nine-color palette, keyed to canonical quantity id and declared role, with color-independent identity and monochrome intelligibility.
- `am-design-home-page-0s7s`: `/` with four question invitations, a concise explanation, the two entry actions, and the count note.
- `am-design-papers-index-afnu`: `/papers` with the four documents, scope, chronology, and the labeled companion.
- `am-design-sources-about-zumd`: `/sources` (edition policy, bibliographic records, rights, corrections, provenance receipts) and `/about` (purpose, authorship, scope, editorial method, translation policy, how to cite, contribution guidance, clarity-signal summary).
- `am-design-og-images-pwok`: generated Open Graph and Twitter cards per paper and laboratory with the German title and a static rendering of the signature equation.

Out of scope, owned elsewhere: responsive page anatomy (`am-read-page-anatomy-l0b`); `/notation` (`am-not-notation-page-2us`); `/timeline`, `/bern`, `/1904`, `/connections`, `/tours` (discovery epic); the clarity signal mechanism (`am-plat-clarity-signal-nlwr`); print styles (`am-plat-print-3orn`); the reading-only setting and adjustable layout (`am-a11y-reading-only-6wwd`).

## Success Criteria

- [ ] Three themes switch like the donor's theme toggle without a flash of the wrong theme; Slate is chosen automatically on `/discover` unless the reader has set a theme; dark modes are optional and never the primary identity.
- [ ] Every color pair used for text passes WCAG AA in every theme, verified by an automated token test.
- [ ] Fonts are self-hosted and subset, with tests proving coverage of German diacritics, Greek letters, subscripts, primes, old notation, and long equations, and stable fallback metrics that keep cumulative layout shift within 0.1.
- [ ] Semantic colors attach to quantity id and role, never to a letter; identity also appears through labels, shapes, outlines, or patterns; red never simply means "bad"; equations and graphs stay intelligible in monochrome print and under color-vision simulation.
- [ ] `/` presents the four invitations as original interface questions, "Show me with an example," "Take me to the paper," and the count note, with no ability gate.
- [ ] `/papers`, `/sources`, and `/about` are complete, statically rendered, and readable without JavaScript.
- [ ] Share cards exist for every paper and laboratory route and render the German title and signature equation statically.

## Sequencing

`am-design-themes-typography-288q` comes first (after `am-scaf-nextjs-app-bu2`) because `am-a11y-baseline-1cg5`, `am-read-page-anatomy-l0b`, `am-disc-journey-framework-umbg`, and `am-inst-embed-route-rnyg` depend on it. `am-design-semantic-color-8vbq` follows once `am-not-quantity-registry-2f7` exists and unblocks `am-eq-colorized-component-1z8` and `am-inst-2d-view-kit-u75r`. `am-design-papers-index-afnu` can ship with the reader shell; `am-design-home-page-0s7s` waits for `am-bm-first-encounter-fjvh` so "Show me with an example" lands on a real entrance; `am-design-sources-about-zumd` waits for `am-src-rights-policy-1dp`; `am-design-og-images-pwok` waits for `am-eq-static-katex-7da`.

## Considerations

- Pages stay light: no hero video, no web fonts beyond the three families and KaTeX, no forced large download on a mobile connection.
- The Annalen theme may echo a 1905 journal page (running-head feel, German masthead set to match the facsimile as closely as the fonts allow and no more); it must never imitate a publisher's branding.
- The domain and branding use the year, never Einstein's name or face; no photograph of Einstein without cleared terms.
- Visitor-facing copy follows the editorial voice rules (no em dashes, no hype words, no "obviously").

title: Discovery book: journeys, knowledge cards, 1904 desk, reasoning instruments, essays, connections, tours, timeline, Bern
description:
# Discovery book: journeys, knowledge cards, 1904 desk, reasoning instruments, essays, connections, tours, timeline, Bern

**Type:** epic · **Priority:** P1 · **Batch:** batch-h (framework pieces land with the Brownian reference slice in batch-b and mature alongside each paper) · **Plan sections:** §3.7–3.8, §5, §6.7, §7.3, §7.10, §9, §14, §15.1, §19.3 (Batch H), §19.7, §22.4 (traceability only)

## Background

Annus Mirabilis is organized around **arguments**, not results. Beyond "How does this work?", every paper asks: what would make a reasonable person suspect this idea, and what distinguishes that suspicion from a derivation or a test? This epic holds the site's signature content, the **discovery journeys**, and the material around the papers that teaches how ideas get found.

The defining experience the epic must deliver:

> You encounter a real difficulty. You try a plausible response. You find out precisely what it preserves and what it breaks. You acquire one more mathematical tool. Then you make a small, consequential move yourself. Only afterward do you see where that move appears in the paper.

Non-negotiable framing that every child bead inherits:

- **"A route you could take," never "What Einstein thought."** Journeys are reconstructions from a dated 1904 shelf. The site distinguishes four historical statements: a result was publicly available by a date; there is evidence Einstein knew or used it; the paper itself cites or asserts it; the site uses it in a plausible reconstruction. A discovery step may use only category-1 items dated on or before the end of 1904, or an explicitly admitted 1905 result with its provenance shown (the September mass–energy journey imports the relativity paper's §8 light-energy transformation).
- **Guided discovery, never compulsory rediscovery.** Offer a fully worked example, a partly completed comparison, an optional prediction, an explanation, and a transfer case, and let the reader move straight to the explanation at every point. Do not equate surprise with learning; never use an animation to hide an omitted inference. No timers, streaks, scores, punitive red marks, or forced full screen.
- **Fair alternatives.** A wrong turn is a coherent hypothesis that works somewhere and fails on a stated constraint or observation. An empirically equivalent alternative (Lorentz's ether plus local time) is never declared refuted by preference. Branches Lorentz, Planck, Poincaré, Nägeli, or Exner took carry their names. Nobody is mocked.
- **Numbers are live.** "Check it against the world" computes its prediction from an accepted instrument snapshot and compares it with a dated, cited measurement labeled as later evidence where it is.

The plan says Batch H "begins with the first slice and matures alongside the physics rather than being prose pasted over finished animations." Its exit evidence: a knowledge-boundary review, a prerequisite graph with no dead ends, and reviewed transfer tasks.

## Scope and Children

Framework and shared infrastructure
- `am-disc-journey-framework-umbg`: journey skeleton renderer, forks, doors, `/discover/[paper]`, Slate theme default.
- `am-disc-knowledge-cards-iw8j`: dated knowledge cards, shelf views, publication and shelf rules.
- `am-disc-exercise-checker-i4h2`: tiny parsed grammar, numerical equivalence, kernel-checked answers, never stored strings.

The four journeys (each split into a shelf bead and a chain bead)
- `am-disc-journey-i-shelf-xjp8` and `am-disc-journey-i-chain-n1lh`: why suspect that light comes in energy quanta?
- `am-disc-journey-ii-shelf-zbli` and `am-disc-journey-ii-chain-pl6u`: how can visible wandering reveal invisible molecules?
- `am-disc-journey-iii-shelf-5z6q` and `am-disc-journey-iii-chain-hpr7`: how could you stop assuming everyone shares the same time?
- `am-disc-journey-iv-shelf-ff7g` and `am-disc-journey-iv-chain-wwrz`: can emitting light change inertia?
- `am-disc-cross-journey-exercises-j53n`: exercises connecting the four journeys.

The 1904 desk
- `am-disc-shelf-michelson-fizeau-dauq`: shelf instruments (Michelson–Morley with and without contraction, Fizeau drag, Maxwell under a Galilean substitution).
- `am-disc-desk-1904-9hgd`: the `/1904` workspace with five objects and three questions.

Five shared reasoning instruments
- `am-reason-missing-step-explorer-rsl4`, `am-reason-hold-fixed-comparison-xgxw`, `am-reason-countermodel-workbench-t07q`, `am-reason-what-can-you-infer-pqwb`, `am-reason-explanation-replay-35ds`.

Learning activities
- `am-disc-ppe-teachback-wnp7`: chapter-end predict-perturb-explain tasks, teach-back prompts, revisit cards, paired-learning sheets.
- `am-disc-capstones-infra-3352`, `am-disc-capstone-brownian-f8tq`, `am-disc-capstone-mass-energy-wbxy`, `am-disc-capstone-relativity-t8hg`, `am-disc-capstone-light-quanta-98xc`.
- `am-tours-infra-g518`, `am-tour-15min-brownian-z034`, `am-tour-15min-mass-energy-nqz1`, `am-tour-15min-relativity-qcxc`, `am-tour-15min-light-quanta-yj70`, `am-tour-evening-and-course-5kcb`.

Material around the papers
- `am-disc-essays-measurement-fixed-cb1i`, `am-disc-essays-routes-analogy-lka5`, `am-disc-essays-subtract-invariant-5bl6`, `am-disc-essays-limits-model-stops-h6c3`: the eight methodological essays.
- `am-disc-connections-page-vhm7`, `am-disc-avogadro-lab-pfi7`, `am-disc-light-thread-7wm4`: `/connections` and its two instruments.
- `am-companion-dissertation-record-nbvv`: the molecular-dimensions companion, scoped to what the Avogadro lab needs.
- `am-disc-timeline-xzef`: the two-track `/timeline`.
- `am-disc-bern-bridge-6euz`: the `/bern` patent-office page.

## Success Criteria

- [ ] All four journeys ship the full skeleton: dated shelf, nagging fact, first honest question, staged chain with embedded instruments, two or three forks with worked branches, the marked move, a live check against the world, the jump to what Einstein wrote with the weave lit, and two to five exercises plus a predict-perturb-explain task.
- [ ] Every journey has a front door and at least one side door that arrive at the same equation, and the page says so.
- [ ] Every shelf card is dated, sourced, and verified against its original source; no premise dated after 1904 enters a discovery step without the parallel-work or admitted-1905 flag; the shelf audit and anachronism lint pass (knowledge-boundary review recorded).
- [ ] The `/1904` desk offers its five objects, three questions, and the shelf instruments.
- [ ] The five reasoning instruments ship with their first acceptance cases and respect the innovation-sequence stop rules.
- [ ] The eight essays, the `/connections` page with all seven threads, the Avogadro lab, and the light thread are published with exact anchors.
- [ ] Tours exist at all three budgets, capstones exist for all four papers, and chapter-end tasks exist for every major chapter.
- [ ] The timeline shows both tracks with typed, dated, sourced cards, and the Bern page links only to verified classic-patents.com records.
- [ ] Transfer tasks have been reviewed, and no activity scores, ranks, or uploads a reader's answers.

## Sequencing

- **Batch B (with the Brownian slice):** `am-disc-journey-framework-umbg`, `am-disc-knowledge-cards-iw8j`, `am-disc-exercise-checker-i4h2`, `am-reason-missing-step-explorer-rsl4`. The slice's own discovery route lives in `bm-slice-discovery-route` (Brownian slice epic) and is the framework's first real consumer.
- **Batch C:** Journey II shelf and chain, `am-reason-hold-fixed-comparison-xgxw`, `am-reason-what-can-you-infer-pqwb`, `am-tours-infra-g518`, `am-tour-15min-brownian-z034`.
- **Batch D:** Journey IV shelf and chain, `am-tour-15min-mass-energy-nqz1`.
- **Batch E:** Journey III shelf, `am-disc-shelf-michelson-fizeau-dauq`, `am-reason-countermodel-workbench-t07q`.
- **Batch F:** Journey I shelf and chain, `am-tour-15min-light-quanta-yj70`.
- **Batch G:** Journey III chain, `am-tour-15min-relativity-qcxc`.
- **Batch H:** the desk, essays, connections, Avogadro lab, light thread, capstones, chapter-end tasks, explanation replay, evening tours and full course, timeline, Bern page, cross-journey exercises, and the companion record (if the launch decision includes it).

Journey shelves can be researched early and in parallel; chains wait for their instruments. Paper definition-of-done beads depend on their journey's shelf and chain beads.

## Considerations

- The anachronism table binds every journey: "ultraviolet catastrophe" is Ehrenfest's 1911 phrase; Rayleigh's June 1900 form is on the shelf and Jeans's 1905 correction is not; Planck's oscillator energy elements are not Einstein's light quanta; photons, wavefunctions, Bose statistics, Langevin and Wiener notation (1908 and later), spacetime diagrams (Minkowski 1908), and the train-and-embankment picture (1917) are labeled later lenses; Michelson–Morley is not presented as the documented sole cause of the relativity paper; modern SI constants are not 1904 measurements.
- The plan's shelf lists are a research queue, not a finished documentary history. Every card needs its original source checked before publication.
- Stop rules (§19.7): the missing-step explorer expands beyond the variance step only after observed readers resolve the obstacle and return; baseline/variant comparison and the countermodel case expand only once the interface distinguishes changed premises from changed representation; identifiability expands only while unknown information stays visible and the uncertainty calculation stays valid; replay, revisit cards, worksheets, capstones, tours, and embeds must help explanation and transfer without becoming required navigation. P0 and P1 innovations are never a license to postpone the remaining papers.
- Plan corrections that apply here: the coal energy card loses a few tenths of a microgram per kilogram burned, not "less than a nanogram"; the glycerol exercise needs a stated temperature and a viscosity of about 1.4 Pa·s, outside the Brownian teaching range; every classic-patents.com record linked from `/bern` must be verified to exist.
- The companion record is built only after the four papers are complete and only if the launch decision includes it. The Avogadro lab's third panel depends on it.

title: Source inventories, German editions, English translations, alignment, gloss, and translation review
description:
# Source inventories, German editions, English translations, alignment, gloss, and translation review

**Epic:** (top level) · **Batch:** A (inventories) through H (introductory glosses) · **Priority:** P0 · **Plan sections:** §3.2–§3.6, §4.5, §6.9, §7.11, §11.2, §11.3, §17.2, §17.3, §19.1 (traceability only)

## Background

The product's first projection is the exact historical passage in German; its second is a faithful English translation aligned to it sentence by sentence. No existing English translation sits beside the German, the classic ones are a century old or in copyright, and none is reused. This epic turns each pinned facsimile and reviewed ledger (`am-ep-sources-zbs`) into four things the rest of the site builds on:

1. **A source manifest inventory per paper**: every title, author line, heading, paragraph, displayed and substantive inline equation, footnote, reference, date-line, and acknowledgment gets a permanent id, a locator, labels, and status fields for transcription, mathematical transcription, translation, and review. **The manifest, not a hand-maintained percentage, decides whether an edition is complete**, and a block is never "covered" by linking to a whole paper. Ids are frozen in Batch A so transcription, translation, explanation, and instruments can proceed in parallel.
2. **A continuous German edition**: typed source blocks with the diplomatic text, footnotes at their occurrences, equations as printed, and no scan-page furniture.
3. **A new English translation** made from the German, sentence-aligned many-to-many, preserving modality and qualification, keeping every symbol as printed, with authored term annotations.
4. **An interlinear gloss** (paper 4 in full first, then introductions and key sections of papers 1–3).

Each translation is reviewed against the German by a qualified human before publication. Machine-drafted material is never marked reviewed because a schema or renderer accepted it.

## Scope and Children

- `am-edn-ledger-validator-edv`: validator and format specification for reviewed ledgers.
- `am-edn-alignment-tooling-do1`: `segment-ledger.ts`, `align-editions.ts`, and the edition contract test harness.
- `am-edn-inventory-light-quanta-skp`, `am-edn-inventory-brownian-slg`, `am-edn-inventory-relativity-0u9`, `am-edn-inventory-mass-energy-g2d`: freeze ids and list translation and notation difficulties.
- `am-edn-german-edition-light-quanta-eou`, `am-edn-german-edition-brownian-phe`, `am-edn-german-edition-relativity-9p5`, `am-edn-german-edition-mass-energy-srv`: continuous German editions.
- `am-edn-translation-brownian-s4-s5-jr4` (reference slice first), `am-edn-translation-brownian-rest-h0z`, `am-edn-translation-mass-energy-f3b`, `am-edn-translation-relativity-s0-s5-hm8`, `am-edn-translation-relativity-s6-s10-qkn`, `am-edn-translation-light-quanta-s0-s4-muc`, `am-edn-translation-light-quanta-s5-s9-lgu`: English translation units, alignment, and term annotations.
- `am-edn-gloss-mass-energy-g0y`, `am-edn-gloss-introductions-rdq`: word-level glosses.
- `am-edn-review-german-brownian-cfh`, `am-edn-review-german-mass-energy-w3y`, `am-edn-review-german-relativity-0sr`, `am-edn-review-german-light-quanta-khv`: human-gated German source reviews.

Out of scope: facsimiles, OCR, and ledgers (`am-ep-sources-zbs`); schemas and compiler (`am-ep-content-model-9e3`); the readings R0–R3 and equation records (paper epics); the notation concordance (`am-ep-notation-vrg`); the faces that render these records (`am-read-bilingual-faces-pao`, `am-read-gloss-face-lp2`).

## Success Criteria

- [ ] Each paper has a frozen source manifest in which every original unit has an id, a locator, and a destination (edition block, planned translation units, planned argument obligations); the Batch A exit evidence "every original source unit has a destination" holds.
- [ ] Each paper has a continuous German edition whose text is contained in the reviewed ledger, with no page markers and every footnote and closing present.
- [ ] Each paper has an English translation whose alignment covers every German sentence, whose equation blocks are byte-identical to the German, whose symbols are as printed, and whose term definitions each exceed 80 characters.
- [ ] Drafts are visibly distinguished from reviewed translations in the data, and no unit is marked reviewed without a named reviewer record.
- [ ] Paper 4 has a complete gloss; introductions and key sections of papers 1–3 have glosses.
- [ ] All four German source reviews are recorded in the provenance receipts with reviewer names and dates.

## Sequencing

1. `am-edn-ledger-validator-edv` and the four inventories in Batch A (inventories need only the facsimiles and `am-cm-source-manifest-6qa`).
2. `am-edn-alignment-tooling-do1` once the manifest compiler and structural checks exist.
3. Brownian first: German edition, then §§4–5 translation for the Batch B slice, then the rest in Batch C.
4. Mass–energy edition, translation, and gloss in Batch D (the first complete paper).
5. Relativity §§0–5 in Batch E, §§6–10 in Batch G; light quanta in Batch F.
6. Reviews follow each paper's translation and require `am-gov-owners-and-reviewers-hte`.

## Considerations

- Stable ids never change once published; splits and merges create aliases, never reused ids.
- Notation is never translated. $V$ stays $V$ in the English face; the concordance is a separate layer.
- Resolve translation disagreements by returning to the facsimile and context, never by majority vote among paraphrases. Record substantive disagreements with historical translations in the receipt.
- The short mass–energy paper is reviewed with the same seriousness as the long ones.

title: Editorial process: voice lint, review records, comprehension testing
description:
# Editorial process: voice lint, review records, comprehension testing

**Type:** epic · **Batch:** A–I · **Priority:** P1 · **Plan sections:** §7.12, §17.1, §17.2, §17.5, §17.6, §19.5, §20 (traceability only)

## Background

The plan treats editorial and human work as first-class engineering, tracked alongside code (§19.5). Three kinds of evidence must exist before a paper can be called complete, and none can be produced by a build:

1. **Voice.** The site speaks in dates, page numbers, equation numbers, units, and named people, without hype words, em dashes, "obviously," or promises of effortless comprehension (§7.12). Much of that is mechanically checkable, and what is checkable should fail the build.
2. **Review.** Review happens at the level of a complete argument: a German source review of each translation, a physics or mathematics review of each complete derivation, and an R2 readability review by a non-physicist; machine drafts never self-certify; corrections are recorded against stable ids so a source correction identifies the translations and claims it affects without marking unrelated visual work obsolete (§17.2).
3. **Understanding.** A release answers five separate questions, the last being whether the explanation actually helps a reader overcome the intended obstacle (§17.1). That requires comprehension testing with readers across starting points, with a rubric that measures understanding rather than satisfaction (§17.5).

The risk table names the failures this epic prevents: generated explanations shipping unreviewed, textbook myths repeated, and beautiful summaries replacing the papers (§20).

## Scope and Children

- `am-edit-voice-lint-trmf`: the editorial voice lint for visitor-facing content and interface strings.
- `am-edit-review-records-hofz`: structured review records, the correction graph, and the five-question release checklist.
- `am-edit-comprehension-protocol-ouih`: the comprehension-testing protocol, consent materials, and rubric.
- `am-edit-comprehension-rounds-tcgi`: running rounds per route and feeding stumbling points back into content (human gate).

Related work owned elsewhere: named reviewers (`am-gov-owners-and-reviewers-hte`); the per-paper review human gates in each paper epic; the full acceptance scenario (`am-bm-acceptance-scenario-vjn4`); disabled-reader co-design (`am-bm-slice-a11y-codesign-3xuq`, `am-a11y-disabled-reader-rounds-jkjr`).

## Success Criteria

- [ ] The voice lint runs in the quality gate chain over content and interface strings, exempting the diplomatic source and faithful translation where appropriate.
- [ ] Every "reviewed" status in the corpus is backed by a non-stale review record naming a reviewer who did not draft the material.
- [ ] A source correction automatically marks dependent translation and explanation reviews stale; an instrument change does not.
- [ ] Each release candidate carries a five-question checklist whose answers link to separate evidence and are never combined into one score.
- [ ] The comprehension protocol, consent materials, and rubric exist before the first round.
- [ ] Rounds have run for the no-algebra, nonvisual, and full-derivation routes on every paper, with findings triaged into beads, and a public summary of tested routes and known barriers exists.

## Sequencing

`am-edit-voice-lint-trmf` after `am-cm-compiler-core-oa7` (Batch A); `am-edit-comprehension-protocol-ouih` early (Batch B) so recruitment starts during the reference slice; `am-edit-review-records-hofz` after `am-cm-schemas-source-1en` and `am-cm-coverage-ledger-0ip`; `am-edit-comprehension-rounds-tcgi` begins after `am-bm-slice-exit-demo-5922` and completes after the remaining paper definitions of done.

## Considerations

- Never claim the site has proved it can teach every person; publish the scope of tested routes and known barriers (§17.5).
- Satisfaction, confidence, time on page, and completion are not substitutes for understanding.
- A lint catches recurring slips; it never replaces reading the prose.

title: Semantic equations, static math rendering, derivation chains, and the equation interaction ladder
description:
# Semantic equations, static math rendering, derivation chains, and the equation interaction ladder

**Epic:** this bead · **Batches:** batch-a (tree), batch-b (rendering, interaction, chains), batch-g (genealogy) · **Priority:** P0 · **Plan sections:** §1.3 items 2 and 4, §1.5 item 3, §2.2, §2.3, §4.7, §11.4–§11.6, §15.5, §15.6, §16.2, §16.5, §19.4 (traceability only)

## Background

Two of the six barriers this project exists to remove are about equations. **Notation:** Einstein writes the speed of light as $V$ (and as $L$ in the light paper), viscosity as $k$, particle radius as $P$, uses $R/N$ where we write $k_B$, never writes $h$, and his $\beta$ is the modern $\gamma$. **Static equations:** every result in the four papers is a relationship between quantities, and relationships are learned by moving one thing and watching another. A reader cannot turn the dial on $T$ in Wien's law or watch $\langle x^2\rangle$ grow linearly with $t$ in a printed page.

The non-negotiable outcome is that **equations are readable instruments**: symbols, operations, units, assumptions, frames, and live quantities are linked explicitly, and color helps identify meaning but never carries it alone.

The donor (classic-patents.com) already has a real foundation: an equation schema that links symbols, roles, units, sentence fragments, colors, and telemetry; a component with term selection, keyboard navigation, a color-blind mode, and live values; and KaTeX HTML plus MathML with a restricted trust callback. Its seams are wrong for a bilingual scientific edition: telemetry lookup by human label and permissive token matching (`variableId.startsWith("var_" + id)`) break when the same letter means different things in different sections. This epic rebuilds equation identity around **exact canonical quantity ids** and a **semantic expression tree**, generates every notation form from that tree, renders mathematics statically at build time, and adds operation-level interaction, derivation chains, and authored spoken forms.

## Scope and Children

- `am-eq-expression-tree-8kl`: the semantic expression model (symbols, operations, relations, powers, fractions, integrals, derivatives, sums, vectors, matrices, piecewise conditions) with term and operation ids and canonical quantity bindings.
- `am-eq-latex-generation-hc3`: plain and colorized LaTeX in printed (source) and modern notation, generated from trees plus the scoped notation concordance; authored-LaTeX exceptions with validated bindings.
- `am-eq-static-katex-7da`: build-time KaTeX HTML plus MathML, narrow trust, macro and size caps, publication failure on malformed math.
- `am-eq-colorized-component-1z8`: the refactored colorized equation component keyed to quantity ids and roles, with legends, keyboard interaction, and a colorized plain-language sentence.
- `am-eq-live-bindings-2se`: term values from accepted experiment snapshots, with units and a visible stale-state distinction.
- `am-eq-derivation-chains-r4c`: step, reason, tool, and the marked move; a small tested set of transformation rules; acyclic proof routes with historical versus oracle edges.
- `am-eq-spoken-forms-w4f`: authored spoken forms as accessible names and the term-and-operation explorer without duplicate announcements.
- `am-eq-interaction-ladder-8ab`: the six-rung ladder (read aloud, what each part does, try a value, show the next step, why is that allowed, show a concrete example) with operation selection.
- `am-eq-genealogy-hmm`: `usedBy` edges drawn as the equation genealogy on the results face.

Out of scope, owned elsewhere: per-paper equation records (`am-bm-equations-s4-s5-6r81`, `am-bm-equations-s1-s3-u6j7`, `am-me-equations-0mgx`, `am-srk-equations-30cq`, `am-sre-equations-2g3h`, `am-lq-equations-s1-s4-9gl5`, `am-lq-equations-s5-s9-3cjh`); the quantity registry and concordance (`am-not-quantity-registry-2f7`, `am-not-concordance-model-uag`); the rational dimension validator (`am-cm-dimension-validator-aoz`); semantic compiler rejections (`am-cm-checks-semantic-lic`); show-the-code (`am-inst-show-the-code-4brv`); the missing-step explorer (`am-reason-missing-step-explorer-rsl4`); the semantic color palette itself (`am-design-semantic-color-8vbq`).

## Success Criteria

- [ ] Every displayed equation is rendered from a semantic expression tree, or from an explicitly authored LaTeX form whose term bindings validate, never from letter substitution on raw LaTeX.
- [ ] Source and translation faces show printed notation; explanation faces default to printed notation and toggle to modern notation by re-rendering from the tree, updating the colorized sentence and legend.
- [ ] Mathematics is present as KaTeX HTML plus MathML in the initial static HTML, readable with JavaScript disabled; malformed mathematics fails the build; raw `$LaTeX$` never reaches a reader.
- [ ] Selecting a term or an operation highlights exactly its authored meaning in every linked view (the plan's closure condition for the semantic equation component).
- [ ] Live values come only from accepted snapshots, carry units, and are visibly marked when stale.
- [ ] Derivation chains show step, reason, and tool with the move marked; each selected proof route is acyclic; historical derivation edges and modern verification-oracle edges are distinct types.
- [ ] Every equation has an authored spoken form as its accessible name, no duplicate announcements occur on tested assistive-technology combinations, and the term explorer is keyboard operable with a clear exit.
- [ ] The interaction ladder works end to end on $D = k_BT/(6\pi\eta a)$, including the statement that doubling $a$ halves $D$ while the one-dimensional RMS displacement at fixed time falls by $1/\sqrt{2}$.
- [ ] Colors attach to quantity id and role (never to a letter), identity also appears through labels, shapes, outlines, or patterns, and equations stay intelligible in monochrome print and under color-vision simulation.
- [ ] The paper 3 genealogy draws the two postulates at the root, the transformation in the middle, the field, Doppler, energy, and electron results as leaves, and one edge leaving to paper 4.

## Sequencing

1. `am-eq-expression-tree-8kl` (after `am-cm-schemas-argument-llm` and `am-not-quantity-registry-2f7`).
2. `am-eq-latex-generation-hc3` (after `am-not-concordance-model-uag`), then `am-eq-static-katex-7da` (after the donor LaTeX renderer extraction in `am-scaf-extract-ui-components-c31`).
3. In parallel after static rendering: `am-eq-colorized-component-1z8` (needs `am-design-semantic-color-8vbq`) and `am-eq-spoken-forms-w4f`.
4. `am-eq-live-bindings-2se` after the colorized component and `am-rt-snapshot-store-aft`.
5. `am-eq-derivation-chains-r4c` after the tree and `am-cm-checks-epistemic-o7n`; it unblocks every paper's equation beads.
6. `am-eq-interaction-ladder-8ab` after live bindings, chains, and spoken forms.
7. `am-eq-genealogy-hmm` after `am-read-results-face-uzh`, needed by `am-sr-results-cards-k9ck`.

The Brownian reference slice exercises all of this first. Generalize beyond what the slice needs only after `am-bm-slice-retrospective-pp09` records which abstractions helped.

## Considerations

- **No general computer algebra system at launch.** An authored derivation graph with a small, tested set of transformation rules is more tractable and auditable. Numerical spot checks help but cannot prove arbitrary symbolic equivalence.
- **Four kinds of meaning** (logical role, historical status, model status, execution status) stay separate on every equation and are never compressed into one color.
- **Human labels are not API keys.** "energy" is not a binding key; `frequencyEnergyDensity` and `wavelengthEnergyDensity` are different quantities even though they share a glyph.
- **Security.** A source record must never inject HTML, CSS, links, or image loads through a mathematical expression. Keep KaTeX trust narrow, validate generated classes and data attributes, cap macro expansion and size, and never display raw error strings.
- **Performance.** Static math lives in HTML; only interaction hydrates. The initial reading route stays within 200 KiB compressed JavaScript, and deferred math activation must not push cumulative layout shift past 0.1.
- **Notation versus knowledge.** Renaming $V$ to $c$ never authorizes importing a later proof; the perspective axis and the notation toggle are modeled independently (`am-read-perspective-toggle-abd`).

title: Foundation library and the zero-assumed-algebra layer
description:
# Foundation library and the zero-assumed-algebra layer

**Epic** · **Batch:** foundations span batch-b to batch-h · **Priority:** P1 · **Plan sections:** §1.5 item 2, §6.4, §7.5, §16.2, §19.3 H (traceability only)

## Background

The second non-negotiable outcome is **no prerequisite dead ends**: unfamiliar mathematics opens into an explanation with a worked example, a picture or manipulable construction, and a route back to the exact interrupted argument. The foundation library delivers that promise. It is built in response to the actual dependency graphs of the four papers, not as an independent undergraduate textbook.

Every foundation has a compact explanation, one worked example, one instrument or manipulable construction where useful, a textual equivalent, prerequisites, and backlinks to every calling passage. Its return caption names the right quantity and what is held fixed at the calling passage. Foundation text renders correctly in print and without JavaScript.

Beneath the library sits the **zero-assumed-algebra layer**: small bridges generated by actual obstacles in the papers, so "Explain from the beginning" lands on a concrete operation (counting, measuring, balancing) rather than another paragraph of words like *linear*, *differential*, *distribution*, and *invariant*.

The prerequisite graph is finite and curated. Every basic node has a stated stopping point (multiplication as repeated scaling, a graph as a record of paired quantities, a rate as change per unit of something). A selected proof has an acyclic dependency route to its stated entry assumptions; the broader concept map may contain cross-links, which are not logical circles. A reader may use an already-understood result while its deeper derivation is marked as available; not everyone must reach the same elementary leaf. No placement tests: readiness is shown by what a reader can explain, never by a quiz.

## Scope and Children

- `am-found-library-infra-002t`: routes, drawer mode, record rendering, backlinks, return captions, print and no-JavaScript rendering, proof-route checks.
- `am-found-quantities-magnitudes-igxe`: quantities and units; ratios and scaling; orders of magnitude; the 1905 unit system.
- `am-found-calculus-6agg`: functions and graphs; derivatives; partial derivatives; exponentials; logarithms.
- `am-found-statistics-inference-pzqv`: error and inference, plus inference extensions of the statistics nodes.
- `am-found-transport-thermo-smv3`: viscosity and Stokes drag; free energy and osmotic pressure; work and energy; temperature and thermal energy; entropy and multiplicity; entropy and temperature.
- `am-found-linear-geometry-7w15`: vectors and components; matrices and linear maps; dot and cross products; hyperbolic functions and rapidity (labeled later aid); conservation and symmetry.
- `am-found-fields-light-cv3o`: frames and events; fields and waves; electromagnetism needed here; momentum and energy of light.
- `am-found-reading-german-u8oc`: reading a German physics sentence.
- `am-found-zero-algebra-rest-oipl`: a letter stands for a quantity; an equals sign describes a relationship; mathematical punctuation; probability notation.
- `am-found-prereq-audit-71ot`: the no-dead-ends audit across all four papers.

Owned in the Brownian reference slice by `am-bm-slice-foundations-f5z9`: integration; Taylor expansion; probability and independence; distributions; mean, variance, and RMS; Gaussian distributions; flux and continuity; diffusion equation; random walks; and the bridges for negative numbers and direction, fractions and ratios, squaring and square roots, scientific notation and units, a graph, and a sum and an average.

**Partition check.** 35 foundation nodes (9 in the slice, 26 in this epic's cluster beads) and 10 zero-algebra bridges (6 in the slice, 4 here). If `am-bm-slice-foundations-f5z9` authors a different subset, the cluster beads absorb the remainder so that every node has exactly one owner.

## Success Criteria

- [ ] All 35 foundations and all 10 bridges exist with the required parts and exactly one owning bead each.
- [ ] Every foundation has backlinks to all calling passages and a return caption for each calling passage.
- [ ] Every foundation renders in print and without JavaScript.
- [ ] Every selected proof route is acyclic back to its entry assumptions; cross-links are typed as cross-links.
- [ ] `am-found-prereq-audit-71ot` reports no dead ends across all four papers.
- [ ] Foundation instruments, where present, satisfy the action contract and accessibility rules of the instrument platform.

## Sequencing

1. `am-found-library-infra-002t` lands in Batch B, then `am-bm-slice-foundations-f5z9` authors the slice nodes.
2. Batch C (before the mass-energy and light papers draw on them): `am-found-quantities-magnitudes-igxe`, `am-found-calculus-6agg`, `am-found-statistics-inference-pzqv`, `am-found-transport-thermo-smv3`, `am-found-zero-algebra-rest-oipl`.
3. Batch E (before relativity): `am-found-linear-geometry-7w15`, `am-found-fields-light-cv3o`.
4. Batch H: `am-found-reading-german-u8oc`.
5. Last: `am-found-prereq-audit-71ot`, after the four papers' definition-of-done audits.

## Considerations

- Do not author a textbook; each node earns its place by a calling passage.
- Analogies follow mechanisms and say where they stop; the programmer, physician, engineer, student, and no-algebra lenses guide authoring but never appear to readers.
- Later aids (rapidity, spacetime geometry, Langevin notation) are labeled with dates and never presented as 1905 premises.
- Voice rules apply: no em dashes, no "obviously," no promises of effortless comprehension.

title: FrankenSim capability audit, first WASM exports, slim artifact, and upstream capability owners
description:
# FrankenSim capability audit, first WASM exports, slim artifact, and upstream capability owners

**Type:** epic · **Batch:** A (audit, exports, artifact, Philox port), B (diffusion owner), later batches (capability owners) · **Priority:** P0 · **Labels:** frankensim, upstream-frankensim · **Plan sections:** §2.2, §12.1–12.4, §12.9, §17.3, §19.1, §19.4 "Diffusion owner" (traceability only)

## Background

The ownership rule: **a reusable physical or numerical law belongs in FrankenSim** (`~/projects/frankensim`, Rust, pinned nightly). A source passage, teaching prompt, historical annotation, visual metaphor, or discovery sequence belongs in Annus Mirabilis. The browser boundary composes generic capabilities into bounded educational experiments. The project must not create four physics engines named after the papers: Brownian diffusion should be useful to other projects, Lorentz transformations reusable beyond this site, and radiation spectra never buried in a React component. The benefit runs both ways: the site improves FrankenSim's reusable capabilities, and Classic Patents can later reuse radiation, statistical, or field tools without importing an Einstein-specific UI.

The planning audit (source inspection at frankensim `5bbbfae6f7de614422f6f97f5798a3e00f8ad813`, 2026-09-13; not an execution audit) found:

- `fs-wasm` already depends on `fs-rand` (counter-based Philox4x32-10 streams keyed by logical identity) and `fs-sparse` (CSR sparse matrices with `spmv`).
- `fs-wasm`'s existing `heat_frames` is a fixed two-blob 2D demonstration with a hard-coded initial field and a dimensionless step (`dt = 0.20`). It takes no diffusion coefficient, spacing, or profile, so it is not an honest owner for any diffusion instrument.
- `fs-lattice` is infill optimization and `fs-flux` is Navier–Stokes. Crate names do not establish semantics.
- `fs-qty` represents dimensions as integer (`i8`) exponents over six base dimensions (m, kg, s, K, A, mol).
- `fs-demo-physics-wasm` shows the typed browser envelope: `{"ok": {...}}` or `{"refusal": {"code", "message", "ranked_repairs"}}`, plus a kernel-version export and a `CONTRACT.md` with explicit no-claim boundaries.
- No ready Brownian, radiation, or special-relativity product API was found. Absence in a search is not proof of absence, and no such capability is assumed.

The exporting crate `fs-wasm` is its own nested workspace (`crate-type = ["cdylib", "rlib"]`), declared no `[features]` table and had no `crates/fs-wasm/tests/` directory at the audited revision. The donor museum's `public/wasm/fs-generic/fs_wasm_bg.wasm` is 4.9 MB, which is the full package even though the donor's loader comments describe a slim artifact. The slim build therefore has to be established here, not copied.

## Scope and Children

- `am-fs-capability-audit-byc`: bounded audit and build probe; writes `docs/FRANKENSIM_BINDING.md`; resolves kernel scaling, the refusal channel, and stream-key mapping before any export is written.
- `am-fs-export-brownian-frames-nhm`: the seeded 1D random-walk export with documented per-kernel scaling.
- `am-fs-export-philox-normals-xnv`: the Philox standard-normal export plus emitted cross-check vectors.
- `am-fs-export-diffusion1d-cew`: the explicit FTCS 1D diffusion export with a typed stability refusal.
- `am-fs-slim-artifact-0yh`: the feature-selected slim WASM bundle, content-addressed into `public/wasm/`, digests pinned, and `scripts/verify-wasm-artifacts.ts`.
- `am-fs-philox-ts-port-7kp`: `src/physics/reference/philox.ts` with bitwise integer cross-checks against `fs-rand`.
- `am-fs-diffusion-owner-sey`: the generic upstream diffusion owner, with the `fs-wasm` exports routed through it (the §19.4 "Diffusion owner" closure).
- `am-fs-annus-adapter-cuw`: the narrow versioned composition boundary, only if the reference slice shows it is needed.
- `am-fs-owner-radiation-6uv`, `am-fs-owner-inference-45g`, `am-fs-owner-relativity-feh`, `am-fs-owner-electrodynamics-mxr`, `am-fs-owner-evidence-rk7`: upstream capability owners from the §12.3 table, each with an explicit downstream adoption step.

Out of scope: the TypeScript reference evaluators that serve as audited host calculations (`am-ep-reference-sln`), the runtime protocol (`am-ep-runtime-iml`), and instrument views (`am-ep-instruments-8gi`).

## Success Criteria

- [ ] `docs/FRANKENSIM_BINDING.md` records the pinned FrankenSim revision, toolchain, audited owners, actual exports, per-kernel step semantics, the refusal envelope, and the stream-key allocation.
- [ ] The three first exports compile natively (rlib) and to `wasm32` (cdylib), have tests under `crates/fs-wasm/tests/`, and ship only through the slim artifact.
- [ ] `scripts/verify-wasm-artifacts.ts` pins digests, instantiates the artifact, steps all three exports, cross-checks Philox integer output bitwise against the TypeScript port, checks the normal transform at a recorded tolerance, verifies the stability refusal, rejects malformed output, round-trips 64-bit identities, and proves the fallback label is never `wasm`.
- [ ] The diffusion owner closure holds: independent analytical and statistical tests pass and its export is admitted in the slim artifact.
- [ ] No adapter or page component contains a second copy of a law owned by a generic crate.
- [ ] Each later capability owner is adopted downstream with the execution label switched only after accepted results, and the TypeScript reference evaluator stays as the labeled fallback.

## Sequencing

1. `am-fs-capability-audit-byc` (after `am-gov-donor-audit-0wa` pins the revision).
2. The three exports in parallel.
3. `am-fs-slim-artifact-0yh` and `am-fs-philox-ts-port-7kp` in parallel.
4. `am-fs-diffusion-owner-sey` before `am-bm-slice-exit-demo-5922`.
5. `am-fs-annus-adapter-cuw` only after `am-bm-slice-retrospective-pp09`.
6. Owners follow their papers: inference (Batch C), relativity (Batch E), radiation (Batch F), electrodynamics (Batch G), evidence (after `am-ver-quantity-records-fby2`). None of these later owners blocks launch; audited host calculation is an honest, labeled state.

## Considerations

- **Upstream process.** Every `upstream-frankensim` change lands in `~/projects/frankensim` under FrankenSim's own conventions: its pinned toolchain (`nightly-2026-07-06` at the audit), per-crate `CONTRACT.md`, safe Rust with `forbid(unsafe_code)` where compatible, its gates and bead tracker. This repository then pins the new upstream revision and reruns dependent fixtures in an explicit adoption step.
- **Rust policy.** No C or C++ physics libraries, hidden FFI solvers, or competing numerical ecosystem. Reuse asupersync and FrankenSim's own libraries where they fit. The `wasm-bindgen` and `getrandom` target dependencies are an observed packaging fact, not permission to add runtime dependencies. Pin the nightly, upstream commits, constellation revisions, generated glue, and lockfiles.
- **Single-threaded browser target first.** Threads, shared memory, SIMD specialization, and GPU compute are optimizations that must earn their complexity through measurement. Rendering may use the GPU while scientific computation stays deterministic CPU/WASM. Add a capability only when a named instrument uses it; the site never waits for unrelated crates to compile for the browser.
- **Plan corrections 3 and 4.** The plan's `brownian_frames` signature states the scale only for kernel 3, and the plan's `diffusion1d_frames` signature returns a bare `Vec<f64>` that cannot carry a refusal code. Both are resolved in the audit before implementation.

# Governance, repository, donor audit, and project decisions

**Type:** epic · **Batch:** A (decisions are resolved at the point they affect work) · **Priority:** P0 · **Plan sections:** §0, §2, §17.8, §18.5, §19.5, §20 (traceability only)

## Background

Annus Mirabilis is a new open-source critical edition and discovery laboratory for Einstein's four 1905 *Annalen der Physik* papers (`light-quanta`, `brownian-motion`, `special-relativity`, `mass-energy`) with the dissertation `molecular-dimensions` as a companion record. It is built from a small, attributable extraction of the architecture donor classic-patents.com and the numerical owner FrankenSim, never by forking the donor and deleting most of it.

Three things must be true before implementation can be trusted:

1. The repository exists with guidelines (AGENTS.md), a README, a license, and git hygiene, so every agent starts from the same rules.
2. The donor revisions are pinned, so every claim about donor code ("the donor already separates facsimile, ledger, edition, and explanation", "`heat_frames` is a fixed two-blob demo") is reproducible against a specific commit.
3. The decisions the plan deliberately left open are made where they affect work, recorded with reasons, and never used as an excuse to defer source inventory, content writing, or the first vertical slice.

The plan lists the open decisions (§20): the final license and rider for new code and content; the distribution basis for each scan; the reviewers for the English editions; framework and package versions after a compatibility and security review; the exact upstream ownership of missing capabilities; the device profiles for performance budgets; and whether the companion record ships at launch.

The plan also records **decisions already made**, which no bead in this epic reopens: the content unit is an argument linked to a source passage; the default is a guided English reader with optional deeper detail; the source stays directly accessible; the 1904 perspective is an authored constraint; Three.js is a presentation tool; numerical capabilities belong upstream in FrankenSim; the core product is static-first with no login and no hosted model; four papers are flagship and the dissertation is a companion; a new translation is made from the German; DNS records are DNS-only at launch; Brownian motion §§4–5 is the reference slice; mass–energy is the first complete paper. Where the plan says "should," a named owner may override the default with a recorded reason (§0).

## Scope and Children

- `am-gov-repo-bootstrap-p5t`: the public repository with README, AGENTS.md, LICENSE, git hygiene, vercel.json, and the beads workspace (already completed; kept as a record).
- `am-gov-donor-audit-0wa`: `docs/DONOR_AUDIT.md` pinning classic-patents.com and FrankenSim revisions and re-verifying every donor finding and reuse decision.
- `am-gov-decision-stack-versions-6ax`: the locked framework, library, and tool versions after a compatibility and security probe.
- `am-gov-decision-license-rights-tps`: the user's final license and rider decision for new code and prose, plus the per-asset exception policy (human gate).
- `am-gov-owners-and-reviewers-hte`: named editorial owners per paper, implementation owners per shared capability, and the German-source, physics, and non-physicist reviewers (human gate).
- `am-gov-decision-device-profiles-1zm`: the hardware, browser, viewport, network, and cache profiles every performance budget is measured against.
- `am-gov-decision-companion-at-launch-936`: whether the dissertation companion record ships at launch or after.

Out of scope, owned elsewhere: the rights basis of each individual scan (`am-src-rights-policy-1dp` and the `src-facsimile-*` beads); the exact upstream placement of missing numerical capabilities (`am-fs-capability-audit-byc`).

## Success Criteria

- [ ] The public repository exists with README, AGENTS.md, LICENSE, `.gitignore`, `.gitattributes`, `vercel.json`, the master plan, and an initialized beads workspace.
- [ ] `docs/DONOR_AUDIT.md` pins exact commit hashes for both donors, states the inspection method and its limits, and re-verifies every finding and reuse decision against the pinned revisions with file-level evidence.
- [ ] `docs/DECISIONS.md` exists as the single decision log. Every decision in this epic is recorded with the question, options considered, the choice, the reason, the decider, the date, and the beads it unblocked.
- [ ] Framework, library, and tool versions are locked in `package.json` and the committed lockfile, with the compatibility probe and security scan results recorded.
- [ ] The user has recorded the license and rider decision before any publication beyond the repository itself.
- [ ] Editorial owners, implementation owners, and each reviewer role are named before any review human gate opens.
- [ ] Device profiles are recorded before `am-plat-perf-budgets-s3ww` enforces a budget.
- [ ] The companion decision is recorded before `am-src-facsimile-dissertation-2mp` starts.
- [ ] No decision in this epic has been used to block work that does not depend on it.

## Sequencing

1. `am-gov-repo-bootstrap-p5t` (complete) unblocks everything else here.
2. `am-gov-donor-audit-0wa` next, because the version decision and all three donor extraction beads need pinned revisions and verified paths.
3. `am-gov-decision-stack-versions-6ax` then unblocks `am-scaf-nextjs-app-bu2` and `am-gov-decision-device-profiles-1zm`.
4. In parallel from the start: `am-gov-decision-license-rights-tps` (blocks only `am-launch-readiness-audit-sc9b`), `am-gov-owners-and-reviewers-hte` (blocks the review human gates in every paper epic), and `am-gov-decision-companion-at-launch-936` (blocks only the dissertation facsimile).

Batch A's exit evidence (plan §19.1) depends on this epic finishing its first three beads quickly: every original source unit has a destination, drafts are visibly distinguished from reviewed translations, and the empty site deploys to the Vercel alias.

## Considerations

- Decisions are made where they affect work. A pending license decision never blocks transcription; a pending reviewer assignment never blocks drafting.
- Two children are human gates. Agents may prepare option memos and evidence, but the user or the named person makes and records the decision.
- Donor repositories are read-only from this project. Changes to classic-patents.com happen only as separately reviewed changes in that repository.
- AGENTS.md and README describe the planned layout. Any bead that changes a documented contract updates those files in the same change.

title: Instrument platform: registry, parameters, labels, predict mode, show the code, permalinks, embeds, views
