title: Build shared SVG and Canvas view primitives that only project accepted snapshots
description:
# Build shared SVG and Canvas view primitives that only project accepted snapshots

**Epic:** `am-ep-instruments-8gi` · **Batch:** batch-b · **Priority:** P0 · **Plan sections:** §8.1 (coordinate traps), §8.2 (rendering rules), §8.3 (diagram scaling), §10.9, §12.5, §12.7, §15.5, §16.2, §16.4 (traceability only)

## Background

Almost every instrument is two-dimensional: histograms, trajectories, spectra, event diagrams, energy ledgers. The plan is emphatic that 2D comes first and Three.js is reserved for the few spatial cases. A shared view kit keeps visual semantics consistent and, more importantly, encodes the rendering rules that protect scientific meaning:

- a logarithmic axis never redefines what a density means;
- a path leaving the viewport stays in the ensemble;
- a smooth polyline is a rendering convention, not a velocity;
- a point distribution at $t = 0$ is not an infinite bar;
- ultraviolet and infrared are never shown as visible colors without a false-color legend;
- rendering a subset of particles never changes the ensemble used for results.

Every primitive consumes accepted snapshots and projects coordinates into pixels. None computes physics.

## Scope

In scope: `src/visuals/kit/` primitives for axes, plots, histograms, trajectories, event diagrams, intervals, ledgers, legends, scale bars, and typed-result rendering; performance tiers; accessibility hooks.

Out of scope: specific instruments; Three.js (`am-inst-three-studio-y0y0`); dataset loading (`am-inst-dataset-overlay-ra9r`); description text generation (`am-a11y-graph-descriptions-vxe1`, integrated here through hooks).

## Requirements

### Axes and units

- Axes take a canonical quantity id and a display unit from the quantity registry; tick labels format through the units adapter, never ad hoc strings.
- Logarithmic axes: the primitive requires the snapshot to declare the density kind of its vertical data (`per-frequency`, `per-wavelength`, `per-ln-interval`, `per-decade`, `total`). A log horizontal axis with a per-frequency density is labeled as such; switching to a per-log-interval view is a data transform supplied by the owner, not a relabel.
- Frequency and wavelength axes are distinct quantity ids; a selected band can be preserved across representations using owner-supplied mappings.

### Plot primitives

- `LinePlot`, `ScatterPlot` with three visually distinct classes: theoretical curves, historical fitted laws, empirical points (markers with uncertainty bars). Class is part of the data contract.
- `Histogram` with explicit bin semantics: bin probability versus density toggle, bin width shown, normalization stated.
- `IntervalShade` for selected intervals with the probability value supplied by the snapshot.
- `AnalyticLimitMarker`: renders an `analytic-limit` point distribution as a labeled marker with interval probabilities, never an infinite bar.

### Trajectories and fields of view

- `TrajectoryLayer` draws sampled positions from typed buffers without copying them into React state; supports up to 10 000 tracers with batched Canvas drawing and instancing where available.
- Paths leaving the viewport are not wrapped, reflected, replaced, or dropped from the ensemble; the view shows an off-screen count. The microscope boundary is a camera viewport, not a wall.
- Smooth lines between samples are labeled a rendering convention in the model note; no primitive derives velocity from a polyline.
- Rendering a subset for performance is allowed only for display; the result panels always read ensemble statistics from the snapshot.

### Event and spacetime diagrams

- `EventDiagram` uses coherent axis scaling so light lines are at 45 degrees, supports light-seconds units with the conversion shown, and marks events by id with frame labels. Camera zoom never implies changed physics. Diagrams carry the label that spacetime diagrams are a later aid (Minkowski 1908).

### Ledgers and legends

- `EnergyLedger` bars and tables for channel accounting, with boundaries drawn from snapshot data.
- `QuantityLegend` keyed by quantity id and role color from the semantic color system, plus a non-color identity (label, shape, outline, or pattern) so meaning survives color-vision differences and monochrome print.
- `FalseColorLegend` required whenever a spectral view shows frequencies outside 380–750 nm.
- `ScaleBar` with calibrated physical length and time scale.

### Performance and lifecycle

- 60 Hz on capable desktops, a stable 30 Hz mobile tier; UI summaries published at a bounded rate; display interpolation separate from scientific stepping.
- A depleted budget reduces visual detail (point size, drawn subset, resolution) and never alters the model, time step, or sample.
- Canvas contexts, listeners, and animation frames are released on unmount; invisible views pause.

### Accessibility hooks

- Each primitive exposes a description provider interface consumed by `am-a11y-graph-descriptions-vxe1`: a statement of what is compared, the current relation after an intentional action, and optional detailed data as a table.
- No 60 Hz live-region updates; committed comparisons only.
- Reduced motion pauses animation and shows the current state.

## Technical Approach

React components over SVG for axes and annotations and Canvas 2D for dense layers; data passed as typed arrays and snapshot references; storybook-free visual fixtures rendered in tests with deterministic snapshots of SVG and pixel hashes where stable.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All primitives exist, take quantity ids and units, and render only from snapshot data.
- [ ] A density-kind declaration is required for log axes; a test proves a per-frequency density cannot be silently shown on a per-log-interval axis label.
- [ ] Trajectories leaving the viewport remain counted; wrap and reflect are impossible through the API.
- [ ] Analytic-limit markers render correctly with interval probabilities.
- [ ] Legends show non-color identity; false-color legend appears for non-visible frequencies.
- [ ] 10 000 tracers render at the desktop tier target on the agreed profile; the drawn subset never changes result panels.
- [ ] Views release resources on unmount (no growing listener or context counts across 50 mount cycles).

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests

- `axes.test.tsx`, `histogram.test.tsx`, `trajectories.test.tsx`, `eventDiagram.test.tsx`, `legends.test.tsx`, `analyticLimit.test.tsx`, `lifecycle.test.tsx`.
- Deterministic SVG snapshot tests for representative fixtures; pixel-hash tests only where rendering is stable across CI browsers.

### End-to-end tests

- BM-01 lane: drive tracers out of the viewport and assert the ensemble count and statistics are unchanged; reduced-motion lane shows a static state; 320 px lane has no horizontal overflow.
- Performance lane records frame times with the device profile metadata.

### Structured logging

JSONL with `suite`, `testId`, `beadId`, `component`, `instrumentId`, `snapshotVersion`, `drawnCount`, `ensembleCount`, `frameTimeP95Ms`, `viewport`, `reducedMotion`, `outcome`, `message`.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- Keep four distinctions visible: trajectory versus ensemble; position versus displacement; signed coordinate versus radius; mean square versus square of the mean.
- Never compute a physical value in a view helper "for convenience."

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-inst-registry-dispatcher-66l0` (views are dispatched and bound to instances).
- `am-design-semantic-color-8vbq` (role colors keyed to quantity ids).
- `am-not-quantity-registry-2f7` (quantity ids, units, formatting).
- `am-a11y-graph-descriptions-vxe1` (description providers the primitives must implement).

Unblocks:
- `am-bm-01-tracer-ensemble-hdly`, `am-bm-05-random-steps-ntzl`, `am-bm-06-gaussian-spread-982y`.
- `am-inst-dataset-overlay-ra9r`, `am-reason-hold-fixed-comparison-xgxw`, `am-reason-what-can-you-infer-pqwb`, `am-disc-shelf-michelson-fizeau-dauq`.

title: Build the HistoricalDataset loader, digitization pipeline, and visually distinct cited overlays
description:
# Build the HistoricalDataset loader, digitization pipeline, and visually distinct cited overlays

**Epic:** `am-ep-instruments-8gi` · **Batch:** batch-c · **Priority:** P1 · **Plan sections:** §5.2, §8.1 (stable evaluation and data honesty), §8.2 (synthetic versus real data), §10.7, §11.2 (HistoricalDataset), §13.1, §17.3 (digitize-datasets/) (traceability only)

## Background

"Empirical points, historical fitted laws, and theoretical curves stay visibly distinct; the site never manufactures a convincing 1904 measurement by sampling a modern formula and adding noise." Historical measurements are typed `HistoricalDataset` records with citations, or they are absent.

This bead builds the shared machinery every dataset and every overlay uses: the record loader and validator, the digitization pipeline that turns a cited table or figure into a CSV with provenance and uncertainty, and the overlay component that shows data beside model curves with dates, citations, and honest styling. It also enforces the knowledge boundary: a dataset published after 1904 never appears on the 1904 shelf, and every overlay says when the measurement was made.

## Scope

In scope: `HistoricalDataset` loader and validator in `src/content/datasets/`; `scripts/digitize-datasets/` pipeline conventions and validation harness; `DatasetOverlay` view component; the typed refusal for uncited data; the shelf-eligibility rule.

Out of scope: individual datasets (`am-ep-datasets-fsk` children); the schema definition (`am-cm-schemas-experiment-fuu`); rights policy (`am-src-rights-policy-1dp`).

## Requirements

### Record fields and validation

- Required: title; full citation (authors, title, journal, series, volume, year, pages) with **table or figure number**; digitizer (name or agent id); digitization date; source scan asset id with rights status; columns with canonical quantity ids and units; rows; uncertainty (reported measurement uncertainty and, separately, digitization uncertainty for values read from figures); notes (reduction choices, corrections applied by the original authors, known reanalyses as secondary citations); publication date for shelf eligibility.
- Validation: units exist in the quantity registry and are dimensionally consistent with the column's quantity; row counts match the documented source table; uncertainty columns are non-negative and aligned; a dataset lacking a table or figure citation fails the build (typed refusal at runtime if loaded dynamically).
- Raw versus derived: each column declares whether it is a reported measurement or a quantity derived by the original author.

### Digitization pipeline (`scripts/digitize-datasets/<dataset-id>/`)

- `source.md`: citation, scan asset, page and table or figure locator.
- `data.csv`: values as printed (with printed units) plus canonical conversions in separate columns.
- `digitization-log.md`: method (transcription from a table, or figure digitization with axis calibration points), tool, date, operator, and a spot-check list of at least three rows re-read from the scan by a second pass.
- `validate.test.ts`: schema, units, row count, spot-check values, and conversion checks.

### Overlay component

- `DatasetOverlay` renders points with uncertainty bars (and a separate digitization band where applicable), using the view kit's empirical-point class, distinct from theoretical curves and historical fitted laws by marker, line style, and label, not color alone.
- Always shows the short citation and publication year; on a view set before the 1905 cutoff (discovery shelf stages) any later dataset shows "later evidence, published YYYY."
- Normalization: if an overlay requires a scale factor (for example relative spectral intensities), the factor, its method, and its uncertainty are displayed and recorded; no hidden fitting.
- Accessible table view of the plotted rows with citations.

### Shelf eligibility

Datasets published on or before the end of 1904 (Fizeau 1851, the 1899–1900 spectra, Kaufmann's 1901–1903 results) may appear in 1904 shelf stages; later datasets cannot be referenced by a shelf step (compiler check integration through `publicationDate`).

## Technical Approach

Loader produces route-local data payloads; the overlay consumes snapshot model curves and static dataset rows; the pipeline runs under `bun test` and emits JSONL.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Loader validates all required fields; uncited datasets fail the build.
- [ ] Pipeline template and validation harness exist and are used by at least one dataset fixture.
- [ ] Overlay styles empirical points, fitted laws, and theoretical curves distinctly without relying on color; citations and years are always visible.
- [ ] Later datasets are rejected in shelf stages; earlier ones are accepted.
- [ ] Normalization factors are displayed and recorded when used.
- [ ] The table view exposes the same rows and citations.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests

- `datasetLoader.test.ts`: required fields, unit and dimension checks, raw versus derived flags, uncertainty alignment.
- `datasetShelf.test.ts`: publication-date eligibility.
- `datasetOverlay.test.tsx`: styling classes, citation rendering, normalization display, table view.
- Pipeline fixture: a small synthetic-free fixture table transcribed from a public-domain source to exercise the harness end to end.

### End-to-end tests

- Consuming lanes (LQ-08 Millikan overlay, BM-07 Perrin data) assert citations, years, "later evidence" labels on pre-1905 views, and the table view.

### Structured logging

JSONL with `suite`, `testId`, `beadId`, `datasetId`, `rowCount`, `units`, `validationErrors`, `shelfEligible`, `normalizationFactor`, `outcome`, `message`.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- Digitizing from figures adds uncertainty that must not be confused with the original measurement uncertainty.
- A reanalysis is a separate cited source, never silently merged into the historical values.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-cm-schemas-experiment-fuu` (the `HistoricalDataset` schema).
- `am-inst-2d-view-kit-u75r` (plot classes, legends, table hooks).

Unblocks:
- `am-data-perrin-1909-p7ku`, `am-data-bancelin-1911-94um`, `am-data-millikan-1916-zh2q`, `am-data-blackbody-1899-1900-1193`, `am-data-kaufmann-1902-1906-52ya`, `am-data-bucherer-1908-w3mf`, `am-data-ives-stilwell-1938-61lp`, `am-data-fizeau-1851-tgl8`.

title: Build /embed/lab/[experiment] with attribution and detail, theme, and reduced-motion parameters
description:
# Build /embed/lab/[experiment] with attribution and detail, theme, and reduced-motion parameters

**Epic:** `am-ep-instruments-8gi` · **Batch:** batch-h · **Priority:** P2 · **Plan sections:** §10.7, §15.1, §16.5, §16.6, §19.7 (P2) (traceability only)

## Background

Teachers and writers will want to place a single instrument in a course page or article. The plan makes every instrument embeddable at `/embed/lab/[experiment]` with attribution, a link back, and respect for detail, theme, and reduced-motion parameters. Embeds are a P2 innovation: useful for transfer, never required navigation, and never a reason to compromise privacy or security.

An embed must carry the same scientific honesty as the site: the execution label, the model note, the `notModeled` line, and a link to the source passage travel with the instrument.

## Scope

In scope: `src/app/embed/lab/[experiment]/page.tsx`, minimal chrome, attribution block, query parameters, framing policy, and embed snippet UI on the lab page.

Out of scope: the lab route (`am-inst-lab-route-f8f3`); site-wide CSP (`am-plat-security-f644`) beyond the embed-specific framing rule.

## Requirements

- Static params from the registry for instruments whose manifest sets `embeddable: true`; others return not-found.
- Minimal chrome: the question, the instrument, execution label and model note, `notModeled` line, and an attribution footer ("Annus Mirabilis, annus-mirabilis.com") with a link back to `/lab/[experiment]` and the source passage.
- Parameters: `detail` (reading level for captions), `theme` (Annalen, Kramgasse Night, Slate), `reducedMotion` (forces the reduced-motion path), `mode`, and an optional `tape` validated exactly like permalinks. Unknown parameters are ignored; invalid values fall back with a small notice inside the frame.
- Framing policy: `/embed/*` allows framing (`frame-ancestors *`) while all other routes deny framing; no third-party scripts, cookies, or analytics inside embeds; the clarity signal is not present in embeds.
- The embed never posts messages to the parent page and never reads parent state.
- Accessibility: a title for the frame content, keyboard operability inside the frame, and reduced motion honored from both the parameter and the user preference.
- Lab pages show a copyable embed snippet with an iframe `title` attribute and recommended height.

## Technical Approach

Reuse lab-route composition with an embed layout; route-specific headers configured through Next.js headers for framing policy.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Embeddable instruments render in a cross-origin iframe with attribution and link back; non-embeddable ids return not-found.
- [ ] Parameters work and invalid values fall back with a notice.
- [ ] Framing is allowed only under `/embed/*`; other routes deny framing (header test).
- [ ] No cookies or third-party requests occur inside embeds (network assertion).
- [ ] Keyboard and reduced-motion lanes pass inside an iframe host fixture.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests

- `embedRoute.params.test.ts`, `embedRoute.headers.test.ts`, `embedRoute.query.test.ts`.

### End-to-end tests

- A local host fixture page embeds BM-01 cross-origin; assertions on attribution, label, theme parameter, reduced motion, tape restoration, and absence of cookies and third-party requests.

### Structured logging

JSONL with `suite`, `testId`, `beadId`, `instrumentId`, `params`, `frameAncestorsHeader`, `thirdPartyRequests`, `cookiesSet`, `outcome`, `message`.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- Embeds must not become a tracking vector; keep them free of analytics entirely.
- Expand embeds only when they help explanation and transfer (the plan's P2 stop rule).

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-inst-lab-route-f8f3` (composition and data loading).
- `am-design-themes-typography-288q` (theme tokens selectable by parameter).

Unblocks: external reuse of instruments; no internal beads depend on it.

title: Show the four execution labels and the expandable model note, earned per accepted snapshot
description:
# Show the four execution labels and the expandable model note, earned per accepted snapshot

**Epic:** `am-ep-instruments-8gi` · **Batch:** batch-b · **Priority:** P0 · **Plan sections:** §2.2 (provenance states), §10.1, §11.4 (execution status), §12.9, §20 (WASM branding risk) (traceability only)

## Background

The donor museum learned the hard way that "WASM" is easy to print and hard to earn: a package can load while the displayed numbers come from unrelated JavaScript. Its coverage manifest distinguishes packaged surfaces, loaded artifacts, typed refusal boundaries, and accepted steps, with distinct `HONEST_PLACEHOLDER`, `TS_FALLBACK`, and `WASM` states. Annus Mirabilis keeps that underlying truth while presenting gentler public wording.

Execution status is one of the four kinds of meaning that must never be compressed into one color (logical role, historical status, model status, execution status). A reader must be able to tell a static worked example, a host calculation, an accepted FrankenSim result, and an unavailable experiment apart at a glance, and an expert must be able to open the exact artifact identity behind the number.

## Scope

In scope: the label component and model-note disclosure in `src/experiments/labels/`; the mapping from accepted snapshot metadata to label; integration with instrument chrome, the lab and embed routes, and show-the-code.

Out of scope: determining which engine ran (`am-rt-determinism-fallbacks-8i4`); worker scheduling; the show-the-code source extraction (`am-inst-show-the-code-4brv`).

## Requirements

### The four public labels

| Label | Earned when |
|---|---|
| "Ideal model, computed with FrankenSim" | An accepted call to the registered FrankenSim owner produced this snapshot |
| "Ideal model, host calculation" | The audited TypeScript reference evaluator produced this snapshot (closed-form physics is not a deficiency; the papers are closed-form) |
| "Static worked example" | The displayed state is a precomputed or authored example, not a live computation |
| "This experiment is unavailable on this device" | No admissible engine can run here; the static example and text remain |

- **A loaded WASM file does not earn the FrankenSim label; only an accepted result does.** The label is derived from `acceptedSnapshot.provenance.engine`, never from loader state.
- A fallback path can never show the FrankenSim label; a test asserts the label for every fallback state.
- While a new request is pending, the label continues to describe the last accepted snapshot, and a separate pending indicator says the displayed numbers belong to the previous accepted inputs.

### The model note (expandable)

Shown on demand, in plain words with exact identifiers:
- owner (module and function, or FrankenSim capability and export);
- model version and artifact digest (content-addressed WASM digest or source hash of the evaluator);
- constant set id;
- seed (decimal string) and stream-semantics version for stochastic runs;
- accepted input revision and snapshot version;
- whether this run is a fallback and why (WASM not loaded, refused, or artifact mismatch);
- comparison kind recorded for cross-engine checks (`bitwise` or `tolerance`) where applicable;
- the instrument's `notModeled` line and model assumptions;
- link to "Show the code."

Internal enum names never leak as cryptic warnings; each state has an ordinary-language sentence.

### Placement and accessibility

- The label sits with every live readout region and in the embed chrome; it is text, not color alone, with an accessible name that includes the full label.
- Label changes are announced only when an accepted snapshot changes engine, not on every frame.

## Technical Approach

- `executionLabelFor(snapshot)` pure function with exhaustive switch over provenance states; `ModelNote` component renders the fields above from snapshot metadata and the registry entry.
- Adapt the donor coverage-manifest provenance states (`HONEST_PLACEHOLDER`, `TS_FALLBACK`, `WASM`) as internal states mapped to public labels.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The label is computed only from accepted snapshot provenance; loader state has no path to the label.
- [ ] Every fallback and unavailable state maps to the correct public label; FrankenSim label appears only with an accepted FrankenSim result.
- [ ] Pending requests keep the previous label with a visible pending indicator.
- [ ] The model note shows all listed fields for host, FrankenSim, static, and unavailable states.
- [ ] Keyboard access to the model note; label text readable by screen readers; no color-only meaning.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests

- `executionLabel.test.ts`: exhaustive mapping from provenance states; a snapshot with `wasmLoaded: true` but engine `reference` must show host calculation.
- `modelNote.test.tsx`: field rendering for each state; decimal-string seeds above $2^{53}$ displayed exactly.
- `pendingState.test.tsx`: label persists across pending requests.

### End-to-end tests

- Lane with WASM blocked (network interception): the instrument shows "Ideal model, host calculation" and the model note says why.
- Lane with WASM available: after the first accepted FrankenSim step the label changes; before it, the label is host or static.
- No-worker lane: "This experiment is unavailable on this device" with the static example.

### Structured logging

JSONL with `suite`, `testId`, `beadId`, `instrumentId`, `snapshotVersion`, `engine`, `executionLabel`, `artifactDigest`, `fallbackReason`, `outcome`, `message`.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- Never label a HUD with the engine name when the value came from a different engine.
- A checksum shows byte identity, not compatible meaning; artifact mismatch pauses the lab rather than relabeling numbers.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-rt-determinism-fallbacks-8i4` (engine selection, fallback states, reproducibility metadata on snapshots).

Unblocks:
- `am-bm-01-tracer-ensemble-hdly`, `am-bm-05-random-steps-ntzl`, `am-bm-06-gaussian-spread-982y` and every later instrument.

title: Build event, interval, partition, coefficient, channel, and expression interactions with nonvisual equivalents
description:
# Build event, interval, partition, coefficient, channel, and expression interactions with nonvisual equivalents

**Epic:** `am-ep-instruments-8gi` · **Batch:** batch-b · **Priority:** P0 · **Plan sections:** §10.4, §10.5, §15.6, §16.2, §19.7 (P0: equivalent nonvisual actions) (traceability only)

## Background

"Sliders suit continuous parameters and nothing else." Simultaneity is a question about choosing events; an integral is a question about choosing an interval; entropy at fixed energy is a question about resizing a constrained volume; a transformation is a question about coefficients; an energy balance is a question about which channel or boundary you include; a derivation is a question about which subexpression you transform.

The plan makes nonvisual equivalence a P0 requirement: a reader who cannot drag, cannot distinguish colors, cannot hear, or cannot see a canvas must still perform the **same scientific action**, not read a long description of someone else doing it. This bead builds the six interaction primitives with that equivalence built in, through the action-contract framework.

## Scope

In scope: `src/experiments/interactions/` primitives, each exposing visual, keyboard, typed, and screen-reader forms of one typed action; integration with the action-contract framework and the runtime command classes.

Out of scope: the action-contract registry and audit (`am-a11y-action-contracts-k75g`); schema-driven sliders (`am-inst-parameter-controls-cmj9`); derivation-chain data (`am-eq-derivation-chains-r4c`).

## Requirements

Each primitive emits a typed action `{ instrumentId, actionId, inputs, commandClass }` handled by the runtime; the visual and nonvisual forms emit identical actions and produce identical accepted snapshots.

| Primitive | Visual action | Equivalent scientific action |
|---|---|---|
| `EventSelector` (clock and event geometry) | Select points on a diagram | Choose named events from a table and ask which frame regards them as simultaneous |
| `IntervalSelector` (probability and diffusion) | Drag a selected histogram interval | Enter lower and upper limits, inspect interval probability, compare two named intervals |
| `PartitionControl` (radiation entropy) | Resize the constrained-state volume | Enter a ratio or choose half, same, or double, with fixed energy and band stated |
| `CoefficientEditor` (fields, boosts, candidate maps) | Rotate an arrow, move an observer, edit a coefficient handle | Select an axis or component and a signed magnitude, then inspect transformed components at the same event |
| `BoundaryChannelSelector` (energy accounting) | Drag a boundary around objects | Select the objects included in the system and inspect energy crossing that boundary |
| `ExpressionActionPicker` (derivations) | Highlight and transform part of an equation | Select a named subexpression, read its role, and advance a justified step |

### Behavior requirements

- Every primitive is keyboard operable with visible focus, has accessible names and descriptions, and works with touch at 320 px.
- Typed entry accepts units through the quantity registry and validates against the owner's domain; invalid entries explain the problem without issuing an action.
- Screen-reader summaries are at the scale of the question (selected events and their frame classification, interval and its probability, system members and boundary flux), never a stream of particle coordinates.
- Observer changes (`observer-change`) never create events or restart runs; physical changes use their own classes. The primitive's copy names which kind of change it performs.
- A scene starts with a useful question and a stable default selection; clearing a selection is explicit.

## Technical Approach

- Headless primitives (state and actions) plus visual adapters for SVG and Canvas views from `am-inst-2d-view-kit-u75r` and nonvisual adapters (tables, form fields, listboxes).
- Each primitive registers its action contract entry so the audit can verify parity.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All six primitives exist with visual, keyboard, typed, and screen-reader forms emitting identical typed actions.
- [ ] Parity tests: performing the visual action and the nonvisual action from the same state yields the same accepted snapshot id and outputs.
- [ ] Keyboard-only and screen-reader smoke tests pass for each primitive; no tooltip-only information.
- [ ] Observer-change actions preserve run and event identities.
- [ ] 320 px layouts have no horizontal overflow and usable touch targets.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests

- `interactions.parity.test.tsx`: for each primitive, drive visual and nonvisual paths with the same inputs and compare emitted actions and resulting snapshots from a real owner fixture.
- `interactions.validation.test.tsx`: unit-aware typed entry and domain explanations.
- `interactions.commandClass.test.ts`: declared classes reach the runtime.

### End-to-end tests

- BM-06 interval selection lane: keyboard entry of limits equals drag selection (same probability and snapshot id).
- SR-03 event selection lane (later instrument) uses the same primitive; this bead supplies a fixture experiment for harness testing.
- Screen-reader lane: selection summaries announced once per committed action.

### Structured logging

JSONL with `suite`, `testId`, `beadId`, `instrumentId`, `actionId`, `inputMode` (`pointer` | `keyboard` | `typed` | `screen-reader`), `commandClass`, `snapshotVersion`, `outcome`, `message`.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- A long prose description alone is not equivalent to being able to investigate.
- Do not generalize beyond the needs of BM-06 and one fixture per family until `am-bm-slice-retrospective-pp09`.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-inst-parameter-controls-cmj9` (shared validation, units, and command dispatch).
- `am-a11y-action-contracts-k75g` (the contract framework each primitive registers with).

Unblocks:
- `am-bm-06-gaussian-spread-982y` (interval selection) and later instruments using events, partitions, coefficients, channels, and expressions.

title: Build the /lab/[experiment] standalone workbench route with source and explanation links
description:
# Build the /lab/[experiment] standalone workbench route with source and explanation links

**Epic:** `am-ep-instruments-8gi` · **Batch:** batch-b · **Priority:** P1 · **Plan sections:** §6.9 (Discover and Experiment are routes), §10.7, §15.1, §15.4, §16.3 (traceability only)

## Background

Instruments live inside the reading face at the step they illuminate, but readers also need a standalone workbench: a teacher projecting BM-01, a programmer exploring SR-04's matrix, a reader returning to the photoelectric apparatus. The plan defines `/lab/[experiment]` as that workbench with source and explanation links, one canonical URL per experiment, and Open Graph cards per laboratory.

The route must remain a book page first: meaningful static HTML without JavaScript, a clear question at the top, and links back to the exact source passages and explanations the instrument serves.

## Scope

In scope: `src/app/lab/[experiment]/page.tsx` with static params from the registry, layout, header, source and explanation links, static worked example, share and model note placement, metadata and Open Graph hooks, not-found behavior.

Out of scope: the embed route (`am-inst-embed-route-rnyg`); Open Graph image generation (`am-design-og-images-pwok`); instruments themselves.

## Requirements

- `generateStaticParams` from the registry; unknown experiment ids return the App Router not-found page (never another instrument).
- Page anatomy: the instrument's explanatory question; the instrument (lazy) with its execution label and model note; "Read this in the paper" links to the anchored source passages (German and English) and "Why this matters" links to the explanation anchors from the manifest; "What this does not model" line; related misconceptions; predict mode default behavior.
- Modes via `?mode=` for instruments with registered modes (for example `lq-08:count-model`), validated against the registry.
- Without JavaScript: the static worked example, the question, the `notModeled` line, and real links remain.
- Metadata: title and description from the manifest; `rel=canonical` without tape or mode noise (modes with distinct scientific content may be canonical subpages if registered).
- Layout follows page anatomy rules: single column on phones with the instrument above its explanation, a bounded sticky lab region on desktop that never traps scroll, no page-level horizontal overflow at 320 px.
- Print: the static representation of the current state with its parameters and a caption.

## Technical Approach

App Router page with server-rendered shell and dispatcher from `am-inst-registry-dispatcher-66l0`; data from compiled route-local payloads, not the aggregate registry.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every registered experiment has a static lab page; an unknown id returns not-found.
- [ ] Source and explanation links resolve to existing anchors (build-time check).
- [ ] JavaScript-disabled render shows question, static example, `notModeled`, and links.
- [ ] 320 px, keyboard-only, and reduced-motion lanes pass.
- [ ] The initial route bundle excludes Three.js, the PDF viewer, and WASM.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests

- `labRoute.params.test.ts`: static params match registry; unknown id not-found.
- `labRoute.links.test.ts`: anchor resolution against compiled content.

### End-to-end tests

- Lanes for BM-01 lab page: desktop, 320 px touch, keyboard only, JavaScript disabled, reduced motion, print emulation; assertions on question text, label, links, and no horizontal overflow.

### Structured logging

JSONL with `suite`, `testId`, `beadId`, `route`, `instrumentId`, `viewport`, `jsEnabled`, `brokenLinks`, `bundleBytes`, `outcome`, `message`.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- One canonical URL per experiment; slider positions are never canonical pages.
- Keep the lab page from becoming a dense control panel; advanced settings stay in the drawer.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-inst-registry-dispatcher-66l0` (registry and dispatcher).
- `am-read-shell-routes-3ua` (App Router shell, layout, and anchors infrastructure).

Unblocks:
- `am-inst-embed-route-rnyg` (embed pages reuse the lab route's composition).

title: Generate controls, URL-state validation, and domain explanations from the parameter schema
description:
# Generate controls, URL-state validation, and domain explanations from the parameter schema

**Epic:** `am-ep-instruments-8gi` · **Batch:** batch-b · **Priority:** P0 · **Plan sections:** §10.3, §10.4, §10.7, §12.6, §12.10, §16.2, §16.5 (traceability only)

## Background

A slider that silently clamps a value while its label shows what the reader typed is a small lie that corrupts every conclusion drawn from the instrument. The plan requires one parameter schema per control that declares physical dimension, display unit, valid model domain, numerical domain, pedagogical default, step or logarithmic mapping, and whether the parameter is independent or derived. That single schema generates the control, URL-state validation, unit formatting, and test cases.

Controls are also where the runtime's command classes meet the reader. Changing initial conditions, intervening mid-run, changing the observer, changing a measurement, changing an estimator, and changing presentation are different operations with different guarantees; each control declares which one it issues.

## Scope

In scope: schema-driven control generation in `src/experiments/controls/`; typed value entry and step buttons beside sliders; domain explanations; URL-state validation; the "Experiment settings" drawer; reset semantics; command-class mapping; seed inputs.

Out of scope: non-slider interactions (`am-inst-interaction-primitives-emwy`); permalink tapes (`am-inst-permalink-tape-s677`); the runtime command semantics (`am-rt-command-classes-dzp`).

## Requirements

### Schema fields (from the experiment manifest)

`dimension`, `displayUnit`, `modelDomain` (interval or set with the reason text for each boundary), `numericalDomain`, `visualRange` (may be narrower than the model domain), `default`, `mapping` (`linear` | `log` with base), `step`, `independent | derived`, `commandClass` (`setup-change` | `physical-intervention` | `observer-change` | `measurement-change` | `estimator-change` | `presentation-change`), accessible name and description.

### Suggested teaching ranges (admitted by owners, documented separately from mathematical domains)

- Radiation temperature 500–10 000 K; logarithmic frequency over $10^{11}$–$10^{16}$ Hz.
- Photoelectric work function 1–6 eV, hypothetical unless a cited metal card is chosen; photoelectric frequency 100–2 000 THz.
- Brownian radius 0.1–5 μm in the dilute-sphere model; viscosity 0.5–20 mPa·s as an explicit fluid parameter (temperature never silently supplies an unmodeled viscosity law); temperature 273–330 K; a gas card refuses because Stokes drag without the Cunningham slip correction is invalid when the mean free path is comparable to the radius.
- Frame speed signed $v/c$ within ±0.95 in the core; no inertial observer at $\lvert v\rvert \ge c$.
- Emitted energy as a positive pedagogical range plus normalized ratios.
- Sample counts and time horizons explicit and finite; a memory or time budget failure is distinct from physical invalidity.

### Control behavior

- Slider plus typed exact-value input plus step buttons, following the WAI-ARIA slider pattern and its warning about touch assistive technology (typed entry is always available).
- Typed values outside the visual range but inside the model domain are accepted and the slider shows the value is beyond its track.
- Out-of-domain inputs are **never silently clamped**. The control shows the problem in ordinary language, offers the admissible boundary or a model change, and does not issue a command until the reader chooses.
- Derived parameters display as read-only values computed by the owner.
- Units display through the quantity registry; entry accepts the display unit and documented alternatives (for example mPa·s and Pa·s) with explicit conversion.

### Seeds and trials

- Seed inputs accept unsigned 64-bit decimal strings; invalid signs, whitespace, overlong input, and overflow are rejected with a message. "Same seed" and "new trial" are explicit actions; a new trial records the chosen seed.

### Drawer and reset

- A scene begins with a useful question and a stable default. Advanced controls live in an "Experiment settings" drawer.
- Reset restores parameters and the relevant experiment history; the reset action states whether it keeps the seed or starts a new trial.

### URL state

- Each control can serialize to and from URL parameters with strict validation (bounded length, known keys, canonical decimal strings, domain checks). Invalid URL state is ignored with a visible notice and the default is used; it never crashes or clamps silently.
- Canonical document URLs are unaffected by control state.

## Technical Approach

- `buildControls(schema)` returns React components and a validation module generated from the same schema; property tests derive valid and invalid cases from domains.
- Commands dispatch through the runtime with their declared class; the control never mutates snapshots.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Controls generated from schema for all field types; typed entry, step buttons, and slider stay synchronized.
- [ ] No code path clamps silently; out-of-domain entries produce explanations and admissible options.
- [ ] Command class is declared for every control and verified by a test that checks the runtime receives the right class.
- [ ] Seed inputs round-trip values at $2^{53}$ and $2^{53} \pm 1$, zero, and $2^{64} - 1$; invalid inputs are rejected.
- [ ] URL state validates strictly; invalid state falls back to defaults with a notice.
- [ ] Keyboard-only operation, visible focus, accessible names, and 320 px layout pass.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests

- `controls.schema.test.ts`: generation for each field type; derived read-only behavior.
- `controls.domain.test.ts`: property tests for inside, boundary, and outside values; no clamp assertions.
- `controls.seed.test.ts`: 64-bit decimal handling.
- `controls.url.test.ts`: serialization round trips, rejection of oversize or unknown keys.
- `controls.commandClass.test.ts`: dispatched class per control.

### End-to-end tests

- Keyboard-only lane types an out-of-domain viscosity and asserts the explanation and that the snapshot's accepted input revision is unchanged.
- Touch lane at 320 px uses step buttons; screen-reader smoke check verifies names and value text.

### Structured logging

JSONL with `suite`, `testId`, `beadId`, `instrumentId`, `parameterId`, `inputValue`, `domainStatus`, `commandClass`, `inputRevision`, `acceptedInputRevision`, `outcome`, `message`.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- A control's visual range and its mathematical domain are different facts; document both.
- Changing a camera's physical exposure is a measurement change; moving the rendered microscope viewpoint is presentation; a moving detector is a physical component, not a frame choice. Name these in ordinary language on the control.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-inst-registry-dispatcher-66l0` (controls are attached to registered instruments).
- `am-not-quantity-registry-2f7` (dimensions, units, formatting).
- `am-rt-u64-identities-7ce` (64-bit seed validation and transport).

Unblocks:
- `am-inst-interaction-primitives-emwy`, `am-inst-permalink-tape-s677`.
- `am-bm-01-tracer-ensemble-hdly`, `am-bm-05-random-steps-ntzl`.

title: Serialize accepted identities and compact tapes into bounded ?tape= permalinks
description:
# Serialize accepted identities and compact tapes into bounded ?tape= permalinks

**Epic:** `am-ep-instruments-8gi` · **Batch:** batch-b · **Priority:** P1 · **Plan sections:** §7.7, §10.7, §12.10, §12.11, §15.1, §16.5 (traceability only)

## Background

A reader should be able to share exactly what they saw: the same experiment, the same seed, the same sequence of controls, and even their prediction, so a teacher can see what a class expected. The plan specifies that permalinks serialize the accepted snapshot's identities and a compact valid control tape into `?tape=`, with bounded size. Canonical document URLs never multiply into an index of slider positions.

Permalinks are also an attack surface and a correctness trap. URL state is untrusted input; a malicious or accidental tape must not freeze the page, and a 64-bit seed must never be rounded through a JavaScript number.

## Scope

In scope: tape encoding and decoding for URLs in `src/experiments/permalink/`; validation and bounds; restoration by replaying to the accepted snapshot; share UI; canonical and indexing rules.

Out of scope: tape semantics and checkpoints (`am-rt-control-tapes-0gc`); control validation (`am-inst-parameter-controls-cmj9`); CSP and global security review (`am-plat-security-f644`).

## Requirements

- **Payload:** version, experiment id and mode, model version, constant set id, seed (canonical unsigned 64-bit decimal string), stream version, quantized control events with command classes and logical times, optional `prediction` events, and the expected final accepted snapshot identity (input revision count and checkpoint digest `host:` or `blake3:`).
- **Encoding:** compact JSON or a documented binary layout, compressed and base64url encoded; decimal strings for all 64-bit values; no `BigInt` passed through ordinary JSON.
- **Bounds:** maximum encoded length (declare a limit, for example 2 048 characters, and test it), maximum event count, and per-parameter domain checks. Oversize, unknown version, unknown experiment, out-of-domain values, or malformed input produce a visible notice ("This shared state could not be restored: reason") and load defaults. Nothing is silently clamped.
- **Restoration:** replay events through the runtime in logical order; when the reproduced checkpoint digest differs from the stored one, show a notice that the run was reproduced under a different model or artifact version and keep both identities visible in the model note.
- **Canonical URLs:** pages with `?tape=` declare `rel=canonical` without the parameter and `noindex` for the tape variant; sitemaps never list tape URLs.
- **Share UI:** a "Copy link to this experiment state" action with an accessible confirmation; works without clipboard permission by showing the URL in a selectable field.

## Technical Approach

- Encoder and decoder as pure functions with schema validation; replay uses the runtime's tape player.
- Fuzz tests with a fixed seed corpus for decoder robustness.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Round trip: encode, decode, replay reproduces the same accepted snapshot identity for BM-01 with seeds $0$, $2^{53}$, $2^{53} + 1$, and $2^{64} - 1$.
- [ ] Oversize, malformed, unknown-version, and out-of-domain tapes produce notices and defaults, never crashes or hangs.
- [ ] Prediction events survive round trips.
- [ ] Tape URLs are `noindex` and canonicalize to the document URL.
- [ ] Decoder fuzzing over the fixed corpus finds no unhandled exceptions and stays within a declared time bound.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests

- `permalink.encode.test.ts`, `permalink.decode.test.ts` (bounds and errors), `permalink.u64.test.ts`, `permalink.replay.test.ts` (real runtime and owner fixtures), `permalink.fuzz.test.ts` (fixed corpus, time bound).

### End-to-end tests

- Lane: set BM-01 parameters and a prediction, copy the permalink, open it in a fresh context, assert identical snapshot identity, overlay, and model note.
- Lane: open a truncated tape URL and assert the notice and defaults.

### Structured logging

JSONL with `suite`, `testId`, `beadId`, `instrumentId`, `tapeLength`, `eventCount`, `seed`, `restoreStatus`, `checkpointDigestExpected`, `checkpointDigestActual`, `outcome`, `message`.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- Never hash a rounded decimal display of a seed.
- A tape records logical actions, not render frames; render cadence must not affect restoration.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-rt-control-tapes-0gc` (tape format, checkpoints, prediction events).
- `am-inst-parameter-controls-cmj9` (domain validation and 64-bit seed handling).

Unblocks:
- `am-plat-security-f644` (reviews bounded URL state) and sharing in every instrument, the lab route, and embeds.

title: Build predict mode with hidden response, candidate curves or sketches, overlay, and tape events
description:
# Build predict mode with hidden response, candidate curves or sketches, overlay, and tape events

**Epic:** `am-ep-instruments-8gi` · **Batch:** batch-b · **Priority:** P1 · **Plan sections:** §6.7, §7.7, §10.7, §12.11, §14.5, §19.7 (P1) (traceability only)

## Background

Predicting before seeing is one of the cheapest ways to make an interaction teach instead of entertain. The plan specifies a predict mode on every instrument, on by default for first-time visitors: before the reader's first change the response plot is hidden and the reader chooses or sketches what will happen. When the reader releases the control, the accepted snapshot draws the real curve over the prediction and both stay visible.

The design rules come from the plan's reading of the education literature: productive exploration followed by sufficient explanation, never compulsory rediscovery, and never a judgment of the person. An incorrect prediction is a productive starting point, not a usability failure. The explanation is available regardless of the prediction.

## Scope

In scope: `src/experiments/predict/` for the hidden-response state, candidate curves, freehand sketch, nonvisual prediction forms, overlay, first-visit default, exemption handling, and the `prediction` tape event.

Out of scope: tape infrastructure (`am-rt-control-tapes-0gc`); chapter-end predict-perturb-explain tasks (`am-disc-ppe-teachback-wnp7`); per-instrument candidate authoring (instrument beads).

## Requirements

- **Default:** on for first-time visitors of each instrument, remembered locally through the storage layer; the reader can turn it off globally or per instrument. Storage failure falls back to "on" without errors.
- **Hidden response:** before the first change, the response region shows empty axes with labeled units and the question; derived readouts that would reveal the answer are hidden too.
- **Ways to predict:**
  - choose one of three authored candidate curves (supplied by the instrument manifest, each a plausible model with a one-line description, not two foolish options and one right one);
  - sketch a freehand line on empty axes;
  - nonvisual equivalent: choose the expected direction and shape in words (increase, decrease, unchanged; linear, square-root, other) or type expected values at named points.
- **Reveal:** after the first accepted snapshot following the change, overlay the real curve on the prediction with a visible legend distinguishing "your prediction" and the computed result (non-color identity included). Both remain until the reader clears them.
- **Tape event:** record `{ type: "prediction", instrumentId, form: "candidate" | "sketch" | "verbal" | "values", payload }` on the control tape so a shared permalink carries it and a teacher can see what a class expected. Sketches are simplified to bounded point sets before serialization.
- **Feedback language:** describes the relationship (for example, "the spread grows with the square root of time, so doubling the time increases it by about 1.41") and never scores the person, uses red crosses, or implies failure.
- **Exemptions:** an instrument may declare `predictMode: { exempt: true, reason }` in its manifest (for example an event ledger whose first action is itself the prediction); the audit requires a non-empty reason.
- **Explanation access:** "Show me the reasoning" is available before and after predicting.

## Technical Approach

- A predict-state machine per instance (`hidden` → `predicted` → `revealed` → `cleared`), driven by the instance's first command after mount.
- Sketch capture on a canvas layer with pointer and keyboard drawing (arrow keys move a cursor, space adds a point), simplified with a documented tolerance.
- Uses `am-plat-local-storage-km8f` for the first-visit flag and `am-rt-control-tapes-0gc` for events.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Predict mode is on for first visits and can be disabled; storage failure keeps it on without errors.
- [ ] Candidate, sketch, verbal, and value predictions work with pointer, keyboard, and screen reader.
- [ ] The response and revealing readouts stay hidden until the first accepted snapshot after a change.
- [ ] The overlay distinguishes prediction and result without relying on color.
- [ ] Prediction events serialize into tapes and restore from permalinks.
- [ ] Exempt instruments show no predict UI and have a recorded reason; the audit fails on an empty reason.
- [ ] No scoring language appears anywhere in predict mode copy (voice lint rule).

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests

- `predictState.test.ts`: transitions, clear, re-predict, storage-failure behavior.
- `predictSketch.test.tsx`: pointer and keyboard sketch capture and simplification bounds.
- `predictTape.test.ts`: event serialization and restoration, including bounded payload size.
- `predictExemption.test.ts`: manifest validation.

### End-to-end tests

- First-visit lane on BM-01: axes hidden, choose a candidate, change the observation interval, assert overlay and hidden readouts appear; reload with a permalink and assert the prediction is restored.
- Keyboard-only lane: verbal prediction path end to end.
- Reduced-motion lane: reveal without animation.

### Structured logging

JSONL with `suite`, `testId`, `beadId`, `instrumentId`, `predictState`, `predictionForm`, `tapeEventCount`, `snapshotVersion`, `outcome`, `message`.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- Being surprised is not the same as learning; predict mode must never delay the explanation.
- Do not equate a matching sketch with understanding; no automatic correctness judgment of free-form predictions.
- Expand beyond the Brownian slice only after observed readers show it resolves a misunderstanding (the plan's stop rule for P1 innovations).

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-inst-registry-dispatcher-66l0` (instances and manifests).
- `am-rt-control-tapes-0gc` (prediction events on tapes).
- `am-plat-local-storage-km8f` (failure-tolerant first-visit flag).

Unblocks:
- Per-instrument predict candidates in every instrument bead; the reference slice's first-encounter and journey steps use it.

title: Offer true physical rate with a scale bar where a natural rate exists
description:
# Offer true physical rate with a scale bar where a natural rate exists

**Epic:** `am-ep-instruments-8gi` · **Batch:** batch-h · **Priority:** P2 · **Plan sections:** §10.2 (BM-01 real-time toggle), §10.7, §12.5, §12.6, §16.2 (traceability only)

## Background

Speeding up a random walk makes its shape visible, but it can also mislead: a reader may come away thinking Brownian particles dart about. Einstein's printed estimate says a half-micron-radius sphere in water wanders about 0.8 μm in one second, which is slow and visible in an ordinary microscope. The plan asks every instrument with a natural physical rate to offer a true-rate view with a calibrated scale bar beside the sped-up version.

True rate is a **presentation change**. It never changes the stochastic experiment, the time step, the seed, or the statistics; it only changes how accepted snapshots are replayed against wall-clock time.

## Scope

In scope: a real-rate playback controller in `src/experiments/playback/`, the UI toggle, calibrated scale bars and time readouts, side-by-side true-rate and accelerated views, and the list of eligible instruments.

Out of scope: runtime stepping (`am-rt-worker-scheduler-7tl`); tape format (`am-rt-control-tapes-0gc`); scale bar drawing primitive (`am-inst-2d-view-kit-u75r`).

## Requirements

- Eligibility declared in each manifest: `naturalRate: { quantity, scale }`. Initial eligible set: BM-01 (tracer wandering at microscope scale), BM-05 and BM-06 when shown against physical time, the kitchen real-data mode (video frame rate). Relativity and radiation instruments whose natural rates are unwatchable (for example $0.6c$ motion or optical frequencies) are not eligible and show no toggle.
- The toggle issues a `presentation-change` command; accepted snapshot identities, run id, and statistics remain unchanged (test).
- Playback maps simulated time to wall time at 1:1 using host-fed time; interpolation affects display only; if the replay grid is coarser than the display frame rate, the view holds or interpolates and labels the interpolation as rendering.
- Scale bar with a physical length (for example 1 μm) derived from calibration, and a time readout in seconds of simulated time; side-by-side mode shows true rate and accelerated rate with their speed factors labeled.
- Reduced motion: true-rate animation does not autoplay; a step control and a static description of the displacement per second are shown.
- Accessible summary: "At true rate a tracer of radius 0.5 μm in water at 17 °C moves about 0.8 μm in one second," computed from the snapshot.

## Technical Approach

A playback clock bound to the instance store that consumes snapshots on a declared replay grid; no new draws or steps are requested because of playback speed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Eligible instruments show the toggle; ineligible ones do not.
- [ ] Switching rates leaves snapshot identities and statistics unchanged.
- [ ] Scale bars are calibrated from snapshot and manifest data; time readouts show simulated seconds.
- [ ] Reduced motion disables autoplay and provides step controls and a textual rate summary.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests

- `realRate.clock.test.ts`: 1:1 mapping with host-fed time, holding and interpolation labels.
- `realRate.invariance.test.ts`: presentation-change leaves run id, seed, accepted input revision, and computed moments unchanged.
- `realRate.eligibility.test.ts`: manifest validation.

### End-to-end tests

- BM-01 lane: toggle true rate, measure displayed displacement over one second against the snapshot's $\lambda_x$ within display tolerance, assert statistics panel unchanged; reduced-motion lane shows step controls.

### Structured logging

JSONL with `suite`, `testId`, `beadId`, `instrumentId`, `playbackRate`, `runId`, `snapshotVersion`, `displayedDisplacementUm`, `expectedDisplacementUm`, `outcome`, `message`.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- Never compute a speed from the rendered polyline; the displayed motion is a rendering of sampled positions.
- Render cadence must never change the experiment.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-inst-registry-dispatcher-66l0` (manifests and instance binding).
- `am-rt-control-tapes-0gc` (host-fed time and replay semantics).

Unblocks: BM-01's real-time toggle and the kitchen mode's video-rate replay.

title: Build the exhaustive experiment registry and dispatcher where unknown ids fail explicitly
description:
# Build the exhaustive experiment registry and dispatcher where unknown ids fail explicitly

**Epic:** `am-ep-instruments-8gi` · **Batch:** batch-b · **Priority:** P0 · **Plan sections:** §2.2, §2.3, §10.1, §10.8, §12.1, §12.5, §12.12, §17.3 (traceability only)

## Background

The donor museum defaulted its visual dispatcher to the Wright Flyer, so an unregistered record silently showed another patent's machine. On a scientific edition that failure is worse than a crash: a reader would see a plausible, wrong model and trust it. The plan's rule is absolute: **every experiment id has an explicit case, and an unknown id fails explicitly.**

The registry is also where the ownership rule becomes enforceable. Each instrument binds to one computational owner (a reference evaluator, a FrankenSim capability, or an explicit static status) through the runtime, and views consume only accepted snapshots. The dispatcher lazily loads each instrument's views so heavy code never enters the reading route.

## Scope

In scope: `src/experiments/registry.ts` (typed registry), `src/experiments/dispatch.tsx` (lazy dispatcher), manifest loading from `content/experiments/<id>.yaml`, explicit unavailable states, and the architectural guards that stop views from importing owners or computing physics.

Out of scope: the snapshot store and worker runtime (`am-rt-snapshot-store-aft`, `am-rt-worker-scheduler-7tl`); controls (`am-inst-parameter-controls-cmj9`); the lab route (`am-inst-lab-route-f8f3`); individual instruments.

## Requirements

### Registry

- Instrument ids: `lq-01` … `lq-09`, `bm-01` … `bm-08`, `sr-01` … `sr-13`, `me-01` … `me-03`, plus shelf instruments registered under their own ids; modes addressed as `lq-08:count-model`.
- Each entry references the compiled `Experiment` manifest (question, source and argument ids, parameter schema, outputs with statuses, views, default scenario, provenance, `notModeled`, acceptance cases, tape model identity, embeddable flag, predict-mode flag or exemption, action contract).
- Each entry names exactly one owner binding: `{ kind: "reference", module, function }`, `{ kind: "frankensim", capability, export }` with a reference fallback, or `{ kind: "static-worked-example" }`. Entries without an owner or explicit static status fail the build (shared rule with the content compiler).
- The TypeScript registry type is a closed union of ids; a `switch` over ids ends in an exhaustiveness check (`const _exhaustive: never = id`).

### Dispatcher

- `ExperimentView({ id, mode, instanceId })` resolves the registry entry and lazy-loads the view module with `next/dynamic` (`ssr: false` for canvas and WebGL views), rendering the static worked example from the compiled payload in the server HTML so the page stays meaningful without JavaScript.
- **Unknown ids** render an explicit state, "This experiment is not available here," with the requested id, a link to the paper passage if known, and no substitute instrument. There is no default case.
- **Unavailable on this device** (worker or WASM missing, WebGL missing for a 3D-only view) renders the public label "This experiment is unavailable on this device" plus the static worked example.
- Views receive an `instanceId` and subscribe to the instance store; two mounted instances of the same experiment are independent.

### Architectural guards

- A lint rule or import-graph test fails if any module under `src/visuals/` or an instrument view directory imports `src/physics/reference/*` or a WASM loader directly; views get numbers only from accepted snapshots.
- A test scans view modules for forbidden calls (`Math.random`, direct physics formulas flagged by a curated list such as `Math.exp(-` inside view files is allowed only in rendering helpers with an allowlist) and fails with the file and line.
- A test enumerates every manifest in `content/experiments/` and asserts a registry case exists, and vice versa.

## Technical Approach

- Registry generated from compiled manifests at build time into a typed module, with the hand-written owner bindings in `src/experiments/owners.ts`.
- Dispatcher tests use the real registry and real compiled fixtures, not mocks.
- Adapt the donor `dispatcher.test.ts` pattern, replacing its Wright default with explicit failure.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every registered id has an explicit case; the exhaustiveness check compiles only when all ids are handled.
- [ ] An unknown id renders the explicit unavailable state; a test proves no other instrument renders.
- [ ] A manifest without owner or static status fails the build with an actionable message.
- [ ] Views cannot import reference evaluators or WASM loaders (guard test fails on a planted violation in a fixture directory).
- [ ] Heavy view modules are not part of the initial reading route bundle (bundle analysis assertion).
- [ ] Two instances of the same experiment on one page do not share state.
- [ ] With JavaScript disabled the static worked example appears in place of each instrument.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests

- `registry.test.ts`: manifests versus cases in both directions; owner binding validity; mode addressing.
- `dispatch.test.tsx`: unknown id state; unavailable-device state; lazy loading; instance independence.
- `viewImportGuard.test.ts`: import graph check with a planted violation fixture.

### End-to-end tests

- Browser lane (via `am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh` once available): load a paper page with an unknown experiment reference in a test fixture route and assert the explicit unavailable text; load two instances of BM-01 and change one control, asserting the other's snapshot id is unchanged; JavaScript-disabled lane shows static examples.

### Structured logging

JSONL with `suite`, `testId`, `beadId`, `instrumentId`, `instanceId`, `ownerKind`, `outcome`, `message`; bundle assertions log route and byte counts.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- Resist a generic "fallback instrument." A missing case is a bug that must be visible.
- Keep the catalogue finite: modes of a shared workbench are registered as modes, not new ids.
- Do not generalize registry features beyond what the Brownian slice needs until `am-bm-slice-retrospective-pp09`.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-cm-schemas-experiment-fuu` (the manifest schema the registry reads).
- `am-rt-snapshot-store-aft` (instance-scoped stores the dispatcher binds views to).

Unblocks:
- `am-inst-2d-view-kit-u75r`, `am-inst-parameter-controls-cmj9`, `am-inst-predict-mode-ti7m`, `am-inst-show-the-code-4brv`, `am-inst-lab-route-f8f3`, `am-inst-real-rate-mode-gtez`.
- `am-a11y-action-contracts-k75g`, `am-disc-journey-framework-umbg`, `am-disc-shelf-michelson-fizeau-dauq`.

title: Extract and pin kernel source for show-the-code with colorized identifiers and binding tests
description:
# Extract and pin kernel source for show-the-code with colorized identifiers and binding tests

**Epic:** `am-ep-instruments-8gi` · **Batch:** batch-b · **Priority:** P1 · **Plan sections:** §7.8, §11.7, §12.12, §15.5, §17.3 (extract-kernel-source.ts) (traceability only)

## Background

"For programmers the code is the derivation; for everyone else it is proof that the number on the screen came from a function anyone can read." Every instrument and every derivation chain gets a "Show the code" disclosure that renders the kernel's actual source (the TypeScript reference evaluator, and the Rust of the FrankenSim owner where it applies), extracted at build time with the function's source hash pinned to the instrument.

Identifiers that correspond to equation terms share the term's color, so `gamma` in the code, $\gamma$ in the formula, and "the stretch factor" in the sentence are visibly the same quantity. The compiler also uses this binding as a correctness check: an instrument whose live terms do not appear as identifiers in its pinned kernel source fails the build.

## Scope

In scope: `scripts/extract-kernel-source.ts`; the build manifest of extracted functions and hashes; the disclosure component; identifier-to-quantity bindings and colorization; the binding test used by the compiler; Rust extraction from the pinned FrankenSim revision.

Out of scope: the semantic color system itself (`am-design-semantic-color-8vbq`); equation components (`am-eq-colorized-component-1z8`); the compiler check wiring (`am-cm-checks-semantic-lic` consumes this bead's output).

## Requirements

### Extraction

- Each instrument manifest and derivation chain names its kernel functions: `{ language: "ts", module, exportName }` or `{ language: "rust", crate, path, fnName, revision }`.
- TypeScript extraction uses the TypeScript compiler API to locate the exported function by symbol and emit its exact source text (including JSDoc), not a regex slice.
- Rust extraction reads the pinned FrankenSim revision recorded in `docs/FRANKENSIM_BINDING.md` and locates the function with a Rust parser (or a documented robust token scan with tests), emitting exact source.
- For each extracted function record `sourceHash` (SHA-256 of normalized LF source), file path, line range, and revision. Output: `generated/kernel-sources.json` consumed by the build.
- If the source changes without the manifest's pinned hash being updated, the build fails with a message naming the instrument, function, old and new hash.

### Bindings and colorization

- The manifest declares identifier bindings `{ identifier: "gamma", quantityId: "lorentzFactor" }`. Colorization applies the role color of the quantity id from the semantic color system, with non-color identity (underline style or label on focus).
- **Binding test:** every live term of the instrument's equations (exact canonical quantity ids) must appear as an identifier binding present in the extracted source; a missing identifier fails the build.
- Hovering or focusing a colored identifier highlights the matching term in the equation and sentence on the page when present.

### Disclosure UI

- A "Show the code" disclosure beside the model note; static HTML with build-time syntax highlighting so it works without JavaScript; code blocks scroll locally, never the page; copy button optional.
- Header shows the function name, file, revision, source hash, and execution label context ("this is the function that produced the current snapshot" only when the accepted snapshot's owner matches).

**Added in review (retrofit and gate registration).** Instruments registered before this bead lands (the slice instruments BM-01, BM-05, and BM-06) receive their show-the-code disclosures and pinned source hashes in this bead, so no core instrument is left without one. This bead also registers the compiler rejection "an instrument's live terms do not appear as identifiers in its pinned kernel source" into `verify-content.ts`; `am-cm-checks-semantic-lic` deliberately does not own that check.

## Technical Approach

- Build step runs after content compilation and before the Next.js build; outputs are deterministic.
- Highlighting via a build-time highlighter with a restricted grammar set (TypeScript, Rust), producing sanitized HTML.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Extraction produces exact source text and stable hashes for TypeScript and Rust functions.
- [ ] A changed kernel without an updated pinned hash fails the build with a clear message.
- [ ] A missing identifier binding for a live term fails the build.
- [ ] The disclosure renders statically without JavaScript and highlights bound identifiers with role colors plus non-color identity.
- [ ] The header states the owner only when it matches the accepted snapshot's owner.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests

- `extractKernelSource.test.ts`: fixtures for exported functions, overloaded names, JSDoc retention, CRLF normalization, hash stability.
- `extractRustSource.test.ts`: fixture crate with nested modules and attributes.
- `kernelBinding.test.ts`: planted missing identifier fails; correct bindings pass.
- `showTheCode.test.tsx`: static rendering, sanitized HTML, owner-match header logic.

### End-to-end tests

- JavaScript-disabled lane: disclosure opens (native `details` element) and shows highlighted code.
- BM-01 lane: focusing `diffusion` identifier highlights the $D$ term in the equation card.

### Structured logging

JSONL with `suite`, `testId`, `beadId`, `instrumentId`, `function`, `sourceHash`, `revision`, `bindingCount`, `missingBindings`, `outcome`, `message`.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- Never show a function that did not produce the number and imply it did; the owner-match rule prevents that.
- Keep extraction deterministic so release manifests are reproducible.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-inst-registry-dispatcher-66l0` (manifests and owner bindings).
- `am-eq-colorized-component-1z8` (term colors and cross-highlighting hooks).

Unblocks:
- The compiler rule "instrument live terms appear as identifiers in the pinned kernel source" (`am-cm-checks-semantic-lic` uses this output) and every instrument's show-the-code requirement.

Added during graph review (blocked by):
- `am-cm-audit-scripts-d34`: the kernel-identifier check is registered into verify-content.ts, which that bead creates.

title: Adapt the Three.js studio for the few spatial instruments with disposal, context-loss handling, and fallbacks
description:
# Adapt the Three.js studio for the few spatial instruments with disposal, context-loss handling, and fallbacks

**Epic:** `am-ep-instruments-8gi` · **Batch:** batch-e · **Priority:** P2 · **Plan sections:** §2.3 (ThreeStudioScene), §10.9, §12.7, §12.8, §16.2, §16.4 (traceability only)

## Background

Three.js is a presentation tool, not a scientific authority. The plan permits it only where the mechanism is spatial and a 2D view genuinely loses information:

- the sphere measured as an ellipsoid with a clock (the SR-03 and SR-05 studio);
- field lines in two frames (SR-08);
- the 1906 photon-in-a-box extension (ME-03);
- an optional spacetime block view (later).

Everything else is SVG or Canvas. Rendering detail and model fidelity are independent settings: a richly rendered body can sit on top of a simple analytic ledger. The donor museum's `ThreeStudioScene.ts` supplies a proven studio pattern (lighting, camera presets, HUD chips) that this bead adapts to snapshot-driven, disposable, context-loss-safe scenes.

## Scope

In scope: `src/visuals/three/studio/` adapted from the donor with license notices; procedural geometry builders for the listed scenes' shared parts (ellipsoid from snapshot axes, clock faces, field-line tubes from sampled polylines, box and pulse markers); lifecycle and fallbacks; HUD integration with execution labels.

Out of scope: the per-scene instruments (`am-srk-sphere-clock-studio-lpxr`, `am-sre-field-lines-studio-4882`, `am-me-03-box-extension-kiei`, `am-later-deep-spacetime-block-7dai`); physics owners.

## Requirements

- **Snapshot-driven:** scenes read only accepted snapshot data (axes, clock readings, sampled field lines, positions); no physics in render loops; no `Math.random`.
- **Procedural geometry:** built from snapshot quantities; no marketplace model files; geometry builders are pure functions testable without WebGL.
- **Lazy and isolated:** loaded with dynamic import only when a spatial scene is requested; never in the initial reading route.
- **Lifecycle:** dispose geometries, materials, textures, render targets, controls, and listeners on unmount; reuse buffers across snapshot updates; pause rendering when invisible; limit concurrent WebGL contexts per page.
- **Context loss:** handle `webglcontextlost` by pausing the laboratory and showing the static 2D representation and text; on `webglcontextrestored` rebuild from the current snapshot without restarting the run or consuming randomness.
- **No-WebGL fallback:** the 2D view or static worked example with the same accessible descriptions and tables.
- **HUD:** execution label and model-note link as text; numeric readouts formatted from the snapshot; colorized terms consistent with equations.
- **Camera and presets:** named presets; camera motion is presentation only and never implies changed physics; axis scaling shown when relevant.
- **Reduced motion:** no auto-rotate or animated transitions; the posed scene reflects the current state.
- **Accessibility:** each scene has a textual description and an inspectable table of the displayed quantities, supplied through the graph-description framework.

## Technical Approach

Adapt the donor studio (scene setup, lights, camera presets, HUD chips) into a small factory `createStudio({ canvas, presets, onContextLost })` returning explicit `update(snapshot)` and `dispose()` methods. Direct Three.js (the donor declares `three`, not React Three Fiber).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Studio factory with update and dispose; geometry builders covered by unit tests without WebGL.
- [ ] 50 mount and unmount cycles show no growth in WebGL contexts, geometries, textures, or listeners.
- [ ] Simulated context loss pauses the lab and shows the 2D fallback; restoration rebuilds from the snapshot with the same run id.
- [ ] No-WebGL lane renders the fallback with descriptions and tables.
- [ ] The studio code is absent from the initial reading route bundle.
- [ ] Reduced motion disables automatic camera motion.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests

- `studioGeometry.test.ts`: ellipsoid axes from $R$ and $\beta$ ($R\sqrt{1-\beta^2}, R, R$), clock hand angles from readings, field-line tube construction from sampled points.
- `studioLifecycle.test.ts`: dispose counts using a WebGL mock-free renderer stub (headless context where available) and resource tracking.

### End-to-end tests

- Chromium and WebKit lanes: mount a fixture scene, force `WEBGL_lose_context`, assert pause and fallback, restore and assert identical run id; resource stress lane with repeated route changes; no-WebGL lane.

### Structured logging

JSONL with `suite`, `testId`, `beadId`, `scene`, `runId`, `snapshotVersion`, `webglContexts`, `geometries`, `textures`, `contextEvents`, `outcome`, `message`.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- Do not let the studio become a reason to build 3D scenes for 1D phenomena.
- Keep the donor license notice on adapted files.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-scaf-extract-ui-components-c31` (the extracted donor studio source).
- `am-rt-memory-lifecycle-5ws` (buffer ownership, visibility pausing, recovery rules).

Unblocks:
- `am-srk-sphere-clock-studio-lpxr`, `am-sre-field-lines-studio-4882`, `am-me-03-box-extension-kiei`, `am-later-deep-spacetime-block-7dai`.

Added during graph review (blocked by):
- `am-inst-execution-labels-5ywv`: the view shows the execution label and expandable model note.
- `am-a11y-graph-descriptions-vxe1`: views need three-layer textual descriptions and inspectable tables.
