description:
# Build the optional Three.js studio view of the 1906 photon-in-a-box extension

**Epic:** `am-ep-later-gap` · **Batch:** later · **Priority:** P3 · **Plan sections:** §8.4, §9.5, §10.9 (traceability only)

## Background

The plan lists the 1906 box as one of the few places where Three.js is justified: the mechanism is spatial (a box of mass $M$ and length $\ell$ recoils while a light pulse crosses it), and a 3D studio can make the recoil and the center-of-mass bookkeeping tangible. The box itself is required content: it is Journey IV's programmer side door and a per-paper definition-of-done item, delivered as a 2D instrument by `am-me-03-box-extension-kiei`. This bead keeps the 3D presentation from gating that required work. Three.js is a presentation tool, never a scientific authority, and rendering detail is independent of model fidelity: the physics stays the simple analytic ledger owned by the reference evaluator.

## Scope

In scope: a lazily loaded Three.js studio view of the box that reads the same accepted snapshot as the 2D view.

Out of scope (owned elsewhere): the box model, its idealizations, and its 2D instrument (`am-me-03-box-extension-kiei`); the studio framework (`am-inst-three-studio-y0y0`); any new physics.

## Requirements

1. **Same snapshot.** The 3D view consumes the accepted snapshot of the box instrument instance: the pulse position, the recoil speed $E/(Mc)$, the flight time $\ell/c$, the displacement $E\ell/(Mc^2)$, and the implied transported mass $E/c^2$. It never recomputes them.
2. **Procedural geometry.** A box, a light-packet marker, a recoil arrow, and a magnified-displacement gauge built procedurally. No marketplace model files. The pulse marker is labeled a teaching representation, not a picture of a photon.
3. **Labels.** "1906 extension" with Einstein's credit to Poincaré (1900) for the formal content, the execution label, and the expandable model note.
4. **Accessibility and fallbacks.** Keyboard-operable camera presets with visible focus; the textual description and inspectable table from the accessibility framework; reduced motion pauses animation and shows the posed state; without WebGL, the 2D view and table remain fully usable with an explanatory line.
5. **Lifecycle.** Switching between 2D and 3D never restarts the run or duplicates the owner. Materials, geometry, textures, subscriptions, and the render loop are disposed when the view unmounts. WebGL context loss pauses the view and keeps the book usable.
6. **Performance.** 60 Hz on capable desktops, a stable 30 Hz mobile tier. Under load reduce visual detail, never the physics.

## Technical Approach

- Build the scene with the studio framework from `am-inst-three-studio-y0y0`, loaded through a dynamic import only when the reader chooses the 3D view.
- Subscribe to the existing instrument instance's snapshot store; map snapshot fields to transforms each frame without React state churn.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The 3D view shows the same `snapshotVersion` and values as the 2D view for every tested state.
- [ ] Toggling 2D and 3D ten times leaves one owner, no new run id, and no growth in GPU contexts or listeners.
- [ ] Reduced motion, no-WebGL, and keyboard camera presets work as specified.
- [ ] Labels and credits appear as specified.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests
- A view-model test maps a fixed snapshot to transforms (box offset equals the snapshot displacement scaled by the declared magnification).
- A lifecycle test mounts and unmounts the view and asserts disposal calls.

### End-to-end tests
- Box lane at desktop: operate $E$, $M$, $\ell$ in 2D, switch to 3D, and assert identical readouts and snapshot ids; reduced-motion and no-WebGL variants; ten-toggle stress with context and listener counts.

### Structured logging
JSONL under `artifacts/test-logs/me-03-box-3d/` with `instanceId`, `runId`, `snapshotVersion`, `view`, `glContexts`, `listeners`, `fps`, `reducedMotion`, `webgl`, `outcome`.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- Never let visual richness imply a quantitative model of the box walls, stresses, or gravity; those are outside the ledger.
- Start only after `am-me-03-box-extension-kiei` is closed and the studio framework exists.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-me-03-box-extension-kiei`: the required 2D box instrument and its snapshot.
- `am-inst-three-studio-y0y0`: the Three.js studio framework with disposal and context-loss handling.

Unblocks: none (optional presentation).

title: Build the labeled 1906 photon-in-a-box extension
description:
# Build the labeled 1906 photon-in-a-box extension

**Epic:** `am-ep-mass-energy-siq` · **Batch:** batch-h · **Priority:** P1 · **Type:** feature · **Plan sections:** §8.4, §9.5 side door, §10.2 ME-03, §10.9, §22.1 (traceability only)

## Background

In 1906 Einstein gave a second argument for the inertia of energy ("Das Prinzip von der Erhaltung der Schwerpunktsbewegung und die Trägheit der Energie," Ann. Phys. (4) 20, 627), crediting Poincaré's 1900 paper for its formal content. A closed box emits a light pulse from one end that is absorbed at the other. The light carries momentum, so the box recoils; if the center of mass of a closed system cannot move on its own, a mass $E/c^2$ must have traveled with the light. This is Journey IV's side door for programmers: simulate the box and the shift appears. It is labeled 1906 everywhere and never presented as the 1905 argument.

## Scope

In scope: the box simulation, its idealizations, the center-of-mass bookkeeping, labels and credits, and the full instrument contract as a labeled extension of ME-03. A 2D view is required; a Three.js view is optional presentation through the studio.

Out of scope: the 1905 ledgers and boundaries (`am-me-01-two-ledgers-g1re`, `am-me-03-system-boundary-0arb`).

## Requirements

### Explanatory question and source links
"If a closed box sends light from one end to the other, what must travel with the light for the box's center of mass to stay put?" Linked to the 1906 paper (as a later Einstein argument), the mass–energy paper's conclusion, and margin record (c).

### Controls

| Control | Unit | Model domain | Default | Class |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Pulse energy $E$ | J | $E > 0$, $E/c^2 \ll M$ | 1 | setup-change |
| Box mass $M$ | kg | $M > 0$ | 1 | setup-change |
| Box length $\ell$ | m | $\ell > 0$ | 1 | setup-change |
| Mass assigned to light | none | $E/c^2$ or 0 (to show the paradox) | $E/c^2$ | setup-change |

### Derived outputs (typed statuses)
- Light momentum $E/c$; box recoil speed $E/(Mc)$ (`value`).
- Flight time $\ell/c$ (to first order in the small recoil) (`value`).
- Box displacement $-E\ell/(Mc^2)$ (`value`).
- Center-of-mass change: exactly 0 when mass $E/c^2$ moves with the light; nonzero when the light is assigned no mass, which contradicts the closed-system theorem (`value` with explanation).
- If $E/c^2$ is not small compared with $M$, the idealization is `outside-domain` with an explanation.

### Idealizations stated on the page
The rigid box transmits the recoil instantly (an idealization; real walls carry the impulse at finite sound speed); the box moves non-relativistically; the pulse is absorbed completely; no external forces. The 1906 credit to Poincaré 1900 is shown.

### Owner, views, action contract
Owner: a box function in `src/physics/reference/massEnergy.ts` (host calculation). Views: a 2D SVG box with the pulse, the recoil arrow, and a magnified displacement readout; an optional Three.js studio view, tracked separately by `am-me-03-box-3d-view-ln42` so it never gates this paper, reading the same snapshot. Nonvisual: type $E$, $M$, $\ell$; read a table of momentum, recoil speed, flight time, displacement, and center-of-mass change; toggle the light's assigned mass.

### `notModeled`
Wall elasticity and finite signal speed in the box, relativistic box motion, pulse spreading, partial absorption, gravity, and quantum effects.

### Predict, probes, tapes, code
Predict: "With the light assigned no mass, does the center of mass stay put?" Probe: the mass-assignment toggle. Teaching tape "the 1906 box." Show the code with pinned hashes.

## Technical Approach

Manifest mode `me-03:box-1906` with its own model identity; explicit dispatcher case; labels "1906 argument" and "credit: Poincaré 1900" on every view.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Outputs match the formulas; the center-of-mass change is exactly zero with mass $E/c^2$ assigned.
- [ ] The 1906 label and Poincaré credit appear on every view and caption.
- [ ] The 2D view works without WebGL; the 3D view, if present, reads the same snapshot.
- [ ] Full instrument contract including the nonvisual table route.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests
- $E = 1$ J, $\ell = 1$ m, $M = 1$ kg: recoil speed $3.33564\times10^{-9}$ m/s, time $3.33564\times10^{-9}$ s, displacement $1.11265\times10^{-17}$ m.
- Center-of-mass change symbolically zero with $E/c^2$ assigned (evaluated with extended precision or exact rational arithmetic to avoid round-off at $10^{-17}$ scales); nonzero without.
- `outside-domain` when $E/c^2$ is not small compared with $M$.

### End-to-end tests
Run the toggle, read the table, disable WebGL and confirm the 2D view, keyboard-only and 320 px.

### Structured logging
JSONL with `instrumentId: me-03:box-1906`, `E`, `M`, `l`, `recoilSpeed`, `displacement`, `comShift`, `lightMassAssigned`, `resultStatus`, `outcome`.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- Displacements near $10^{-17}$ m underflow naive floating-point bookkeeping of absolute positions; compute shifts relative to the initial position.
- Never merge this argument into the 1905 ledger.

## Dependencies

Blocked by: `am-me-03-system-boundary-0arb` (host instrument and labels).

Unblocks: none in the manifest; Journey IV's programmer side door uses it.

Unblocks: `am-dod-mass-energy-oxh2` (definition-of-done item 6: the box is Journey IV's programmer side door), `am-disc-journey-iv-chain-wwrz` (the side door is embedded in the journey), `am-me-03-box-3d-view-ln42` (optional 3D presentation).

title: Build ME-03 system-boundary energy ledger with cited energy-source cards
description:
# Build ME-03 system-boundary energy ledger with cited energy-source cards

**Epic:** `am-ep-mass-energy-siq` · **Batch:** batch-d · **Priority:** P1 · **Type:** feature · **Plan sections:** §7.6, §8.4, §9.5, §10.2, §13.2 (traceability only)

## Background

Most confusion about mass and energy is confusion about the system boundary. When a body emits light its mass falls, but the energy has not vanished: it travels with the radiation, and the combined isolated system neither gains nor loses total energy. ME-03 follows energy through three boundaries (the body alone, the emitted radiation, the combined isolated system) and checks the idea against the world with cited cards: radium, the Sun, coal, a candle. A modern extension, under a distinct model identity, introduces four-momentum and invariant mass, where two equal opposite pulses have nonzero invariant mass as a system despite massless constituents.

## Scope

In scope: the boundary ledger, internal transfer versus escape, cited energy-source cards with refusal when uncited, the heated sealed box example, the modern four-momentum mode, and the full instrument contract.

Out of scope: the 1906 photon-in-a-box extension (`am-me-03-box-extension-kiei`); the two ledgers (`am-me-01-two-ledgers-g1re`).

## Requirements

### Explanatory question and source links
"When energy leaves a body, which system loses mass, and which does not?" Linked to the paper's inertia-change and generalization blocks and to its conditional radium remark.

### Controls

| Control | Unit | Model domain | Default | Class |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| System boundary | none | body alone, radiation, combined isolated system | body alone | measurement-change (which system is described) |
| Energy retained or released | none | radiation escapes; radiation absorbed inside an enclosure | escapes | setup-change |
| Emitted energy $L$ | J or normalized | $L > 0$ | normalized 1 | setup-change |
| Energy-source card | none | radium-226 alpha decay, the Sun, burning coal, a candle, a 100 W bulb for a year | radium | setup-change |
| Mode | none | 1905 ledger, modern four-momentum (distinct model identity) | 1905 | setup-change |

### Derived outputs (typed statuses)
- Energy crossing each boundary and mass change of each system: body $-L$ and $-L/c^2$; radiation $+L$; combined isolated system $0$ (`value`).
- Internal transfer (radiation absorbed inside the enclosure) leaves the enclosure's total mass unchanged (`value`).
- **Cards** (each with a citation; computed by the owner from the cited value):
  - Radium-226 alpha decay releases about 4.87 MeV, so one mole loses about 5.2 mg in that single step.
  - The Sun radiates about $3.83\times10^{26}$ W, so it loses about $4.3\times10^{9}$ kg (about four million tonnes) every second.
  - Burning a kilogram of coal releases roughly 24–35 MJ, so the mass lost is about $(2.7\text{–}3.9)\times10^{-10}$ kg, a few tenths of a microgram. (Correction: the plan's "less than a nanogram" holds per gram, not per kilogram.)
  - A candle releasing about 80 W (cited value, stated as an assumption) loses about 3.2 ng of mass per hour through the energy it emits.
  - A 100 W bulb running for a year emits about $3.2\times10^{9}$ J, a mass of about 35 μg.
  - A card without a citation refuses with a typed reason.
- **Heated sealed box:** the example states how energy entered (for example a declared electrical input through leads) and what is inside; the mass increases by the added energy over $c^2$. It is an energy and inertia ledger, not a gravitational weighing experiment, and it adds no unmodeled external work or wall stresses.
- **Modern four-momentum mode** (labeled later formalism): invariant mass of a single pulse 0; of two collinear pulses 0; of two equal opposite pulses with total energy $L$, exactly $L/c^2$ (`value`).

### Assumptions and owner
Closed-system energy conservation; mass change of a system equals its energy change over $c^2$; cited energy values. Owner: `src/physics/reference/massEnergy.ts` (boundary ledger, card mass computation, invariant mass of pulse systems), host calculation until upstream adoption.

### Views and action contract (energy accounting family)
SVG diagram with draggable boundaries, energy arrows crossing them, a ledger table, and the card panel. Nonvisual: select the objects included in the system from a list, read energy crossing the boundary and the mass change in a table, choose a card and read its computation and citation.

### `notModeled`
Gravitational weighing, wall stresses or external work beyond declared inputs, nuclear and chemical mechanisms beyond cited energies, heat losses not declared, the practical measurability of tiny mass changes, and the 1905 argument's premises (inherited, not re-derived).

### Predict mode, probes, tapes, weave, code
- Predict: "A sealed box holds a lamp and a mirror. When the lamp turns on inside, does the box's total mass change?"
- Probes: move the boundary; release versus retain; switch to the four-momentum mode for two opposite pulses.
- Weave: the combined-system zero lights the conclusion sentence's scope note.
- Show the code: boundary ledger, card computation, invariant mass.

### Misconceptions addressed
"$E = mc^2$ is about nuclear bombs"; "mass converts into energy"; "a massless pulse cannot carry mass."

## Technical Approach

Manifest `content/experiments/me-03.yaml`; explicit dispatcher case; cards are data records with citations validated at build time; the four-momentum mode has its own model id and tape identity.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Boundary ledgers match: body $-L$, radiation $+L$, combined 0; internal transfer leaves total mass unchanged.
- [ ] Every card computes from a cited value; an uncited card refuses.
- [ ] The coal card uses the corrected magnitude.
- [ ] The four-momentum mode is labeled later formalism with a distinct model identity.
- [ ] Full instrument contract, including nonvisual boundary selection and a JavaScript-disabled worked example.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests
- Cards: radium $4.871\,\text{MeV}/931.494\,\text{MeV u}^{-1}$ per decay gives $5.23$ mg per mole; Sun $3.828\times10^{26}$ W gives $4.259\times10^{9}$ kg/s; coal 24 MJ gives $2.670\times10^{-10}$ kg and 35 MJ gives $3.894\times10^{-10}$ kg; candle 80 W for 3600 s gives $3.20$ ng; bulb 100 W for one year gives $35.1$ μg (tolerances $10^{-3}$ relative).
- Invariant masses: single pulse 0; two collinear 0; two opposite with total energy $L$ gives $L/c^2$ within $10^{-12}$.
- An uncited card fixture is refused with the typed code.
- Noncircularity: no body energy is initialized with $Mc^2$ in 1905 mode.

### End-to-end tests
Select each boundary by keyboard and read the ledger; run the sealed-box prediction; switch cards and confirm citations display; switch to four-momentum mode; 320 px, reduced motion, permalink round trip.

### Structured logging
JSONL with `instrumentId: me-03`, `boundary`, `mode`, `card`, `citationPresent`, `energy`, `massChange`, `resultStatus`, `expected`, `actual`, `tolerance`, `outcome`.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- Do not imply an isolated system loses mass when energy merely moves inside it.
- Keep the box example free of unmodeled work.

## Dependencies

Blocked by: `am-ref-mass-energy-ht0` (ledger and card functions), `am-bm-slice-retrospective-pp09` (frozen platform).

Unblocks: `am-me-03-box-extension-kiei`, `am-me-e2e-qbbm`, `am-disc-journey-iv-chain-wwrz` (check against the world).

Added during graph review (blocked by):
- `am-inst-show-the-code-4brv`: the instrument contract requires a show-the-code disclosure pinned to the kernel source.
- `am-inst-predict-mode-ti7m`: the instrument contract requires predict mode or a recorded exemption.
- `am-inst-permalink-tape-s677`: the instrument contract requires bounded ?tape= permalinks.

# Write the continuous browser acceptance journey for the mass-energy paper

**Epic:** `am-ep-mass-energy-siq` · **Batch:** batch-d · **Priority:** P1 · **Labels:** testing, e2e · **Plan sections:** §8.4, §12.6, §17.4, §17.7 item 9, §18.3 smoke test (traceability only)

## Background

The mass–energy paper is the first complete paper, so its browser suite is the first proof that the complete-paper contract holds end to end. It is also the page the release workflow uses for its post-promotion smoke test, because it is quick. This suite enters through a deep source passage, uses every face including the interlinear gloss, opens a foundation, operates all three instruments, verifies observer changes preserve the world and that no ledger bakes in the answer, and runs every lane with structured logs.

## Scope

In scope: the `mass-energy` suite, its lanes, and a `smoke` subset reusable by the release workflow.

Out of scope: the harness (`am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh`); the release smoke-test wiring (`am-rel-smoke-rollback-cache-phre`).

## Requirements

### Continuous journey
1. Deep link to the conclusion sentence on the English face.
2. Switch to German, parallel, and gloss faces; the same sentence stays focused; the gloss shows word-level English under the German.
3. Open the foundation for the binomial series $(1 - x)^{-1/2}$ used in the low-speed expansion; return to the exact step.
4. ME-01: type $\phi = 60^\circ$ and read pulses $0.4375L$ and $0.8125L$ with sum $1.25L$; change observer speed to 0.3 and confirm `runId` and event ids are unchanged (observer change); step the subtraction by keyboard; relax the premise and see `underdetermined`.
5. ME-02: type 0.6 and read $0.25L$, $0.18L$, proxy $1.388889\,L/c^2$; approach zero on the logarithmic axis; type 0 and see the `analytic-limit` $L/c^2$.
6. ME-03: select the combined system and read zero net energy change; open the coal card and confirm the corrected magnitude and citation; switch to four-momentum mode and read invariant mass $L/c^2$ for two opposite pulses.
7. Select the colorized $L$ term and confirm highlighting across views; return to the conclusion sentence.

### Contracts and invariants
Direct numeric entry and out-of-domain refusals ($\lvert\beta\rvert \ge 1$); permalink round trips; uncited card refusal fixture; the first encounter by pointer, keyboard, and table; noncircularity: inspect snapshots and DOM to confirm no 1905-mode ledger contains a numeric absolute body energy or $Mc^2$.

### Smoke subset
Tag steps 1, 2 (German face), and 5 as `smoke`: fast, deterministic, and runnable against a deployed URL.

### Lanes, evidence, logs
Desktop, tablet, 320 px touch, WebKit, keyboard-only, reduced motion, high zoom, no-WebGL, JavaScript disabled (full paper text with static MathML), print. JSONL at `artifacts/test-logs/mass-energy/<run-id>.jsonl` with the standard fields; screenshots, traces, DOM snapshots, console logs, and snapshot JSON on failure; the canary proves the failure path.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The journey passes in every applicable lane.
- [ ] Contracts, invariants, and the noncircularity inspection pass.
- [ ] The `smoke` subset runs against a deployed URL within a recorded time budget.
- [ ] Logs and failure evidence are produced; the suite runs in CI.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests
Helpers for snapshot identity comparison, ledger inspection, and the smoke-tag runner.

### End-to-end tests
The suite as specified.

### Structured logging
As specified, with per-lane summaries and a separate summary for the smoke subset.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- Keep the smoke subset free of statistical or timing-sensitive checks.
- The gloss face must be exercised, since it is part of this batch's contract.

## Dependencies

Blocked by: `am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh` (harness), `am-me-01-two-ledgers-g1re`, `am-me-02-coefficient-dtmi`, `am-me-03-system-boundary-0arb` (instruments), `am-me-readings-69bo` (content), `am-read-gloss-face-lp2` (gloss face).

Unblocks: `am-dod-mass-energy-oxh2` (definition-of-done item 9).

title: Author equation records and the two-ledger derivation chain with the imported relativity result
description:
# Author equation records and the two-ledger derivation chain with the imported relativity result

**Epic:** `am-ep-mass-energy-siq` · **Batch:** batch-d · **Priority:** P1 · **Plan sections:** §3.6, §6.5, §8.4, §11.4–11.6, §15.6 (traceability only)

## Background

The mass–energy argument is a short chain, which makes every premise and every import visible if the records are exact and invisible if they are not. Its single input from outside the paper is the relativity paper's §8 transformation of light energy, admitted with provenance so Batch D need not wait for the relativity epics. Its central move is a subtraction that removes unknown internal energies; its conclusion rests on a stated premise about an unchanged additive constant and on the Newtonian form of kinetic energy at second order. The records must make the import an explicit cross-paper edge, keep absolute body energies symbolic, and mark the approximation with its order and error.

## Scope

In scope: `Equation` records for every displayed and substantive inline equation in the paper (anchors under `s0`); the two-ledger chain; the cross-paper import edge; spoken forms; bindings; dimension checks.

Out of scope: the relativity §8 records themselves (`am-sre-equations-2g3h`); the instruments (`am-me-01-two-ledgers-g1re`, `am-me-02-coefficient-dtmi`, `am-me-03-system-boundary-0arb`); concordance entries (`am-not-entries-mass-energy-wq2`).

## Requirements

### Records (verify the printed set, labels, and notation against the inventory and facsimile)
1. **Imported transformation (from paper 3 §8):** $E'/E = \beta\left(1 - \frac{v}{V}\cos\varphi\right)$ with Einstein's $\beta = (1 - v^2/V^2)^{-1/2}$ (modern $\gamma$). The record's provenance names the relativity paper's §8 anchor from `am-edn-inventory-relativity-0u9`.
2. **Rest-frame balance:** $E_0 = E_1 + \tfrac12L + \tfrac12L$, i.e. $E_0 - E_1 = L$.
3. **Moving-frame pulse energies:** $\tfrac12L\beta(1 - \frac{v}{V}\cos\varphi)$ and $\tfrac12L\beta(1 + \frac{v}{V}\cos\varphi)$; modern $\frac{L}{2}\gamma(1 \mp \beta\cos\phi)$ with modern $\beta = v/c$.
4. **Moving-frame balance:** $H_0 = H_1 + L\beta$ (angle-independent sum), i.e. $H_0 - H_1 = L\beta$.
5. **The subtraction:** $(H_0 - E_0) - (H_1 - E_1) = L(\beta - 1)$.
6. **The premise:** $H - E = K + C$ with the same additive constant $C$ before and after emission; hence $K_0 - K_1 = L(\beta - 1)$.
7. **The expansion:** $K_0 - K_1 = L(\beta - 1) = \tfrac12\frac{L}{V^2}v^2 + \dots$ with the next term $\tfrac38\frac{L}{V^4}v^4$ shown as the leading neglected term.
8. **The conclusion:** comparison with $\tfrac12mv^2$ gives a mass decrease of $L/V^2$; the general statement that the mass of a body is a measure of its energy content.

Each record carries its tree, printed and modern forms generated from the tree, term and operation ids (the angle factor, the sum that cancels $\cos\varphi$, each subtraction, the premise substitution, the expansion order), canonical bindings (`emittedEnergyRestFrame`, `bodyEnergyRestBefore`, `bodyEnergyRestAfter`, `bodyEnergyMovingBefore`, `bodyEnergyMovingAfter`, `kineticEnergyBefore`, `kineticEnergyAfter`, `additiveConstant`, `observerSpeed`, `lorentzFactor`, `emissionAngle`, `speedOfLight`, `inertialMassDecrease`), the printed number or label, an authored spoken form, R0–R3 readings, and a passing rational dimension check.

**Statuses:** $E_0, E_1, H_0, H_1$, and $C$ are `symbolic` in every record on the historical route; only differences carry values.

### The chain (historical route)
Import (cross-paper historical edge to paper 3 §8, an admitted 1905 result with provenance) → symmetric emission in the rest frame → moving-frame pulse energies → **sum removes the angle** → two balances → **the subtraction removes the unknown body energies (the move)** → premise node (unchanged additive constant; Newtonian kinetic energy at second order) → identification with kinetic-energy difference → expansion to second order with the error term → coefficient → mass decrease $L/V^2$ → generalization (a broader inference node, labeled).

**Edges kept distinct:** the four-momentum invariant-mass check is a **modern verification oracle**, never a premise; initializing any body energy with $Mc^2$ or $\gamma Mc^2$ is forbidden on this route (the compiler's circularity check must catch it).

## Technical Approach

Author under `content/equations/mass-energy/` in the frozen formats; bind notation through the mass–energy concordance ($L$ is energy here, $V$ is light speed, $\beta$ is the modern $\gamma$); the import edge references the relativity block id even before the relativity readings exist.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every displayed equation has a complete record; absolute energies are symbolic.
- [ ] The chain is acyclic with the import, the move, the premise, and the expansion order marked.
- [ ] The oracle edge is typed and never used as a premise; the circularity check passes.
- [ ] English and German equation blocks are byte-identical.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests
- Schema, symbol, and quantity-id validation; dimension checks (energy, speed, mass).
- Numeric spot checks: at $v = 0.6c$ the pulse sum equals $1.25L$ for $\varphi = 0, 60^\circ, 90^\circ, 2$ rad within $10^{-12}$; the subtraction gives $0.25L$; the second-order term gives $0.18L$ and the fourth-order term $0.0486L$ (the partial sums approach the exact value).
- Circularity test: a fixture chain that initializes $E_0 = Mc^2$ is rejected by the compiler.
- Import-edge test: removing the relativity anchor makes the compiler fail with an actionable message.

### End-to-end tests
From the conclusion sentence, open the chain, select the subtraction, open the premise node, and return; toggle modern notation and confirm $\beta \to \gamma$, $V \to c$, $L \to E$ from trees.

### Structured logging
JSONL with `equationId`, `chainId`, `stepIndex`, `rule`, `edgeType`, `expected`, `actual`, `tolerance`, `outcome`.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- Einstein's $\beta$ is the modern $\gamma$; call it out in red on first use through the concordance.
- The generalization is an inference beyond the radiation argument, not a derived identity.

## Dependencies

# Build the no-algebra first encounter: two accounting sheets and one subtraction

**Epic:** `am-ep-mass-energy-siq` · **Batch:** batch-d · **Priority:** P1 · **Plan sections:** §1.8, §7.2, §8.4 "teach the coefficient before the slogan" (traceability only)

## Background

The mass–energy paper's key move is an accounting trick: two ledgers share unknown entries, and subtracting one from the other removes what you cannot know. That move needs no algebra. The first encounter presents two before-and-after accounting sheets in words and small numbers, with the unknown internal quantities as covered boxes, lets the reader subtract, and shows that the covered details are not needed. Only afterward come the frame transformation and the small-speed coefficient. The trap to avoid: putting $Mc^2$ inside a covered box and pretending the comparison discovered it.

## Scope

In scope: the authored sheets, the subtraction interaction, the bridge to the radiation transformation and the coefficient, the nonvisual equivalent, and the links to ME-01 and the source.

Out of scope: the instruments (`am-me-01-two-ledgers-g1re`, `am-me-02-coefficient-dtmi`); the readings (`am-me-readings-69bo`).

## Requirements

### Authored sheets (not measured data; the page says so)
- **Sheet A, the body's own view.** Before: covered box "energy inside." After: the same covered box, minus 10 units of light sent out (5 units each way).
- **Sheet B, a traveler passing by.** Before: covered box "energy inside" plus a line "energy of motion (before)." After: the covered box, minus the light as the traveler measures it (12.5 units in total, because the traveler sees one pulse carry more and the other less, and the sum comes out larger), plus "energy of motion (after)."
- The body stays at rest in its own view, so the traveler sees the same speed before and after.

### The interaction
1. Ask whether we can find out how much energy is inside. (We cannot: the boxes stay covered.)
2. Subtract Sheet A from Sheet B line by line. The covered boxes cancel.
3. What remains: the energy of motion dropped by 2.5 units (12.5 − 10) while the speed stayed the same.
4. Ask what must have changed if a moving thing has less energy of motion at the same speed. The thing is now easier to set in motion: its inertia fell.
5. State the premise plainly: the covered boxes hold the same unknown in both sheets apart from the motion line; the 1905 paper asserts this.
6. Offer the next steps: the traveler's 12.5 comes from the radiation transformation (`am-me-01-two-ledgers-g1re`); the relation between the 2.5 units, the speed, and inertia is the small-speed coefficient (`am-me-02-coefficient-dtmi`); and the original passage.

The numbers correspond to a traveler at $0.6c$ ($\gamma = 1.25$, $L = 10$ units, $L(\gamma - 1) = 2.5$); the entrance does not say so until the bridge.

### Equivalence across interfaces
Dragging a "subtract" bar between sheets, keyboard subtraction line by line, and a screen-reader table of both sheets with a difference column manipulate the same entries and expose the same totals. The JavaScript-disabled route presents both sheets and the worked subtraction as static content.

### Trap
No covered box ever contains $Mc^2$, $\gamma Mc^2$, or any number implying absolute rest energy.

## Technical Approach

Author as content records with anchor `#entry-mass-energy`, rendered through the reader's passage actions; arithmetic asserted by tests; links use stable anchors.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Both sheets, the six steps, the premise statement, and the bridge appear as specified.
- [ ] The page labels the numbers as authored.
- [ ] Pointer, keyboard, table, and no-JavaScript routes give identical totals.
- [ ] No covered box contains an absolute rest energy.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests
Arithmetic: $12.5 - 10 = 2.5$; consistency with ME scenario ($L = 10$, $\gamma = 1.25$, $L(\gamma-1) = 2.5$); a content check that no covered-box value is numeric; voice lint.

### End-to-end tests
Complete the subtraction by pointer, keyboard, and table; follow the bridge to ME-01 and back; JavaScript-disabled lane; 320 px.

### Structured logging
JSONL with `anchor`, `interface`, `totals`, `expected`, `actual`, `outcome`.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- Keep "energy of motion" in words; "kinetic energy" appears only after the bridge.
- Do not say mass "turns into" light.

## Dependencies

Blocked by: `am-me-readings-69bo` (destination passages), `am-read-passage-actions-vbe` (host actions).

Unblocks: `am-dod-mass-energy-oxh2`, `am-tour-15min-mass-energy-nqz1`.

# Author the required historian's-margin records for the mass-energy paper

**Epic:** `am-ep-mass-energy-siq` · **Batch:** batch-d · **Priority:** P1 · **Plan sections:** §3.6 editorial boundary, §3.9, §11.2 EditorialNote, §17.7 item 7, §22.1 (traceability only)

## Background

The short paper attracts the most myths, so its margin must be precise. The required entries are typed `EditorialNote` records with primary sources, and the paper is not done until they are present. They carry what was actually written by Einstein, Poincaré, Hasenöhrl, Ives, Stachel and Torretti, Cockcroft and Walton, and Bainbridge, and they keep later formal explanations labeled as later.

## Scope

In scope: the six required records and the editorial-boundary note on Einstein's later derivations.

Out of scope: R3 prose in readings (`am-me-readings-69bo`); timeline cards (`am-disc-timeline-xzef`).

## Requirements

### Required entries
- **(a)** $E = mc^2$ does not appear in the 1905 paper; the paper says the mass diminishes by $L/V^2$. The familiar form belongs to 1907 and later writings (locate and cite the first appearance used by the site, for example Einstein's 1907 review in the *Jahrbuch der Radioaktivität und Elektronik*, after checking it).
- **(b)** The additive constant and the Newtonian kinetic-energy premise: H. E. Ives, *J. Opt. Soc. Am.* 42, 540 (1952), called the argument circular; J. Stachel and R. Torretti, *Am. J. Phys.* 50, 760 (1982), answered. Present both positions from what they wrote.
- **(c)** Einstein's 1906 center-of-mass paper, *Ann. Phys.* (4) 20, 627, credits Poincaré 1900 (*Archives néerlandaises* 5, 252) for the formal content of the argument.
- **(d)** Hasenöhrl 1904–1905 (radiation in a moving cavity adding to its mass, with a factor he later corrected) and later priority claims, each stated from what was actually written; verify the Annalen citations before publication.
- **(e)** The radium proposal and the first quantitative nuclear checks: J. D. Cockcroft and E. T. S. Walton, *Proc. R. Soc. A* 137, 229 (1932); K. T. Bainbridge, *Phys. Rev.* 44, 123 (1933).
- **(f)** Two equal opposite light pulses have nonzero invariant mass as a system: a later formal explanation that resolves a common confusion and is not a hidden premise of 1905.

### Editorial-boundary note
Einstein's later derivations (1906; 1907; 1935; 1946) listed with citations after verification, framed as later work that neither replaces nor invalidates the 1905 argument's scope and premises.

### Record fields
Author, claim, source support (full citation; a short attributed phrase at most), kind (historian's margin, dispute, correction, side note), affected `s0` block ids, review state, verification status (checked by whom, when), and which of the four historical statements the record concerns.

## Technical Approach

Author records under `content/annotations/mass-energy/`; register citations in the bibliography; render at R3 anchors and on results cards.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Six required records and the boundary note exist with complete fields.
- [ ] Every citation verified against its source and the check recorded.
- [ ] Priority entries state what each author wrote, without verdicts the sources do not support.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests
Required-entry audit; citation resolution; date-order checks (1900, 1904–1905, 1905, 1906, 1932–1933, 1952, 1982); voice lint.

### End-to-end tests
R3 at the subtraction and coefficient anchors renders (b), (c), and (f) with citations; the JavaScript-disabled lane shows them.

### Structured logging
JSONL with `noteId`, `kind`, `anchor`, `citationResolved`, `verificationStatus`, `outcome`.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- Do not adjudicate priority beyond the record; present it.
- Keep the invariant-mass explanation explicitly labeled as later formalism.

## Dependencies

Blocked by: `am-me-readings-69bo` (the R3 anchors).

Unblocks: `am-dod-mass-energy-oxh2` (definition-of-done item 7).

# Author the mass-energy misconception ledger

**Epic:** `am-ep-mass-energy-siq` · **Batch:** batch-d · **Priority:** P1 · **Plan sections:** §7.6, §8.4, §13.5, §17.7 item 4 (traceability only)

## Background

No result carries more misconceptions than the one people write as $E = mc^2$. Each paper's typed ledger is surfaced inline as "common wrong turn" callouts and collected on the results face; the compiler rejects fewer than five entries.

## Scope

In scope: the ledger entries, anchors, instruments, sources, and readings.

Out of scope: the callout UI (`am-read-misconception-callouts-a3o`).

## Requirements

### Entries
1. **"$E = mc^2$ is about nuclear bombs."** What is true: the argument concerns any body that radiates; a candle flame loses mass. Instrument: ME-03 energy-source cards (radium, Sun, coal, candle). Anchor: the generalization and radium remark.
2. **"Mass converts into energy."** What is true: the mass of a closed system is conserved; the body's rest mass falls because energy left it. Instrument: ME-03 system boundaries. Anchor: the inertia-change sentence.
3. **"The formula is in the paper."** What is true: it is not; the paper says the mass diminishes by $L/V^2$, and the familiar form belongs to 1907 and later. Instrument: results card and margin record (a). Anchor: the conclusion.
4. **"Einstein was first."** What is true: the site presents the record: Poincaré's 1900 "fictitious fluid" of mass $E/c^2$, Hasenöhrl 1904–1905 on cavity radiation, and Einstein's 1906 credit to Poincaré, each from what was written. Instrument: margin records (c) and (d). Anchor: the conclusion.
5. **"A massless pulse cannot carry mass."** What is true: two equal opposite pulses have nonzero invariant mass as a system (a later formal explanation). Instrument: ME-03 four-momentum extension. Anchor: the two-emission block.
6. **"The low-speed proxy is the exact mass loss at every speed."** What is true: $2L(\gamma-1)/v^2$ equals $L/c^2$ only in the limit; at $0.6c$ it is about $1.389\,L/c^2$. Instrument: ME-02 three-output view and its adversarial fixture. Anchor: the low-speed expansion.

### Fields per entry
Tempting claim in people's words; why tempting; what is true at R0–R3; instrument id and mode; anchors; sources. Numbers trace to scenario ids or citations.

## Technical Approach

Author `Misconception` records under `content/misconceptions/mass-energy/`, linked to results cards and instruments.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Six entries with all fields; the five-entry minimum passes.
- [ ] Instruments and anchors resolve; numbers trace.

## Test Plan

`audit-misconceptions`; numeric-trace; voice lint; the adversarial fixture for entry 6 exists and passes.

### End-to-end tests
Callouts render inline and on the results face; instrument links open the named modes; JavaScript-disabled lane.

### Structured logging
JSONL with `misconceptionId`, `anchor`, `instrumentId`, `outcome`.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- Present the priority entry as a record, not a verdict.
- Avoid implying nuclear processes are special; the relation is general.

Unblocks: `am-dod-mass-energy-oxh2` (definition-of-done item 4).

description:
# Author R0-R3 readings for every argument block of the mass-energy paper

**Epic:** `am-ep-mass-energy-siq` · **Batch:** batch-d · **Priority:** P1 · **Plan sections:** §3.6, §6.2, §6.5, §6.6, §8.4, §9.5 (traceability only)

## Background

The mass–energy paper is three printed pages with no sections. Its brevity makes exhaustive treatment feasible and makes a missing premise easy to hide. The readings must carry the argument exactly as it is: an imported light-energy transformation, a symmetric emission chosen to remove recoil, two energy ledgers, one subtraction that removes unknown internal energies, a stated premise about an unchanged additive constant, and a low-speed coefficient. They must teach the coefficient before the slogan and never pretend the formula $E = mc^2$ appears in the paper. The site neither presents the 1905 argument as the last word nor as wrong; it teaches the difference between a productive physical argument and a theorem with fully specified hypotheses.

## Scope

In scope: R0–R3 for every paragraph and displayed equation of the paper (paper 4 anchors use `s0`), captions for ME-01, ME-02, ME-03, authoring contracts, and R3 texts attached to these anchors.

Out of scope: typed margin records (`am-me-margin-entries-kfg5`); equation records (`am-me-equations-0mgx`); the gloss (`am-edn-gloss-mass-energy-g0y`); the no-algebra entrance (`am-me-first-encounter-kejt`).

## Requirements

### Treatment map (argument blocks)

| Argument block | Required treatment | Results and checks |
|---|---|---|
| Imported result from paper 3 | Trace the radiation-energy transformation to §8 of the relativity paper; never use the desired mass–energy result as an input | $E'/E = \beta(1 - \frac{v}{V}\cos\varphi)$ (Einstein's $\beta$ is the modern $\gamma$) |
| Two equal opposite emissions | Explain the choice of symmetry and why the body remains at rest in its original frame | $\tfrac12 L$ each way |
| Energy balances in two frames | Track all before and after quantities with separate frame and event identifiers; the sum of the two transformed pulse energies is $L\beta$ for any emission angle | $E_0 - E_1 = L$; $H_0 - H_1 = L\beta$ |
| Subtraction and kinetic energy | Show the cancellation, the role of additive energy constants, and the identification of the kinetic-energy difference as a stated premise of the source | $K_0 - K_1 = L(\beta - 1)$ |
| Low-speed expansion | Derive the quadratic term and expose the approximation error rather than substituting an unexplained series | $L(\beta - 1) = \tfrac12\frac{L}{V^2}v^2 + \dots$ |
| Inertia change and generalization | Separate the specific radiation argument, the broader inference, and the later modern formulation | The mass diminishes by $L/V^2$; "the mass of a body is a measure of its energy content" |
| Empirical closing remark | Preserve the conditional suggestion (radium salts) without a nuclear-history digression | As printed |
| Date-line | | "Bern, September 1905" |

### Content every reading carries at its resolution
- **Why the symmetric emission is clever:** in the body's own frame it removes recoil from the bookkeeping and isolates an energy change. Do not begin by saying each pulse is "mass converted to energy"; the argument investigates the relation.
- **Two ledgers, four body-energy quantities:** $L$ is the total emitted energy in the rest frame; $E_0, E_1$ the body's energies before and after in that frame; $H_0, H_1$ in a frame moving at $v$. The pulses carry $\frac{L}{2}\gamma(1 - \beta\cos\phi)$ and $\frac{L}{2}\gamma(1 + \beta\cos\phi)$ in the moving frame; their sum is $\gamma L$ for any emission angle (modern $\beta = v/c$).
- **The subtraction:** $(H_0 - E_0) - (H_1 - E_1) = L(\gamma - 1)$. Each cancellation is a selectable operation in ME-01.
- **The premise:** each frame-energy difference equals kinetic energy plus the same additive constant before and after emission. The source asserts that unchanged constant; the cancellation is not an independent derivation of the assertion. The argument also relies on the Newtonian form of kinetic energy at second order.
- **The coefficient:** $K_0 - K_1 = L(\gamma-1) \approx \tfrac12\frac{L}{c^2}v^2$. At $v = 0.6c$ the exact difference is $0.25L$ and the quadratic approximation $0.18L$; that discrepancy makes the approximation's domain visible. The finite-speed proxy $2L(\gamma-1)/v^2$ is not the limiting coefficient; it exceeds $L/c^2$ by about $\tfrac34(v/c)^2$ at small speed. Distinguish the positive mass lost $M_{\text{before}} - M_{\text{after}} = L/c^2$ from the signed change $\Delta M = -L/c^2$.
- **The generalization** is a broader inference beyond the specific radiation argument; the modern formulation (four-momentum, invariant mass) is a later development and labeled so.
- **The radium remark** stays conditional as printed.
- **Notation:** printed symbols by default ($L$ emitted energy, $V$ light speed, $\beta$ the modern $\gamma$, $E_0, E_1, H_0, H_1$, $K$ kinetic energy, $C$ additive constant), with the modern toggle generated from equation trees.
- **Teach the coefficient before the slogan**, and close by naming the techniques this paper shares with the other three: infer hidden structure from constraints; choose observables that survive complexity; examine operational definitions; compare the same process in two descriptions; exploit symmetry to cancel what you do not need to know. Link to the essays; do not claim a finished unified theory.

### R3 texts attached to these anchors
$E = mc^2$ does not appear (the familiar form belongs to 1907 and later writings); the additive-constant and Newtonian kinetic-energy premises, with Ives's 1952 charge of circularity and Stachel and Torretti's 1982 reply; Einstein's later derivations (the 1906 center-of-mass argument, which credits Poincaré 1900 for the formal content; 1907; 1935; 1946); Hasenöhrl 1904–1905 with what he wrote; the first quantitative nuclear checks (Cockcroft and Walton 1932; Bainbridge 1933); two opposite pulses have nonzero invariant mass as a system (a later formal explanation, not a hidden premise). Verify every citation against its source before publication.

### Four readings, tests, contracts
R0–R3 rules and tests (R0 no-physics claim test; R2 physician test); the six-question minimum explanation unit; the authoring contract. No reading places $Mc^2$ or $\gamma Mc^2$ inside a ledger as an input on the historical route.

## Technical Approach

Use the frozen reading format; attach to `s0` block ids; numeric literals trace to printed values, citations, or ME scenario ids; weave predicates: the angle-independent sum lights the "for any emission angle" sentence; the stabilized coefficient lights the "mass diminishes by $L/V^2$" sentence.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every block of the paper has R0–R3; ME-01, ME-02, ME-03 captions have all four.
- [ ] The additive-constant premise and the Newtonian kinetic-energy premise are explicit at R1, R2, and R3.
- [ ] The exact, quadratic, proxy, and limit outputs are distinguished at R1 and R2.
- [ ] No reading claims the paper contains $E = mc^2$ or initializes a ledger with $Mc^2$.
- [ ] Numeric literals trace to sources or scenario ids; R3 citations are verified.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests
`audit-readings` over `s0` blocks; schema validation; numeric-trace test; voice lint; a noncircularity text check that flags any reading on the historical route referencing $Mc^2$ as an input without the modern-lens label.

### End-to-end tests
JavaScript-disabled R1 rendering of the paper; `?detail=2` permalink; parallel face with the gloss; reading-face budget.

### Structured logging
JSONL with `suite`, `testId`, `beadId`, `paper: mass-energy`, `anchor`, `detail`, `expected`, `actual`, `outcome`.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- Neither pretend the argument is the last word nor that it is wrong.
- "Mass converts into energy" is a misconception; the readings speak of energy leaving the body and the body's mass falling.

## Dependencies

Blocked by: `am-edn-translation-mass-energy-f3b` (aligned translation), `am-bm-slice-retrospective-pp09` (frozen reading format).

Unblocks: `am-me-margin-entries-kfg5`, `am-me-first-encounter-kejt`, `am-me-misconceptions-tr18`, `am-me-e2e-qbbm`, `am-me-review-physics-1t2l`, `am-me-review-reader-l6iy`, `am-disc-connections-page-vhm7`.

Added during graph review (blocked by):
- `am-found-fields-light-cv3o`: these readings link that foundation cluster's lessons, which must exist for links to resolve.
- `am-found-transport-thermo-smv3`: these readings link that foundation cluster's lessons, which must exist for links to resolve.

1. **Imported light-energy transformation** $E'/E = \beta(1 - \frac{v}{V}\cos\varphi)$, with provenance to the relativity paper's §8. Probe: ME-01 pulse energies.
2. **Symmetric emission:** $\tfrac12L$ each way; why it removes recoil. Probe: ME-01 at $v = 0$.

A three-page argument hides premises easily, and the paper's reception includes a published charge of circularity (Ives 1952) and a published reply (Stachel and Torretti 1982). A qualified reviewer checks the whole argument, the instruments, the cards, and the modern extensions, and records acceptance in the provenance receipt. The short paper gets the same seriousness as the long ones.

## Scope

In scope: review of the readings, equation records and chain, ME-01, ME-02, ME-03 (and the 1906 box extension if built), cards, misconceptions, results cards, and margin physics claims for the mass–energy paper.

# Non-physicist R2 readability review and fifteen-minute tour test for mass-energy

**Epic:** `am-ep-mass-energy-siq` · **Batch:** batch-d · **Priority:** P1 · **Labels:** human-gate · **Plan sections:** §6.2, §7.3, §17.2, §17.5, §17.7 items 8–9 (traceability only)

For the mass–energy paper both tests matter especially: the popular slogan is familiar, and the actual claim is narrower and more interesting.

## Scope

In scope: the R2 readability review of the whole paper and its instrument captions; the fifteen-minute tour test; fixes for findings.

Out of scope: physics correctness (`am-me-review-physics-1t2l`); German fidelity (`am-edn-review-german-mass-energy-w3y`); the tour's authoring (`am-tour-15min-mass-energy-nqz1`).

## Requirements

### R2 readability review
A reviewer without physics training beyond high school reads every R2 text and ME-01, ME-02, ME-03 caption; records per passage whether it was followable and any stumbling point (undefined symbol, omitted inference, misleading visual cue, inaccessible control, too much at once) with the block id; every finding becomes a revision (with R0, R1, R3 reread) or a recorded reason.

### Fifteen-minute tour test
A separate reader with no physics background completes the tour (first encounter, R0 readings of the key passages, instruments in predict mode, the R0 line of the move) without equations and states the claim in one sentence. The facilitator records the sentence and whether it captures the claim: a body that gives off energy as light becomes less massive by that energy divided by the square of the speed of light, shown here for light emission under stated premises. Participation is voluntary, accessible, and compensated where feasible; no diagnosis or score is collected.

## Human Gate

- **Who qualifies:** a non-physicist R2 reviewer; a separate tour participant with no physics background; a named facilitator; never an agent.
- **Evidence to record:** names and roles, dates, participant code, reviewed block ids, findings and resolutions, the participant's one-sentence claim, and record locations (receipt and `docs/testing/`).
- **What agents may prepare:** the packet, the tour build, consent materials, draft revisions.
- **Closing:** agents never close this bead on their own judgment; it closes when both checks are recorded, findings resolved, and the tour participant's sentence captures the claim.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every R2 passage reviewed with findings resolved.
- [ ] The tour completed and the one-sentence claim recorded and adequate.
- [ ] Names, dates, and locations recorded.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests
Before the review, `audit-readings` passes for the paper and tour anchors resolve.

### End-to-end tests
Before the tour test, run the tour route in the 320 px, keyboard, and reduced-motion lanes and link run ids.

### Structured logging
Findings are documents; pre-session runs log JSONL as usual.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- A participant who repeats "$E = mc^2$" has not stated the paper's claim; record that honestly and improve the tour.
- Do not coach.

## Dependencies

Blocked by: `am-me-readings-69bo` (R2 texts), `am-tour-15min-mass-energy-nqz1` (the tour), `am-gov-owners-and-reviewers-hte` (assignment).

Unblocks: `am-dod-mass-energy-oxh2`.

title: Implement the scoped notation concordance model with rename, unit-conversion, and modernization operations
description:
# Implement the scoped notation concordance model with rename, unit-conversion, and modernization operations

**Epic:** `am-ep-notation-vrg` · **Batch:** A · **Priority:** P0 · **Plan sections:** §2.3 (glossary refactor), §4.5 step 3, §4.7, §6.1, §11.4 (traceability only)

## Background

The donor kept a global archaic-term dictionary keyed by spelling. That model fails here because the same glyph means different things in different papers and sections: $\beta$ is Wien's constant in paper 1 and the modern $\gamma$ in papers 3 and 4; $L$ is the speed of light in paper 1, a magnetic-field component in paper 3 §6, and emitted energy in paper 4; $k$ is viscosity in paper 2. The concordance is therefore scoped: an entry holds only within a paper and a set of sections, and resolving a glyph without a scope is an error.

It also separates three operations a careless reader collapses into one: a **symbol rename** ($V \to c$), a **unit-system conversion** (Gaussian to SI), and a **substantive modernization** (a later formalism or convention, such as the modern transverse mass). Only renames are applied by the notation toggle; conversions and modernizations are explicit, labeled content.

## Scope

In scope:
- The `ConcordanceEntry` schema and file layout `content/notation/<paper-slug>.yaml`.
- `src/content/notation/resolve.ts`: the scoped resolver.
- The collision registry and first-use callout data.
- The toggle contract consumed by `am-eq-latex-generation-hc3` and `am-read-perspective-toggle-abd`.
- Validation hooks used by `am-cm-checks-semantic-lic`.

Out of scope: per-paper entries (the `not-entries-*` beads), the UI toggle (`am-read-perspective-toggle-abd`), expression trees (`am-eq-expression-tree-8kl`), the `/notation` page (`am-not-notation-page-2us`).

## Requirements

### Entry fields

- `id` (for example `bm.k.viscosity`), `paper` (route slug), `scope` (section ids such as `s1`–`s5`, or specific block ids), `glyph` (`unicode`, `latex`, and typographic variants such as bold or primed forms).
- `meaning` (definition in plain words) and `binding`: either `quantityId` (from `am-not-quantity-registry-2f7`) or a non-quantity kind (`coordinateSystemLabel`, `index`, `function`, `historicalConstant`, `bookkeepingConstant`).
- `modernSymbol` (LaTeX) where a rename exists; `dimension` (derived from the quantity); `frameOrReference`.
- `operation`: `rename` (with `modernSymbol`), `unitConversion` (with `fromSystem`, `toSystem`, and the conversion expression, for example Gaussian field components to SI), or `modernization` (with a link to the modern-lens record and a statement that it changes the argument, not just the letters).
- `collision`: `{ severity: danger | caution, collidesWith: [entry ids], firstUseAnchor }`. Danger collisions (Einstein's $\beta$ as the modern $\gamma$; $k$ as viscosity) render in red on first use; caution collisions render as scoped callouts.
- `notes`, `sources` (facsimile page and anchor where the meaning is established).

### Resolver

- `resolveGlyph(paper, anchor, glyph)` returns exactly one entry or a typed error: `unscoped` (no entry covers the anchor), `ambiguous` (two entries with the same glyph overlap in scope), `unknownPaper`.
- `entriesForAnchor(paper, anchor)` lists the entries active at an anchor for legends and callouts.
- `firstUse(entryId)` returns the anchor where a callout appears.

### Rules

- No global find-and-replace; there is no API that maps a glyph to a modern symbol without a paper and anchor.
- The source and translation faces use printed notation only.
- The explanation faces default to printed notation; the toggle applies `rename` operations by re-rendering from the semantic tree. It never applies `unitConversion` or `modernization`.
- "Modern notation" and "modern knowledge" are independent choices: the data model never lets a rename import a later proof.

## Technical Approach

- zod schema plus TypeScript types; entries compiled into a per-paper interval index keyed by glyph for fast scoped lookup.
- Build-time validation: every entry's `quantityId` exists; scopes reference real section or block ids; no overlapping scopes for the same glyph in one paper; every danger collision has a first-use anchor.
- The toggle contract is an exported function `modernSymbolFor(termBinding, perspective)` that consults only `rename` entries.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The schema, resolver, collision registry, and toggle contract exist with typed errors.
- [ ] Overlapping scopes and unscoped glyphs fail validation.
- [ ] The toggle contract applies renames only; conversions and modernizations are never applied implicitly.
- [ ] Danger and caution collisions carry first-use anchors.
- [ ] `am-cm-checks-semantic-lic` can call the resolver to reject unresolved equation symbols.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests
`src/content/notation/resolve.test.ts` with fixture entries covering the real collisions:
- $\beta$ at a paper 3 §3 anchor resolves to a `rename` entry bound to `lorentzFactor` with modern symbol $\gamma$; $\beta$ at a paper 1 §2 anchor resolves to Wien's constant, not the Lorentz factor;
- $k$ at a paper 2 §3 anchor resolves to `viscosity`;
- $\tau$ at a paper 3 anchor binds to the moving-frame coordinate time, not `properTime`;
- $L$ resolves to three different entries in papers 1, 3 (§6), and 4;
- a glyph at an anchor with no entry returns `unscoped`; two overlapping entries return `ambiguous`;
- `modernSymbolFor` returns $c$ for $V$ under the modern perspective and leaves a Gaussian field component unconverted (no implicit `unitConversion`);
- a `modernization` entry is flagged and never returned by `modernSymbolFor`.

### End-to-end tests
- None in this bead; `am-read-perspective-toggle-abd` tests the toggle in the browser.

### Structured logging
JSONL to `artifacts/test-logs/notation-model/<run-id>.jsonl`: `timestamp`, `suite`, `testId`, `paper`, `anchor`, `glyph`, `expectedEntry`, `actualEntry`, `errorCode`, `outcome`.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- A letter can appear inside a LaTeX command name, exponent, or subscript; resolution works on semantic term bindings, never on raw LaTeX strings.
- Scopes are section or block ids from the frozen inventories; never scope by page.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-not-quantity-registry-2f7`: entries bind to exact quantity ids.

Unblocks:
- `am-not-entries-brownian-1rq`, `am-not-entries-mass-energy-wq2`, `am-not-entries-relativity-f6e`, `am-not-entries-light-quanta-9cb`: entries are authored in this model.
- `am-eq-latex-generation-hc3`: modern-notation rendering uses the toggle contract.
- `am-read-perspective-toggle-abd`: the UI toggle consumes the contract.

# Author notation concordance entries for the Brownian paper

**Epic:** `am-ep-notation-vrg` · **Batch:** B (reference slice) · **Priority:** P0 · **Plan sections:** §3.4, §4.7, §11.4 (traceability only)

## Background

The Brownian paper is the reference slice, and its notation contains the plan's second dangerous collision: $k$ is viscosity, not Boltzmann's constant. $P$ is a radius, $\nu$ is a number density, and $\tau$ is an observation interval, each colliding with a different meaning elsewhere in the corpus. Each entry says where a printed symbol means what, what the modern reader would write, its dimension and frame, and whether moving to modern form is a rename, a unit conversion, or a change to the argument. Without these entries the notation toggle cannot work, equation terms cannot resolve, and readers meet collisions unprepared.

## Scope

In scope: `content/notation/brownian-motion.yaml` with an entry for every printed symbol of the paper, scoped to the frozen section and block ids, including first-use anchors and collision flags; verification of each printed glyph against the German edition or ledger.

Out of scope: the model and resolver (`am-not-concordance-model-uag`), quantity records (`am-not-quantity-registry-2f7`; add a missing quantity there first), equation records (`am-bm-equations-s4-s5-6r81`), the modern-lens explanations that modernization entries link to (readings and margin beads).

## Requirements

### Entries required (verify every glyph and scope against the edition)

- $k \to \eta$: viscosity (rename; binds `viscosity`; historical CGS values also need a `unitConversion` entry from poise to Pa·s, since the printed $k = 1.35\times10^{-2}$ is in poise).
- $P \to a$: particle radius (rename; binds `particleRadius`; not pressure).
- $\nu \to n$: number density of suspended particles (rename; binds `numberDensity`; not frequency).
- $p$: osmotic pressure (binds `osmoticPressure`; modern symbol $\Pi$ in the explanation layer).
- $R/N \to k_B$: the composite rename (binds `boltzmannConstant`); $R$ gas constant (`gasConstant`), $N$ Avogadro's number as used in 1905 (`avogadroNumberEstimate`).
- $K$: the force on a particle in §3 (binds `externalForce`; modern $F$).
- $v$: the particle's drift velocity in §3 (binds `driftVelocity`).
- $D$: diffusion coefficient (binds `diffusionCoefficient`).
- $\tau$: the observation interval of §4 (binds `observationInterval`; modern $\Delta t$).
- $\Delta$: displacement over $\tau$ (binds `displacement1d`).
- $\varphi(\Delta)$: the transition kernel, the probability density of $\Delta$ (non-quantity `function` binding with a note on normalization and symmetry).
- $f(x,t) \to p(x,t)$: number density or probability density as a function of position and time (rename; state which normalization the source uses).
- $\lambda_x \to \sqrt{\langle x^2\rangle}$: the root-mean-square displacement along $x$ (rename; binds `rmsDisplacement1d`).
- $x$, $t$, $T$: position, time, temperature.
- $\mu$ (micron) as a printed unit: a `unitConversion` display entry to μm.
- Any further symbols found in §§1–5, including those of the §2 configuration-integral argument.

### Collisions

- **Danger**: $k$ (viscosity here; Boltzmann's constant in modern notation) with a red first-use callout at its first appearance.
- **Caution**: $P$ (work function in paper 1), $\nu$ (frequency in papers 1 and 3), $\tau$ (moving-frame time in paper 3), $K$ (coordinate system in paper 3, kinetic energy in paper 4), $\varphi$ (entropy density in paper 1, an angle in paper 3), $N$ (a magnetic-field component in paper 3).

### Rules

1. Every entry has `paper`, `scope`, `glyph`, `meaning`, `binding`, `operation`, `dimension` (through the quantity), `frameOrReference`, `sources` (facsimile page and anchor where the meaning is established).
2. `rename` entries give the modern symbol; `unitConversion` entries give the systems and the conversion; `modernization` entries link to a labeled modern-lens record and state that the argument changes.
3. Danger collisions carry a first-use anchor for the red callout; caution collisions carry a first-use anchor for a scoped callout.
4. No entry is written from memory or from a translation that changes notation; the printed glyph in the German edition decides.

## Technical Approach

- Start from the paper's difficulties file (`docs/editorial/brownian-motion-difficulties.md`) and the inventory's symbol list; walk every equation and inline formula in order.
- Validate with the concordance model's build-time checks; resolve any `unscoped` or `ambiguous` report before closing.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every symbol in the inventory's symbol list and every math token in the paper's ledger (when available) resolves to exactly one entry for its anchor.
- [ ] All entries listed above exist with complete fields and correct operation kinds.
- [ ] Collision flags and first-use anchors exist for every collision listed.
- [ ] Every entry cites the facsimile page and anchor that establishes its meaning.
- [ ] Validation passes with zero `unscoped` and zero `ambiguous` results.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests
`src/content/notation/brownian.notation.test.ts`:
- coverage: every math token in the paper's German edition blocks (or, before the edition exists, the inventory's symbol list) resolves through `resolveGlyph`;
- `resolveGlyph('brownian-motion', <§3 anchor>, 'k')` binds `viscosity` and is flagged danger;
- $\nu$ in §1 binds `numberDensity`, never `frequency`;
- the printed $1.35\times10^{-2}$ poise converts to $1.35\times10^{-3}$ Pa·s through the unit-conversion entry;
- every danger collision entry has a first-use anchor that resolves to an existing block.
Unresolved equation symbols are also rejected at build time by `am-cm-checks-semantic-lic`.

### End-to-end tests
- None in this bead; `am-not-notation-page-2us` and `am-read-perspective-toggle-abd` exercise the entries in the browser.

### Structured logging
JSONL to `artifacts/test-logs/notation-brownian-motion/<run-id>.jsonl`: `timestamp`, `suite`, `testId`, `paper`, `anchor`, `glyph`, `entryId`, `check`, `outcome`, `message`.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- Build §§4–5 entries first so the reference slice can proceed; complete §§1–3 in the same bead.
- The velocity-warning verification flag from the inventory does not affect notation, but do not add an entry for a "Brownian speed"; `apparentSpeed` belongs only to the explanation layer's velocity-trap discussion.
- A symbol that is a label (a coordinate-system name, an index) still needs an entry with a non-quantity binding.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-not-concordance-model-uag`: the schema, resolver, and validation.
- `am-edn-inventory-brownian-slg`: frozen section and block ids for scopes and the symbol list.

Unblocks:
- `am-not-notation-page-2us`: the searchable concordance lists these entries.
- `am-bm-equations-s4-s5-6r81`: equation terms resolve through these entries.

title: Author notation concordance entries for the relativity paper
description:
# Author notation concordance entries for the relativity paper

**Epic:** `am-ep-notation-vrg` · **Batch:** E (whole paper, including the §6 conversions needed in Batch G) · **Priority:** P1 · **Plan sections:** §3.5, §4.7, §11.4 (traceability only)

## Background

The relativity paper holds the plan's first dangerous collision ($\beta$ is the modern $\gamma$; the modern $\beta = v/c$ appears nowhere in the paper), moving-frame coordinates whose time symbol $\tau$ must not be read as proper time, Gaussian field components that need unit conversion as well as renaming, and a §10 mass convention that is a modernization, not a rename. Each entry says where a printed symbol means what, what the modern reader would write, its dimension and frame, and whether moving to modern form is a rename, a unit conversion, or a change to the argument. Without these entries the notation toggle cannot work, equation terms cannot resolve, and readers meet collisions unprepared.

## Scope

In scope: `content/notation/special-relativity.yaml` with an entry for every printed symbol of the paper, scoped to the frozen section and block ids, including first-use anchors and collision flags; verification of each printed glyph against the German edition or ledger.

Out of scope: the model and resolver (`am-not-concordance-model-uag`), quantity records (`am-not-quantity-registry-2f7`; add a missing quantity there first), equation records (`am-srk-equations-30cq`), the modern-lens explanations that modernization entries link to (readings and margin beads).

## Requirements

### Entries required (verify every glyph and scope against the edition)

- $V \to c$ (rename); $v$ frame speed (`frameSpeed`); $w$ and $U$ the velocities of §5 (`particleVelocity` scoped).
- $\beta \to \gamma$ (rename; `lorentzFactor`).
- $K$ (the stationary system) and $k$ (the moving system): `coordinateSystemLabel` bindings, modern $S$ and $S'$.
- $x, y, z, t$ in $K$; $(\xi, \eta, \zeta, \tau) \to (x', y', z', t')$ in $k$ (renames; $\tau$ binds `coordinateTime` in the moving frame with a note that it is not `properTime`).
- $t_A$, $t_B$, $t'_A$: the clock readings of §1 (bind `coordinateTime` with event tags).
- $R$: the sphere radius of §4 (`rodLengthRest` or a radius quantity, scoped to §4).
- $X, Y, Z \to \mathbf{E}$ and $L, M, N \to \mathbf{B}$ in §§6–9: a `rename` to vector components plus a `unitConversion` from Gaussian to SI (the modern SI transformation laws differ in form by factors of $c$); primed components likewise.
- $\varphi$: the angle between the wave normal and the direction of motion (§§7–8; `propagationAngle`).
- $\nu$, $\nu'$: frequency (cyclic) in each frame; amplitude symbols as printed in §§7–8.
- $E$, $E'$: the energy of the light complex in each frame (`lightComplexEnergy`).
- $\rho$ and the current or velocity components of §9 (`chargeDensity`, `currentDensity`).
- $\varepsilon$, $\mu$ or $m$ as printed in §10 for the electron's charge and mass; the longitudinal and transverse masses as printed (`modernization` entries linking to the modern force-convention treatment: the source's transverse coefficient corresponds to $m\gamma^2$ under its comoving-force convention, the laboratory convention gives $m\gamma$).
- $W$: the work of §10 (`electronWork`).
- "Light complex" (*Lichtkomplex*): a term, not a symbol, noted with a pointer to its term annotation.
- Any further symbols found in the introduction and §§1–10.

### Collisions

- **Danger**: $\beta$ (the modern $\gamma$) with a red first-use callout in §3.
- **Caution**: $\tau$ (not proper time; an observation interval in paper 2), $L$ and $N$ (magnetic-field components here; speed of light and Avogadro's number elsewhere), $E$ (light-complex energy here, an electric field in modern notation), $K$ and $k$ (systems here; a force and viscosity in paper 2), $\varphi$ (an angle here), $V$ and $v$.

### Rules

1. Every entry has `paper`, `scope`, `glyph`, `meaning`, `binding`, `operation`, `dimension` (through the quantity), `frameOrReference`, `sources` (facsimile page and anchor where the meaning is established).
2. `rename` entries give the modern symbol; `unitConversion` entries give the systems and the conversion; `modernization` entries link to a labeled modern-lens record and state that the argument changes.
3. Danger collisions carry a first-use anchor for the red callout; caution collisions carry a first-use anchor for a scoped callout.
4. No entry is written from memory or from a translation that changes notation; the printed glyph in the German edition decides.

**Added in review (the §3 auxiliary coordinate).** In §3 Einstein himself writes $x' = x - vt$ as a Galilean auxiliary coordinate, which is not the moving-frame coordinate $\xi$. The modern rename $(\xi, \eta, \zeta, \tau) \to (x', y', z', t')$ would therefore collide with a printed symbol inside §3. The concordance scopes Einstein's printed $x'$ to §3 with the meaning "Galilean auxiliary coordinate $x - vt$" and binds it to its own quantity id; the modern notation form renders that auxiliary with a distinct glyph (for example $\tilde{x}$) wherever the moving-frame $x'$ also appears. A test renders every §3 equation in modern notation and fails if one glyph denotes both quantities.

## Technical Approach

- Start from the paper's difficulties file (`docs/editorial/special-relativity-difficulties.md`) and the inventory's symbol list; walk every equation and inline formula in order.
- Validate with the concordance model's build-time checks; resolve any `unscoped` or `ambiguous` report before closing.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every symbol in the inventory's symbol list and every math token in the paper's ledger (when available) resolves to exactly one entry for its anchor.
- [ ] All entries listed above exist with complete fields and correct operation kinds.
- [ ] Collision flags and first-use anchors exist for every collision listed.
- [ ] Every entry cites the facsimile page and anchor that establishes its meaning.
- [ ] Validation passes with zero `unscoped` and zero `ambiguous` results.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests
`src/content/notation/relativity.notation.test.ts`:
- coverage: every math token in the paper's German edition blocks (or, before the edition exists, the inventory's symbol list) resolves through `resolveGlyph`;
- $\beta$ at a §3 anchor binds `lorentzFactor` and is flagged danger;
- $\tau$ binds moving-frame `coordinateTime`, never `properTime`;
- $Y'$ in §6 resolves to a rename plus a Gaussian-to-SI unit conversion, and the toggle contract applies only the rename;
- the §10 transverse mass resolves to a modernization entry that the toggle never applies;
- every danger collision entry has a first-use anchor that resolves to an existing block.
Unresolved equation symbols are also rejected at build time by `am-cm-checks-semantic-lic`.

### End-to-end tests
- None in this bead; `am-not-notation-page-2us` and `am-read-perspective-toggle-abd` exercise the entries in the browser.

### Structured logging
JSONL to `artifacts/test-logs/notation-special-relativity/<run-id>.jsonl`: `timestamp`, `suite`, `testId`, `paper`, `anchor`, `glyph`, `entryId`, `check`, `outcome`, `message`.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- Give §§6–10 the same care as §§1–5.
- Never convert Gaussian formulas by string substitution; conversion is a derivation owned by the explanation layer, recorded here as an operation.
- A symbol that is a label (a coordinate-system name, an index) still needs an entry with a non-quantity binding.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-not-concordance-model-uag`: the schema, resolver, and validation.
- `am-edn-inventory-relativity-0u9`: frozen section and block ids for scopes and the symbol list.

Unblocks:
- `am-not-notation-page-2us`: the searchable concordance lists these entries.
- `am-srk-equations-30cq`: equation terms resolve through these entries.

title: Build the searchable /notation page
description:
# Build the searchable /notation page

**Epic:** `am-ep-notation-vrg` · **Batch:** H · **Priority:** P2 · **Plan sections:** §4.7, §15.1, §16.1, §16.2 (traceability only)

## Background

Readers who meet $\beta$, $k$, or $L$ in a passage get a scoped callout at that anchor, but many also want the whole map in one place: every symbol Einstein prints, in every paper and section where it holds, beside its modern form and the kind of change that modern form involves. `/notation` is that reference. It must be fully readable without JavaScript and must make collisions obvious rather than hiding them behind a single dictionary entry per letter.

## Scope

In scope: the `/notation` route, its static rendering of all concordance entries, filters, search integration, collision views, first-use links, print styles, and tests.

Out of scope: the entries themselves (`not-entries-*` beads), the resolver (`am-not-concordance-model-uag`), the site-wide search index (`am-plat-search-index-snx1`), per-passage callouts (`am-read-perspective-toggle-abd` and the reader faces).

## Requirements

1. **Static page** generated at build time listing every entry grouped by paper and section, with: the glyph as printed (static KaTeX), the meaning, the modern symbol, the dimension and display units, the frame or reference condition, the operation kind (rename, unit conversion, modernization) with its rule, the collision flag, and a link to the first use in the edition.
2. **Collision view**: selecting a glyph (for example $\beta$) shows every entry for that glyph across papers side by side, with danger collisions marked in red and also by an icon and text label (never color alone).
3. **Filters**: paper, section, glyph, modern symbol, operation kind, collision severity. Filters enhance the page; without JavaScript the full grouped list and a glyph index of in-page anchors remain usable.
4. **Search**: entries are indexed by `am-plat-search-index-snx1` under the glyph, its LaTeX, its modern symbol, and plain-language meaning, so `β`, `beta`, `k viscosity`, and `speed of light` all find the right entries.
5. **Links**: each first-use link opens the paper at the anchor in the reading face with the notation callout visible; each entry has its own stable anchor (for example `/notation#lq.beta.wien`).
6. **Accessibility**: glyphs have authored spoken names ("beta, Wien's constant, light-quanta paper, section 2"); the table is navigable by keyboard and screen reader; no horizontal page overflow at 320 px (long rows reflow into cards).
7. **Print**: a print stylesheet produces a clean concordance grouped by paper.

## Technical Approach

- App Router page `src/app/notation/page.tsx`, statically generated from compiled concordance records and quantity metadata.
- Client-side filters as progressive enhancement over the static list; search through the shared palette and index.
- Static KaTeX rendering for glyphs and modern symbols.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The page lists every concordance entry with all required fields and a working first-use link.
- [ ] The collision view shows all entries for a glyph, with danger collisions marked by color and by text.
- [ ] Filters and search work, and the page remains fully usable with JavaScript disabled.
- [ ] Keyboard, screen-reader, 320 px, and print checks pass.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests
- `src/app/notation/notationPage.test.ts`: the page data includes every compiled entry; every first-use link resolves to an existing anchor; every entry anchor is unique.

### End-to-end tests
`scripts/e2e-paper-vertical-slices.ts` notation scenario (lanes: desktop, 320 px touch, keyboard-only, JavaScript disabled, print):
- search `β` and see Wien's constant (light quanta) and the Lorentz factor (relativity, mass–energy) with the danger marking in text and color;
- search `k` and see viscosity in the Brownian paper;
- follow a first-use link and land on the anchor with the callout visible;
- with JavaScript disabled, reach the $L$ entries through the glyph index;
- no page-level horizontal overflow at 320 px; print output groups entries by paper.

### Structured logging
JSONL per the browser harness: `timestamp`, `suite: "notation-page"`, `testId`, `browser`, `viewport`, `jsEnabled`, `query`, `expectedEntryIds`, `actualEntryIds`, `outcome`, `message`; failures retain a screenshot, trace, and DOM snapshot.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- Do not collapse entries for the same glyph into one row; the collision is the lesson.
- Keep the page static-first; filtering must never be the only way to find an entry.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-not-entries-brownian-1rq`, `am-not-entries-mass-energy-wq2`, `am-not-entries-relativity-f6e`, `am-not-entries-light-quanta-9cb`: the entries the page lists.
- `am-read-shell-routes-3ua`: App Router shell and anchor conventions.
- `am-plat-search-index-snx1`: the build-time search index.

Unblocks:
