- No direct dependents; the concordance becomes browsable as a whole.

title: Build the canonical quantity registry and unit display adapters
description:
# Build the canonical quantity registry and unit display adapters

**Epic:** `am-ep-notation-vrg` · **Batch:** A · **Priority:** P0 · **Plan sections:** §2.2 (equation seams), §8, §11.2 (`Quantity`), §11.4, §11.5, §13.4, §22.5 (traceability only)

## Background

The donor's colorized equations looked telemetry up by human label and matched tokens permissively (`variableId.startsWith("var_" + id)`). That is tolerable in a patent museum and wrong in a bilingual scientific edition where one symbol means different things in different sections. Here every live term, control, readout, dataset column, color role, and unit adapter binds to an **exact canonical quantity id**. The registry also carries the distinctions dimensions cannot settle: cyclic versus angular frequency, a spectral density versus a total, coordinate time versus a proper interval, laboratory versus comoving force, mean square versus variance, measured versus latent position. Frame and observation identities belong on quantities, not only in captions.

## Scope

In scope:
- `content/quantities/*.yaml`: one record per quantity, grouped by domain.
- `src/content/quantities/registry.ts`: loader, validation, lookup that fails on unknown ids.
- `src/units/`: display adapters from canonical SI transport to display units, including historical CGS and Gaussian displays.
- The seed registry for all four papers.

Out of scope: constant values and constant sets (`am-ref-constants-xik`), dimension arithmetic on expressions (`am-cm-dimension-validator-aoz`, which this registry uses), notation entries (`am-not-concordance-model-uag`), precision and uncertainty formatting rules (`am-ver-precision-display-5e5`), color palette values (`am-design-semantic-color-8vbq`).

## Requirements

### Record fields

- `id`: lower camel case, semantic, frame-tagged where needed (`frequencyEnergyDensity`, `wavelengthEnergyDensity`, `stoppingPotentialMagnitude`, `transverseForceComoving`). Never a glyph.
- `name`, `description` (one or two sentences).
- `dimension`: exact rational exponents over the SI base dimensions (length, mass, time, current, temperature, amount, luminous intensity). Fractional exponents are allowed and never truncated.
- `kind`: `scalar | vector | vectorComponent | density | total`, plus flags `frequencyConvention: cyclic | angular`, `timeKind: coordinate | proper`, `frame: laboratory | comoving | rest | moving | frameIndependent`, `statistic: meanSquare | variance | rms | mean | none`, `observation: measured | latent | model`.
- `referenceConditions` where meaningful (for example "per unit frequency interval", "one-dimensional marginal").
- `units`: `canonical` (SI) and `display` units with exact conversion factors.
- `colorRole`: one of the semantic roles owned by `am-design-semantic-color-8vbq` (energy, time and rates, space and geometry, material response, statistical quantities, fields, quanta).
- `formatting`: default display unit and notation hints; significant-figure policy is delegated to `am-ver-precision-display-5e5`.
- `constantStatus` for quantities that name constants: `definedExact | measured | historicalEstimate` (values live in `am-ref-constants-xik`).

### Unit display adapters (`src/units/`)

- Canonical transport in SI; display conversions include m to μm, Pa·s to mPa·s, J to eV, Hz to THz, meters to light-seconds (1 ls = 299 792 458 m exactly), kelvin, and historical CGS and Gaussian units: poise (1 P = 0.1 Pa·s, so Einstein's printed $1.35\times10^{-2}$ P is $1.35\times10^{-3}$ Pa·s), erg ($10^{-7}$ J), statcoulomb, statvolt (exactly 299.792458 V; historical calculations often used 300 V, and a historical fixture records which factor reproduces a printed number), gauss ($10^{-4}$ T), statvolt per centimeter for electric fields.
- **Conversions apply to sensitivities**: a derivative per meter becomes a derivative per micrometer by the inverse factor.
- Locale-aware display over the canonical numeric transport (from `am-cm-i18n-readiness-b2g` once available); display language never changes a stored value.

### Seed registry (at minimum)

Radiation and light quanta: `frequency` (cyclic), `angularFrequency`, `wavelength`, `temperature`, `frequencyEnergyDensity` (J·m⁻³·Hz⁻¹), `wavelengthEnergyDensity` (J·m⁻⁴), `logFrequencyEnergyDensity`, `spectralEntropyDensity`, `radiationEnergy`, `radiationEntropy`, `volume`, `bandwidth`, `independentPointCount`, `configurationProbability`, `workFunction`, `maxKineticEnergy`, `stoppingPotentialMagnitude`, `collectorPotential` (signed), `incidentPower`, `quantumRate`, `quantumEfficiency`, `ionizationEnergy`.
Diffusion and inference: `diffusionCoefficient`, `viscosity`, `particleRadius`, `numberDensity`, `osmoticPressure`, `mobility`, `dragForce`, `externalForce`, `driftVelocity`, `particleFlux`, `displacement1d`, `meanSquareDisplacement1d`, `rmsDisplacement1d`, `radialDistance2d`, `observationInterval`, `elapsedTime`, `localizationErrorStd`, `exposureTime`, `apparentSpeed` (labeled a model artifact, never a physical velocity), `avogadroNumberEstimate` and `avogadroConstant`, `boltzmannConstant`, `gasConstant`.
Kinematics and electrodynamics: `frameSpeed` (signed), `lorentzFactor`, `rapidity`, `coordinateTime`, `properTime`, `eventSeparationSpatial`, `eventSeparationTemporal`, `rodLengthRest`, `rodLengthMeasured` (frame-tagged), `clockOffset`, `particleVelocity`, `electricField`, `magneticField`, `fieldInvariantE2MinusC2B2`, `fieldInvariantEDotB`, `chargeDensity`, `currentDensity`, `dopplerFactor`, `propagationAngle`, `lightComplexEnergy`, `mirrorSpeed`, `reflectedFrequencyRatio`, `interceptedPower`, `radiationForce`, `transverseForceComoving`, `transverseForceLaboratory`, `longitudinalForce`, `electronWork`.
Mass–energy: `emittedEnergyRest`, `bodyEnergyRestBefore`, `bodyEnergyRestAfter`, `bodyEnergyMovingBefore`, `bodyEnergyMovingAfter`, `kineticEnergyDifference`, `finiteSpeedMassProxy`, `massLossCoefficient`, `massChangeSigned`, `invariantMassSystem`, `emissionAngle`.

## Technical Approach

- YAML records validated by a zod schema derived from `am-cm-schemas-argument-llm`'s `Quantity` entity; dimension objects use the rational type from `am-cm-dimension-validator-aoz`.
- `getQuantity(id)` throws a typed error for unknown ids; no fuzzy lookup exists.
- Unit adapters are pure functions with exact rational factors where the definition is exact.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every seed quantity exists with complete fields, and ids are unique lower camel case.
- [ ] Unknown ids throw; there is no label or prefix lookup.
- [ ] All listed unit conversions exist, round-trip within stated tolerance, and apply correctly to sensitivities.
- [ ] Paired quantities that differ only in frame, convention, or statistic are distinct records with distinct ids.
- [ ] The registry compiles into the content build and is consumable by equations, controls, datasets, and colors.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests
`src/content/quantities/registry.test.ts` and `src/units/units.test.ts`:
- schema validation for every record; unique ids; lower camel case;
- dimensions: `diffusionCoefficient` is L²·T⁻¹; `rmsDisplacement1d` is L; the product of `diffusionCoefficient` and `elapsedTime` raised to 1/2 has dimension L (rational exponent arithmetic); `frequencyEnergyDensity` (M·L⁻¹·T⁻¹) differs from `wavelengthEnergyDensity` (M·L⁻²·T⁻²);
- distinctness: `transverseForceComoving` versus `transverseForceLaboratory`; `properTime` versus `coordinateTime`; `frequency` versus `angularFrequency`; `meanSquareDisplacement1d` versus a variance quantity;
- conversions: 1.35e-2 P equals 1.35e-3 Pa·s; 1 ls equals 299 792 458 m; 1 eV equals 1.602176634e-19 J; 1 statvolt equals 299.792458 V; a sensitivity of 2 per meter equals 2e-6 per micrometer;
- unknown id lookup throws a typed error.

### End-to-end tests
- None in this bead; controls and equations exercise the registry in their own browser lanes.

### Structured logging
JSONL to `artifacts/test-logs/quantities/<run-id>.jsonl`: `timestamp`, `suite`, `testId`, `quantityId`, `check`, `expected`, `actual`, `tolerance`, `outcome`, `message`.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- A missing $2\pi$ is invisible to dimensional analysis; the frequency convention flag is the guard.
- Do not store historical constant values here; keep values in `am-ref-constants-xik` with era and provenance.
- `apparentSpeed` exists only to label the velocity trap as a model artifact; it must never feed a physical claim.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-cm-schemas-argument-llm`: the `Quantity` entity schema.
- `am-cm-dimension-validator-aoz`: rational dimension arithmetic.

Unblocks:
- `am-not-concordance-model-uag`, `am-eq-expression-tree-8kl`, `am-cm-checks-semantic-lic`, `am-ref-constants-xik`, `am-ver-precision-display-5e5`, `am-inst-2d-view-kit-u75r`, `am-inst-parameter-controls-cmj9`, `am-design-semantic-color-8vbq`: all bind to exact quantity ids.

title: Build the cookieless clarity signal and the weekly About-page summary
description:
# Build the cookieless clarity signal and the weekly About-page summary

**Epic:** `am-ep-platform-8ci` · **Batch:** batch-i · **Priority:** P2 · **Plan sections:** §6.2, §16.6, §17.5, §20 (traceability only)

## Background

The site keeps exactly one analytic: **the clarity signal**. Under every paragraph a one-click "this was clear / this was not" control records **the detail level and anchor**, **aggregated without cookies, identifiers, or IP retention**, because it tells editors exactly where an explanation fails; **its weekly summary is published on the About page**. Free-text answers are never sent anywhere, and there are no third-party scripts, fingerprinting, advertising, or accounts. With small traffic, results are descriptive observations, never claims of statistical power.

A statically generated site needs a small first-party write path and aggregate storage for this, and abuse control must work without retaining anything that identifies a person.

## Scope

In scope: the paragraph control; the first-party endpoint; aggregate storage schema; abuse control without IP retention; the weekly summary job and its publication on `/about`; the privacy design record; tests proving the privacy properties.

Out of scope: the About page itself (`am-design-sources-about-zumd`); comprehension testing (`am-edit-comprehension-rounds-tcgi`); local storage layer (`am-plat-local-storage-km8f`).

## Requirements

- **Control**: two buttons under each readable unit ("This was clear" and "This was not clear") with accessible names naming the paragraph; a short thank-you confirmation; no counts shown to readers, no badges, no prompts for text; hidden in print; unobtrusive in reading-only mode.
- **Payload**: `{ anchor, paper, detail (0, 1, or 2), vote ("clear" or "unclear"), contentRevision }` only. The client prevents repeat votes for the same unit in a session using local storage when available.
- **Endpoint**: a first-party function (for example `/api/clarity`) accepting `POST` with a bounded body; it validates the anchor and revision against a build-emitted manifest, increments aggregate counters keyed by week, revision, anchor, detail, and vote, and stores nothing else. It never logs or persists IP addresses, user agents, or request identifiers.
- **Abuse control without retention**: in-memory, short-lived rate limiting that never writes identifying data (for example a sliding window keyed by a daily-rotating in-memory salted hash that is never persisted); oversized, malformed, or unknown-anchor requests are rejected. Record the chosen design and its privacy review in `docs/decisions/clarity-signal-privacy.md`.
- **No cookies**: the endpoint and pages set no cookies.
- **Weekly summary**: a scheduled job produces a static JSON summary per week with, per section and anchor, counts by detail level and vote, suppressing anchors below a minimum count; the About page shows the latest summary (via rebuild or a static JSON fetch) in plain language, emphasizing where explanations were found unclear, with counts and no inferential claims.
- **Editor view**: the same summary sorted by the share of "unclear" votes with counts, linked to anchors.
- **Without JavaScript**: the control does not appear; nothing else depends on it.

## Technical Approach

- `src/platform/clarity/ClarityControl.tsx`, `app/api/clarity/route.ts`, `aggregateStore.ts` (first-party storage chosen at implementation with the privacy review), `scripts/clarity/weeklySummary.ts`, and a summary section component consumed by `/about`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Votes from the control increment the correct aggregate counters in a test store; nothing else is stored.
- [ ] Requests with unknown anchors, oversized bodies, or wrong methods are rejected; rate limiting works without persisting identifiers.
- [ ] No cookies are set; no third-party requests occur.
- [ ] The weekly summary suppresses low counts and appears on `/about` in plain language.
- [ ] The privacy design record exists with its review.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests

- `route.test.ts`: validation, method and size limits, manifest checks, aggregate increments.
- `aggregateStore.test.ts`: the persisted record shape contains only aggregate keys and counts (a schema assertion over every write).
- `rateLimit.test.ts`: limits within a window; no persistence calls with request-derived data.
- `weeklySummary.test.ts`: aggregation, suppression threshold, deterministic output.

### End-to-end tests

Through `am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh` against a preview deployment or local function runtime: vote on a Brownian paragraph at two Detail levels; verify counters; assert no `Set-Cookie`, no third-party requests, and no repeat votes in a session; render `/about` with a fixture summary.

### Structured logging

JSON lines with `anchor`, `detail`, `vote`, `status`, `rejectedReason`, `cookiesSet`, `thirdPartyRequests`, `summaryWeek`, `suppressedAnchors`, `outcome`; logs never include IP addresses or user agents. Path: `artifacts/test-logs/platform-clarity/<run-id>.jsonl`.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- A vote is a pointer for editors, not a measure of learning; satisfaction and confidence are not understanding.
- Hosting platforms may log requests by default; configure or document that behavior in the privacy record.

## Dependencies

Blocked by: `am-read-detail-axis-sfc` (readable units and the Detail level recorded with each vote); `am-design-sources-about-zumd` (the page that publishes the summary).

Unblocks: no manifest rows depend on this bead directly.

title: Build the later installable offline edition
description:
# Build the later installable offline edition

**Epic:** `am-ep-later-gap` · **Batch:** later · **Priority:** P3 · **Plan sections:** §12.8, §16.3, §18.3, §19.7 (traceability only)

## Background

Readers on unreliable connections, in classrooms without network access, or traveling benefit from an edition that works offline. The plan sequences this carefully. First comes an explicit "save this chapter for offline reading" path, a self-contained HTML chapter with its size stated, "before a service worker exists" (`am-plat-offline-chapter-un8i`). Then "a later installable mode caches a coherent edition manifest, its required assets, and optionally the selected laboratory packages, claiming offline numerical operation only when the exact bundle and initialization path have been tested without a network; prior cached editions stay readable during an update; storage eviction never corrupts the online reader; private notes are never cached into shareable URLs or exports by default."

**Why later:** a service worker can pin readers to stale or broken content and interferes with rollback if done carelessly. The site is static-first, so the online reader must stay excellent without one. The innovation sequence allows offline work to expand only after "the access need is tested and the publication and revision path is reliable." **Start only when:** the offline-chapter path has shipped and been used, the release manifest and rollback have proven reliable in real releases, and a tested access need for installable offline reading is recorded.

## Scope

In scope: the service worker, edition caches keyed by release, explicit install and update flows, optional laboratory packages, eviction handling, rollback compatibility, and tests.
Out of scope: the offline chapter export (`am-plat-offline-chapter-un8i`); background sync or push features (not planned).

## Requirements

1. **Explicit install.** A reader chooses "Install this edition for offline reading," sees the download size, and selects papers and, optionally, laboratory packages. Nothing installs silently.
2. **Coherent edition cache.** The cache is keyed by `releaseId` from the release manifest (`am-rel-release-manifest-3gna`). It holds the HTML for the chosen routes, route payloads, fonts and KaTeX assets, figures, and the search index. It is complete or it is not used; a partial download never serves.
3. **Updates.** When the server's current `releaseId` differs (including a rollback to an older release), download the new edition completely, verify every hash against its manifest, then switch atomically. Keep the previous edition readable until the switch. Follow the server's current release even when it is older, so rollback reaches offline readers.
4. **Laboratory packages.** Content-addressed WASM and worker bundles for selected instruments may be cached. An instrument is labeled as working offline only after its exact bundle and initialization path have passed an offline test. Otherwise it shows "This experiment is unavailable on this device" offline, and the static worked example remains.
5. **Eviction safety.** Detect missing cache entries and fall back to the network online, or to an honest unavailable state offline, without corrupting the reader. Optionally request persistent storage with an explanation, never by default.
6. **Privacy.** Local notes, predictions, and tours stay in local storage and are never written into caches, shareable URLs, or exports by default.
7. **Safety valves.** The service worker validates the manifest schema and refuses an invalid edition; a versioned kill switch unregisters the worker if a release marks it unsafe; `/release-manifest.json` is always revalidated, never served stale from the cache when online.
8. **Headers and CSP.** The worker respects the cache policy from `am-rel-smoke-rollback-cache-phre` and the site's Content-Security-Policy.

## Technical Approach

A small hand-written service worker (`public/sw.js` generated at build with the manifest's asset list) using Cache Storage with one cache per `releaseId`; an install UI in the reader settings; a verification step that hashes cached responses against the manifest. Avoid framework plugins that hide caching behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Start conditions are recorded before work begins.
- [ ] Install is explicit and shows sizes; partial downloads never serve.
- [ ] Update and rollback both reach installed readers, verified by tests.
- [ ] Offline instrument labels appear only for bundles whose offline initialization passed.
- [ ] Eviction and invalid-manifest cases degrade honestly.
- [ ] No private notes appear in any cache or export by default.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests
- `src/workers/offline/editionCache.test.ts`: cache key derivation from `releaseId`; completeness check; hash verification against a fixture manifest; atomic switch logic; downgrade on rollback.

### End-to-end tests
- Playwright with a production build: install two papers and one laboratory package; `context.setOffline(true)`; read both papers on German, English, and reading faces; run the cached instrument to an accepted snapshot; confirm an uncached instrument shows the unavailable state.
- Update scenario: publish fixture release B while the reader has A installed; confirm A stays readable during download and B serves after the switch. Rollback scenario: server returns to A; confirm the installed reader follows.
- Eviction scenario: delete entries from Cache Storage; confirm online fallback and an honest offline state.
- Privacy scenario: create notes, install, then inspect all caches for note content (must be absent).

### Structured logging
- `artifacts/test-logs/offline/<run-id>.jsonl` with `releaseId`, `scenario`, `route`, `cached`, `online`, `executionLabel`, `hashVerified`, `outcome`, `message`; failures retain screenshots and a dump of cache keys.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- A service worker that serves a stale `release-manifest.json` defeats rollback; treat the manifest as network-first.
- Offline numerical claims are easy to overstate; test the exact initialization path without network.
- Storage quotas vary widely on phones; always state sizes before download.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-plat-offline-chapter-un8i`: the simpler offline chapter path ships and proves the need first.
- `am-fs-slim-artifact-0yh`: content-addressed WASM artifacts with pinned digests are required for cacheable laboratory packages.

Unblocks: none.

title: Build the failure-tolerant local storage layer with export and clear
description:
# Build the failure-tolerant local storage layer with export and clear

**Epic:** `am-ep-platform-8ci` · **Batch:** batch-b · **Priority:** P0 · **Plan sections:** §6.2, §6.8, §7.3, §7.7, §16.2, §16.3, §16.6 (traceability only)

## Background

The site has no accounts and no cookies. "Local reading progress, tours, notes, and predictions stay in `localStorage`, exportable and clearable." Settings such as Detail, Perspective, notation, theme, and reading-only mode also persist locally and are read before first paint. Browser storage is unreliable: it can be blocked (private modes, disabled site data), full, evicted, corrupted, or changed by another tab. The plan's rule is that **saving may fail and reading continues**, important data has an explicit export, and nothing is uploaded.

## Scope

In scope: a typed, namespaced storage layer with schema versions and migrations; non-throwing results; in-memory fallback for the session; cross-tab synchronization; size accounting; export and clear per feature and globally; shared key constants for inline pre-paint scripts; privacy guarantees.

Out of scope: feature logic that stores data (`am-read-notebook-tde`, `am-tours-infra-g518`, `am-inst-predict-mode-ti7m`, `am-a11y-reading-only-6wwd`, `am-read-detail-axis-sfc`, `am-read-perspective-toggle-abd`, `am-design-themes-typography-288q`); the later installable offline mode (`am-plat-installable-offline-oit3`).

## Requirements

- **Namespaces and keys**: documented, versioned keys (for example `am:settings:v1`, `am:notebook:v1`, `am:tours:v1`, `am:predictions:v1`), with key constants injected at build time into inline pre-paint scripts so names never drift.
- **Results, not exceptions**: `read` returns `{ status: "ok" | "missing" | "unavailable" | "corrupt", value? }`; `write` returns `{ status: "ok" | "unavailable" | "quota" }`; no call throws into rendering code.
- **Session fallback**: when storage is unavailable, settings and data live in memory for the session, and features show a brief, non-blocking notice where persistence matters (for example the notebook).
- **Migrations**: forward migrations per namespace; corrupt or unknown-version data is preserved under a quarantine key and reported, never silently discarded.
- **Cross-tab**: subscribe to `storage` events so a settings change in one tab updates others without reload.
- **Size accounting**: per-namespace size estimates and soft limits with graceful trimming policies defined by each feature (never trimming data without telling the reader).
- **Export and clear**: a single "Your data on this device" panel offering export as JSON (all namespaces or one) and clear (all or one), with in-page confirmation rather than browser dialogs.
- **Privacy**: no storage content is sent over the network, placed in URLs, or used for analytics; no identifiers are generated for tracking.

## Technical Approach

- `src/platform/storage/keys.ts`, `store.ts` (typed get and set with results), `migrations.ts`, `crossTab.ts`, `exportClear.ts`, `DataPanel.tsx`; a build step that emits key constants into the inline scripts of Detail, Perspective, theme, and reading-only.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Reads and writes behave correctly with working storage, a throwing storage getter, `QuotaExceededError` on write, and corrupt JSON.
- [ ] Session fallback keeps settings for the visit when storage is blocked.
- [ ] Migrations upgrade fixture data and quarantine unknown versions.
- [ ] Cross-tab changes propagate.
- [ ] Export produces valid JSON for all namespaces; clear removes exactly the chosen namespaces.
- [ ] A network assertion shows storage content never leaves the device; inline scripts and modules share key constants.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests

- `store.test.ts`: result statuses under working, throwing, quota, and corrupt conditions using real `Storage` implementations with injected failures.
- `migrations.test.ts`: upgrades and quarantine.
- `crossTab.test.ts`: event handling and state updates.
- `keysInjection.integration.test.ts`: compiled inline scripts contain the same key constants as the module.

### End-to-end tests

Through `am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh`: set Detail and theme, reload, and confirm persistence; repeat in a context with storage blocked (settings last for the session only, with notices where relevant); open two tabs and change a setting; export and clear from the data panel; record network traffic and assert no storage payloads are sent.

### Structured logging

JSON lines with `namespace`, `operation`, `status`, `schemaVersion`, `bytes`, `fallback`, `crossTabEvent`, `networkLeak`, `outcome`; values are never logged. Path: `artifacts/test-logs/platform-storage/<run-id>.jsonl`.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- Wrap every access, including `window.localStorage` itself, because merely touching it can throw.
- Do not use cookies as a fallback; the site sets none.
- Private notes never enter exports automatically shared elsewhere or any URL.

## Dependencies

Blocked by: `am-scaf-nextjs-app-bu2` (the application and build that host the layer).

Unblocks: `am-a11y-reading-only-6wwd` (persistent reading-only setting); `am-inst-predict-mode-ti7m` (first-visit prediction state); `am-read-notebook-tde` (notebook persistence); `am-tours-infra-g518` (local tour progress).

title: Offer save-this-chapter offline as self-contained HTML
description:
# Offer save-this-chapter offline as self-contained HTML

**Epic:** `am-ep-platform-8ci` · **Batch:** batch-i · **Priority:** P2 · **Plan sections:** §1.3, §1.7, §16.3, §16.6, §19.7 (traceability only)

## Background

Some readers have limited or intermittent connections, or want to study a chapter on a train. Before any service worker exists, the plan asks for **an explicit "save this chapter for offline reading" path: a self-contained HTML chapter with permitted figures and source references, with its size stated.** A later installable mode is separate and must not be implied. Private notes are never cached into shareable exports by default. In the innovation sequence, offline chapters are P2 and expand only after "the access need is tested and the publication and revision path is reliable."

## Scope

In scope: build-time generation of one self-contained HTML file per chapter (each paper section, and paper 4 as a whole); inlined styles, fonts subset to the chapter's glyphs, and static mathematics; all readings with offline Detail switching; static worked examples in place of instruments; rights filtering of figures; attribution, license, and revision identities; the download link with stated size.

Out of scope: the installable offline edition and service worker (`am-plat-installable-offline-oit3`); print styles (`am-plat-print-3orn`); notebook export (`am-read-notebook-tde`).

## Requirements

- **Self-contained**: one HTML file with inlined CSS, KaTeX markup, subset fonts (only glyphs used in the chapter), and permitted figures as data URIs; opening it from the file system with the network disabled makes no requests.
- **Readings**: R0 to R3 included, with Detail and margin switching by a tiny inline script and R1 visible without JavaScript.
- **Instruments**: replaced by their static worked examples with captions; no WASM or workers.
- **Rights**: only assets whose recorded publication decision allows redistribution are embedded; others are replaced by a citation and link; facsimile scans are excluded unless admitted.
- **Identity**: title, paper, section, canonical URL, generation date, `contentRevision` and `translationRevision`, license and attribution notices for text, translation, fonts, and figures.
- **Privacy**: no notebook entries, predictions, or other local data are included.
- **Download**: a "Save this chapter for offline reading" link on the section shows the file size before download; files are static, content-addressed, and cached.
- **Size budget**: a stated maximum per chapter; generation fails with a report when exceeded.

## Technical Approach

- `scripts/build-offline-chapters.ts` using compiler projections and print-safe static structure from `am-plat-print-3orn`; font subsetting per chapter from the shipped font files; output under `public/offline/<paper>/<section>-<hash>.html`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Offline files exist for the fixture chapters with stated sizes matching actual bytes.
- [ ] Opening a file from disk with networking disabled renders the chapter completely with no requests.
- [ ] Detail switching works in the file; R1 shows without JavaScript.
- [ ] A non-admitted figure is excluded and cited; attribution and revision identities are present; no local data is included.
- [ ] The size budget gate fails a seeded oversized chapter.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests

- `buildOfflineChapters.test.ts`: inlining, glyph subsetting, rights filtering, identity block, size computation and budget.

### End-to-end tests

Playwright opens generated files from `file://` in an offline context with request interception asserting zero requests, switches Detail, checks equations and figures, and runs with JavaScript disabled.

### Structured logging

JSON lines with `chapter`, `bytes`, `budgetBytes`, `fontsSubsetGlyphs`, `figuresEmbedded`, `figuresExcluded`, `requestsWhenOffline`, `jsEnabled`, `outcome`. Path: `artifacts/test-logs/platform-offline/<run-id>.jsonl`.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- Do not claim offline numerical operation; instruments are static in these files.
- Keep generated files reproducible so revisions are comparable.

## Dependencies

Blocked by: `am-plat-print-3orn` (print-safe static structure and the essential-content policy).

Unblocks: `am-plat-installable-offline-oit3` (the later installable mode builds on proven offline chapter generation).

title: Enforce the performance budgets in CI with recorded measurement conditions
description:
# Enforce the performance budgets in CI with recorded measurement conditions

**Epic:** `am-ep-platform-8ci` · **Batch:** batch-b · **Priority:** P1 · **Plan sections:** §1.5 item 6, §6.2, §12.7, §16.4, §17.4, §20 (traceability only)

## Background

"Rich UI compromises the book" is a named risk: large bundles, tiny panes, endless controls, slow hydration. The response is a set of **provisional budgets set before the reference slice and adjusted only with recorded measurements naming hardware, browser, viewport, network profile, and cache state**:

| Surface | Initial target | Measurement boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Initial reading route | No Three.js, PDF viewer, or WASM in the initial dependency graph; at most 200 KiB compressed first-route JavaScript | Cold production build, transferred script bytes |
| Reading-face HTML with all readings | 250 kB gzipped for the largest paper, else JSON fragments | Static output size in CI |
| Visible text and math | Main content in initial HTML; locally hosted subset fonts with stable fallback metrics | JavaScript disabled; cold font cache |
| Reader responsiveness | 200 ms or better interaction latency at the 75th percentile on the agreed profile | Real interactions including a detail drawer |
| Layout stability | Cumulative layout shift at most 0.1 | Initial load and deferred math activation |
| A simple analytical instrument | Parameter feedback within 100 ms once loaded | Input to accepted visible snapshot, not to pending-state paint |
| Animated instruments | 60 Hz on capable desktops; a stable 30 Hz mobile tier | Rendering measured separately from solver accuracy |
| Resource lifecycle | No growing count of workers, GPU contexts, listeners, or particle buffers across repeated route changes | Open/close and experiment-switch stress run |

**Report total transfer separately from JavaScript.** Under load, reduce visual detail, displayed particle count, resolution, or rendering frequency; **never enlarge the integration step, change the model, or reduce the statistical sample behind an inference**; rendering a subset of particles never changes the ensemble used for results.

## Scope

In scope: measurement scripts for rows one through seven; integration of the reading-face size check owned by `am-read-detail-axis-sfc`; the CI gate and its reports; performance marks the runtime must emit for instrument feedback; the measurement record format; the rule for changing budgets.

Out of scope: the resource lifecycle stress run (row eight, `am-plat-resource-stress-9zgu`); device profile decisions (`am-gov-decision-device-profiles-1zm`); fixing regressions in feature beads.

## Requirements

- **Initial route**: inspect the production module graph for the reading route to prove Three.js, pdf.js, and WASM loaders are absent; measure transferred compressed JavaScript on a cold load under the agreed network profile; fail above 200 KiB.
- **Reading face**: consume the per-paper gzipped sizes from `scripts/measure-reading-face.ts`; fail above 250 kB unless the paper uses fragments.
- **Text and math**: with JavaScript disabled and a cold font cache, assert main content and equations are present in the initial HTML and fonts are local subsets with fallback metrics.
- **Responsiveness**: scripted interactions (face switch, Detail change, opening a detail drawer, opening a clarification) measured with the Event Timing API over a fixed number of runs on the agreed profile (including CPU throttling where the profile says so); compute the 75th percentile; fail above 200 ms.
- **Layout stability**: cumulative layout shift during load and deferred math activation at most 0.1.
- **Instrument feedback**: the runtime emits performance marks carrying `instanceId` and `inputRevision` at input and at accepted visible snapshot paint; a simple analytical instrument fixture must stay within 100 ms from input to the accepted visible snapshot.
- **Animation**: frame timing measured per tier (60 Hz desktop, 30 Hz mobile) with physics accuracy measured separately and never traded for frame rate.
- **Records**: every run writes a JSON report with hardware, browser and version, viewport, network profile, cache state, build revision, and each metric with its budget; budgets change only in a commit that includes such a report and a reason.
- **Total transfer**: reported separately from JavaScript for each route measured.

## Technical Approach

- `scripts/perf/initialRouteGraph.ts`, `transferredBytes.ts`, `interactionLatency.ts`, `layoutShift.ts`, `instrumentFeedback.ts`, `frameTiming.ts`, and `report.ts`; a CI job running them against a production build; runtime performance marks added in coordination with the runtime beads.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All measurement scripts run in CI on the fixture site and produce a report with recorded conditions.
- [ ] The gate fails on seeded violations of each budget row one through seven and passes on the baseline.
- [ ] Reports list total transfer separately from JavaScript.
- [ ] A budget change without an accompanying measurement report is rejected by a repository check.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests

- Unit tests for each script's parsing and percentile computation using recorded fixture traces.
- `initialRouteGraph.integration.test.ts`: detects a seeded import of Three.js into the reading route.
- `budgetChangeCheck.test.ts`: the repository check requires a report when budget constants change.

### End-to-end tests

Through `am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh` against a production build: run the full suite on the Brownian slice pages and a fixture instrument, cold and warm caches, desktop and mobile profiles.

### Structured logging

JSON lines per metric with `metric`, `value`, `budget`, `unit`, `route`, `profile`, `cacheState`, `buildRevision`, `runs`, `percentile`, `outcome`; full reports at `artifacts/budgets/perf-<run-id>.json`.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- Laboratory measurements approximate field experience; state the profile and do not claim real-user performance.
- Under load the fix is always visual; never "improve" a budget by coarsening physics or sampling.

## Dependencies

Blocked by: `am-gov-decision-device-profiles-1zm` (the agreed hardware, browser, viewport, network, and cache profiles); `am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh` (browser automation and logging); `am-read-detail-axis-sfc` (the reading-face size check).

Unblocks: `am-launch-readiness-audit-sc9b` (performance budgets are launch criteria).

Added during graph review (blocked by):
- `am-rt-worker-scheduler-7tl`: budget runs read runtime timing marks from the scheduler.

title: Build the print policy and print styles for coherent chapters
description:
# Build the print policy and print styles for coherent chapters

**Epic:** `am-ep-platform-8ci` · **Batch:** batch-c · **Priority:** P1 · **Plan sections:** §1.5 item 6, §6.2, §15.4, §15.5, §16.3, §17.4, §21 (traceability only)

## Background

The book must work as a book, including on paper. The plan: **"Print produces a coherent chapter with equations, source references, visible explanations, and representative figures with captions for interactive states; hidden drawers have a deliberate print policy (essential explanations expanded, collapsed headings never printed alone)."** Browser acceptance adds: **print output with complete prose, uncut equations, expanded essential explanations, and static representations of the chosen state.** Classrooms, reviewers, and readers who study away from screens depend on this.

## Scope

In scope: the print stylesheet; the essential-for-print content flag and its policy; static snapshots of instrument states with captions; source references and link targets in print; page-break rules for equations, figures, and callouts; monochrome safety; print acceptance tests.

Out of scope: offline chapter files (`am-plat-offline-chapter-un8i`); capstone worksheet print views (`am-disc-capstones-infra-3352`); layout on screen (`am-read-page-anatomy-l0b`).

## Requirements

- **What prints**: the paper section at the reader's current Detail; source references (printed *Annalen* page numbers and section anchors); footnotes; essential explanations expanded; derivation chains marked essential expanded; misconception callouts collapsed unless essential; non-essential drawers omitted entirely, headings included (a collapsed heading never prints alone).
- **Essential flag**: explanation units, derivation chains, and callouts carry an authored `essentialForPrint` flag with a default by type; the compiler reports sections whose printed form would lose a required step.
- **Equations**: never split across pages or clipped; long equations use authored line breaks in print; KaTeX fonts print crisply.
- **Instruments**: on `beforeprint`, each visible instrument is replaced by a static representation of its current accepted state (SVG clone or raster of the canvas) with a caption naming the instrument, the key parameters, the seed and stream version where relevant, the snapshot identity, the execution label, and the words "static representation of an interactive state." Without JavaScript, the static worked example prints instead.
- **Links**: link targets print as footnoted URLs or an end list, never as bare underlined text with no destination.
- **Chrome**: navigation, palettes, controls, and compasses do not print.
- **Color**: semantic color identity survives monochrome through the non-color cues.
- **Page flow**: sensible widows and orphans control; running heads with paper and section where the browser supports paged media.

## Technical Approach

- `src/platform/print/print.css`, `beforePrint.ts` (instrument snapshot replacement and restoration after print), compiler flag defaults and a coverage check `printCoverage.ts`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A Brownian §4 print output contains the complete prose at the chosen Detail, all equations uncut, essential explanations expanded, footnotes, source references, and a captioned static figure of BM-06's current state with its snapshot identity.
- [ ] Non-essential collapsed headings do not print.
- [ ] Links show their destinations; chrome is absent; monochrome output keeps role identity.
- [ ] JavaScript-disabled print shows static worked examples in place of instruments.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests

- `printCoverage.test.ts`: sections losing required steps in print are reported.
- `beforePrint.test.ts`: snapshot replacement and restoration with the real snapshot store and a fixture instrument.

### End-to-end tests

Through `am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh`: print emulation and `page.pdf()` for fixture chapters; extract text from the generated PDF (the site's own output, not OCR of scans) and compare with essential HTML text; render PDF pages to images for layout review of equation integrity; assert collapsed headings absent; verify figure captions include snapshot ids; JavaScript-disabled print.

### Structured logging

JSON lines with `route`, `detail`, `pages`, `missingEssentialText`, `equationsSplit`, `figuresCaptioned`, `snapshotVersions`, `jsEnabled`, `outcome`. Path: `artifacts/test-logs/platform-print/<run-id>.jsonl`; generated PDFs retained on failure under `artifacts/print/`.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- A printed animation frame is not evidence; captions must say what the figure is.
- Do not print every hidden reading; print the chosen Detail and essentials.

## Dependencies

Blocked by: `am-read-detail-axis-sfc` (reading structure and Detail state); `am-read-page-anatomy-l0b` (layout structure the print styles override).

Unblocks: `am-plat-offline-chapter-un8i` (offline chapters reuse print-safe static structure); `am-disc-capstones-infra-3352` (capstone print views); `am-launch-readiness-audit-sc9b` (print is a launch criterion).

Added during graph review (blocked by):
- `am-eq-static-katex-7da`: printed equations come from the static KaTeX output.

title: Run the resource-lifecycle stress test across route and experiment switches
description:
# Run the resource-lifecycle stress test across route and experiment switches

**Epic:** `am-ep-platform-8ci` · **Batch:** batch-c · **Priority:** P1 · **Plan sections:** §12.5–§12.9, §16.4 (resource lifecycle row), §17.4 (traceability only)

## Background

Interactive physics pages leak in ways unit tests miss: a worker survives a route change, a WebGL context is never released, a particle buffer is retained by a closure, a store subscription duplicates on remount, or a presentation change quietly consumes random draws. The budget row is explicit: **no growing count of workers, GPU contexts, listeners, or particle buffers across repeated route changes**, measured by an **open/close and experiment-switch stress run**. The runtime contract adds that mount and unmount probes, repeated subscriptions, and route transitions must not create duplicate stepping owners, leak workers, or advance randomness, and that switching between 2D and 3D must not restart physics, duplicate the owner, or consume new randomness. Browser acceptance also requires that two instances of the same experiment do not interfere and that worker refusal, unavailable WASM, stale responses, context loss, and restart never produce false results.

## Scope

In scope: a diagnostics hook enabled only in test builds; the stress scenario; pass criteria and thresholds; the CI job and report.

Out of scope: fixing leaks (owning feature beads); lifecycle implementation (`am-rt-memory-lifecycle-5ws`); budget rows one through seven (`am-plat-perf-budgets-s3ww`).

## Requirements

- **Diagnostics hook** (test builds only, absent from production bundles): active workers from the runtime registry; stepping owners per `instanceId`; store subscriptions; WebGL contexts created, lost, and disposed; Three.js renderer memory counts (geometries, textures, programs) where scenes exist; tracked listeners; particle and typed buffers by bytes; per-stream random draw counters; JavaScript heap samples after forced garbage collection in Chromium.
- **Scenario** (repeated for a stated number of cycles, 50 by default): open BM-01 and run it; switch faces; open BM-06; toggle 2D and 3D where a studio exists; navigate to another paper and back; close laboratories; open two instances of one experiment side by side and operate both; inject WebGL context loss and worker termination; force a stale response and a refusal.
- **Pass criteria**: counts of workers, owners, subscriptions, contexts, tracked listeners, and buffers return to baseline after each cycle; heap growth after garbage collection stays under a stated slope; random draw counters do not change on face, presentation, or observer changes; `runId` stays constant across face changes; exactly one owner exists per `instanceId`; the two instances never share state; recovery paths show refusals or new visible runs, never false values.
- **Report**: JSON with per-cycle counts, thresholds, and violations; runs nightly and before release candidates.

## Technical Approach

- `src/testing/diagnostics/registry.ts` (compiled out of production), `scripts/stress/resourceLifecycle.ts` (Playwright with the Chrome DevTools Protocol for garbage collection and heap samples), thresholds in `scripts/stress/thresholds.json`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The diagnostics hook exists only in test builds (bundle check).
- [ ] The full scenario runs against the Brownian slice and passes all criteria; seeded leaks (an undisposed worker, a duplicate subscription, a draw on face change) each fail with a named violation.
- [ ] Reports are produced nightly and attached to release candidates.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests

- `registry.test.ts`: counters increment and decrement correctly for fixture owners, workers, and buffers.
- `productionBundle.test.ts`: the diagnostics module is absent from production output.

### End-to-end tests

The stress scenario itself, plus seeded-leak variants, in Chromium (heap sampling), Firefox, and WebKit (counts without heap sampling).

### Structured logging

JSON lines per cycle with `cycle`, `workers`, `owners`, `subscriptions`, `webglContexts`, `threeGeometries`, `threeTextures`, `listeners`, `bufferBytes`, `heapBytesAfterGc`, `rngDrawDelta`, `runIdStable`, `violations`, `browser`, `outcome`. Path: `artifacts/test-logs/platform-stress/<run-id>.jsonl`; heap snapshots retained on failure.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- React development double mounting must not be mistaken for leaks; run against production-mode builds with the diagnostics hook.
- A depleted budget may reduce visual detail, never change diffusivity or skip scientific time.

## Dependencies

Blocked by: `am-rt-memory-lifecycle-5ws` (disposal and buffer ownership under test); `am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh` (automation and logging); `am-bm-01-tracer-ensemble-hdly` (the first heavy instrument to stress).

Unblocks: `am-launch-readiness-audit-sc9b` (the resource lifecycle budget is a launch criterion).

title: Build the build-time search index and offline command palette
description:
# Build the build-time search index and offline command palette

**Epic:** `am-ep-platform-8ci` · **Batch:** batch-c · **Priority:** P1 · **Plan sections:** §2.3, §4.7, §6.9, §16.1, §16.4, §16.6 (traceability only)

## Background

Readers search the way they think, not the way the papers are indexed. The plan asks for a search that **indexes both everyday language and technical terms**:

- "how far does it wander" leads to RMS displacement;
- "clocks disagree" finds simultaneity and synchronization;
- `βν` finds the quantum energy;
- `0.8 μ` finds paper 2 §5;
- `Besso` finds the closing line of paper 3.

Sections, sentences (German and English), equations by symbol and printed number, results, argument nodes, instruments, foundations, misconceptions, glossary terms, timeline cards, and people are **indexed at build time into a client-side index (MiniSearch or FlexSearch), so ⌘K works offline and without a server.** The default reader does not need the index to find the four papers or their outlines, and **browser text search must still find the full section, so paragraphs are not virtualized out of the DOM.**

The donor has a search palette (`src/components/layout/PatentSearchPalette.tsx` with a test, opened from `Header.tsx`) that this bead adapts; the donor does not use a dedicated search library.

## Scope

In scope: choosing and pinning the index library; `scripts/build-search-index.ts`; document types and fields; everyday-language alias tables; symbol and notation-aware normalization; German normalization; lazy index loading and size limits; the adapted command palette; result grouping with scope labels; privacy of queries.

Out of scope: content compilation (`am-cm-compiler-core-oa7`); the `/notation` page (`am-not-notation-page-2us`); outlines and anchors (`am-read-anchors-navigation-a6o`).

## Requirements

### Index contents

Documents for: sections; German and English sentences; equations (printed number, printed and modern symbols, spoken form); results; argument nodes; instruments (id, name, question); foundations; misconceptions (tempting claim text); glossary terms (term annotations and concordance entries); timeline cards; people. Each document carries its anchor, face, paper, section, language, and type.

### Everyday language and notation

- An authored alias table (`content/search/aliases.yaml`) maps everyday phrases to targets, covering at least the five plan examples, each with a test.
- Symbol normalization treats Greek letters and their names equivalently (β and "beta"), separates the micro sign from Greek mu while matching both for "μ" queries, handles primes and subscripts (`λ_x`, `λx`), and understands spaced unit forms (`0.8 μ`, `0.8 µm`).
- Scope labels distinguish meanings of the same glyph: a query for β returns Wien's constant in paper 1 and the Lorentz factor in papers 3 and 4, each labeled.

### German

- Case folding, umlaut folding (ä also matches ae and a), ß matching ss, and prefix matching for compound words; results show their language.

### Loading and budgets

- The index is not part of the initial route; it loads when the palette opens (or on idle after first interaction), is content-addressed, and splits by paper or type if its compressed size exceeds a stated budget.
- Once loaded, search works with the network disconnected.

### Palette

- Opens with ⌘K on macOS and Ctrl+K elsewhere, plus a visible search button; follows the WAI-ARIA combobox and listbox pattern; arrow keys, Enter, and Escape; results grouped by type with scope labels; selecting a result navigates to the anchor and face.
- Queries are never sent anywhere and never logged outside local test runs.

## Technical Approach

- `scripts/build-search-index.ts` consuming compiler projections; `src/search/normalize.ts` (symbols, German), `aliases.ts`, `query.ts`; `src/components/layout/SearchPalette.tsx` adapted from the donor with license notice; library choice recorded with `am-gov-decision-stack-versions-6ax`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The five plan example queries return the expected top results in fixture tests.
- [ ] β returns both scoped meanings with labels; German folding works for umlauts and ß.
- [ ] The initial route contains no index data; after the palette loads the index, search works offline.
- [ ] The palette passes keyboard and screen-reader combobox checks.
- [ ] No network request carries a query.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests

- `normalize.test.ts`: Greek names, micro sign versus mu, primes and subscripts, unit spacing, German folding.
- `aliases.test.ts`: every alias resolves to an existing target.
- `query.integration.test.ts`: a fixture index built from the fixture corpus answers the plan examples and scope-labeled symbol queries.
- `buildIndex.test.ts`: document counts per type; size report; split behavior over budget.

### End-to-end tests

Through `am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh`: open with ⌘K and Ctrl+K; run the five examples; navigate to a result and confirm the anchor and face; disconnect the network after loading and search again; verify the initial bundle excludes the index; keyboard only and screen-reader smoke check; 320 px.

### Structured logging

JSON lines with `queryFixtureId` (never raw user queries outside tests), `topResultIds`, `expectedId`, `rank`, `indexBytes`, `loadedLazily`, `offline`, `outcome`. Path: `artifacts/test-logs/platform-search/<run-id>.jsonl`.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- Search must never become the only way to find the papers; outlines and `/papers` remain primary.
- Keep the alias table editorial and reviewed; it teaches as much as it finds.

## Dependencies

Blocked by: `am-cm-compiler-core-oa7` (compiled documents to index); `am-scaf-extract-ui-components-c31` (the donor search palette extracted with license notices).

Unblocks: `am-not-notation-page-2us` (the searchable concordance uses the same index); `am-launch-readiness-audit-sc9b` (search is a launch criterion of the book working as a book).

title: Harden inputs, KaTeX trust, URL state, CSP, WASM loading, and third-party exclusion
description:
# Harden inputs, KaTeX trust, URL state, CSP, WASM loading, and third-party exclusion

**Epic:** `am-ep-platform-8ci` · **Batch:** batch-c · **Priority:** P1 · **Plan sections:** §12.7, §12.10, §16.5, §16.6 (traceability only)

## Background

"Imported text, bibliographic data, URL state, and reader notes are untrusted input." The plan requires a closed content schema and sanitized rendering; no evaluation of user expressions as JavaScript (the exercise checker parses a tiny grammar, never `eval`); KaTeX trust kept narrowly scoped so a source record cannot inject HTML, CSS, links, or image loads through mathematics; validated generated classes and data attributes; capped macro expansion and size; no raw error strings; bounded URL-state size, particle counts, iteration counts, and numeric inputs; cancellable heavy calculations so a malicious or accidental preset cannot freeze the page; trusted build provenance for content-addressed WASM; `application/wasm` for streaming instantiation; a Content-Security-Policy verified with the real loading path; no broad `unsafe-eval`; and CSP and worker loading tested in supported browsers. Privacy adds: no third-party scripts, fingerprinting, advertising, or cookies.

## Scope

In scope: site-wide security headers and CSP; sanitization rules for content rendering; input and URL-state bounds; adversarial preset tests; WASM serving and provenance checks; third-party and cookie exclusion checks; dependency auditing; an error-message policy.

Out of scope: the KaTeX trust callback implementation (`am-eq-static-katex-7da`); the exercise grammar (`am-disc-exercise-checker-i4h2`); tape parsing (`am-inst-permalink-tape-s677`); worker chunking (`am-rt-worker-scheduler-7tl`); release manifests (`am-rel-release-manifest-3gna`).

## Requirements

- **CSP** (verified in Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit): `default-src 'self'`; `script-src 'self'` plus hashes for the inline pre-paint scripts, adding `'wasm-unsafe-eval'` only if the chosen WASM path requires it and never `'unsafe-eval'`; `worker-src 'self'`; `connect-src 'self'`; `img-src 'self' data:`; `font-src 'self'`; `object-src 'none'`; `base-uri 'self'`; `form-action 'self'`; `frame-ancestors 'none'` except on `/embed/lab/*`, which allows embedding. Record the decision for KaTeX inline style attributes (for example a narrow `style-src-attr` allowance) with its reasoning.
- **Headers**: `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, a strict `Referrer-Policy`, a minimal `Permissions-Policy` (no camera, microphone, or geolocation; the kitchen mode reads local files, not live capture), and `application/wasm` for `.wasm` files.
- **Content rendering**: the constrained Markdown renderer allows a fixed element set; links must be relative anchors or `https` URLs; no inline event handlers, `style` attributes from content, or raw HTML; math goes only through the static KaTeX pipeline.
- **No dynamic code**: a lint and a build scan reject `eval`, `new Function`, and string-based timers in application code.
- **Bounds**: maximum lengths for every state parameter (`view`, `panes`, `detail`, `lens`, `notation`, `open`, `page`, `tape`), maximum particle counts (for example the BM-01 ensemble at 10 000), iteration and time-horizon limits, and numeric ranges from parameter schemas; oversized or invalid values are ignored or refused with an explanation, never crash the page.
- **Adversarial presets**: crafted URLs that request extreme ensembles, huge tapes, deep clarification stacks, or pathological ranges stay responsive, because heavy work runs in bounded, cancellable worker chunks.
- **WASM provenance**: served artifacts match release-manifest digests; a mismatch refuses to load and the laboratory shows "unavailable," never a silent fallback labeled as FrankenSim.
- **Third parties and cookies**: a build and deployment check rejects external script, style, font, or connect origins and any `Set-Cookie` header; no analytics or advertising libraries; dependency vulnerability audit in CI.
- **Errors**: readers see ordinary-language messages; raw error strings and stack traces never render.

## Technical Approach

- Header and CSP configuration in the Next.js and Vercel configuration with hashes emitted by the build; `src/platform/security/sanitizeMarkdown.ts`; `bounds.ts` shared with URL parsers; `scripts/security/scanBuild.ts` (dynamic code, external origins, cookies); Playwright CSP-violation listeners.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] CSP and headers are applied; no violations occur across the fixture site in three browsers, including worker, WASM, and pdf.js loading.
- [ ] The content security suite rejects injected HTML, CSS, links, images, and event handlers in content and math.
- [ ] Every state parameter enforces its bound; adversarial preset URLs keep the page responsive.
- [ ] A digest-mismatched WASM fixture refuses to load with an honest label.
- [ ] Build scans find no dynamic code, external origins, or cookies; the dependency audit passes.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests

- `sanitizeMarkdown.test.ts`: allowed and rejected constructs.
- `bounds.test.ts`: each parameter at, below, and above its limit, including malformed encodings.
- `scanBuild.test.ts`: seeded `eval`, external script tag, and cookie header each fail.

### End-to-end tests

Through `am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh`: record `securitypolicyviolation` events on every lane and fail on any; load adversarial URLs and assert responsiveness (input latency and worker cancellation); load a mismatched WASM digest; check response headers for HTML, WASM, fonts, and images.

### Structured logging

JSON lines with `check`, `route`, `browser`, `violationDirective`, `blockedUri`, `parameter`, `inputLength`, `responsiveMs`, `wasmDigestMatch`, `outcome`. Path: `artifacts/test-logs/platform-security/<run-id>.jsonl`.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- The embed route legitimately needs framing; scope the exception to that route only.
- Security checks must run against the deployed candidate as well as local builds, since hosting configuration can change headers.

## Dependencies

Blocked by: `am-eq-static-katex-7da` (math trust policy); `am-rt-worker-scheduler-7tl` (cancellable bounded work); `am-fs-slim-artifact-0yh` (content-addressed WASM and digests); `am-inst-permalink-tape-s677` (the largest URL state).

Unblocks: `am-launch-readiness-audit-sc9b` (security is a launch criterion).

title: Keep stable anchors across faces with alias redirects, outline, and scroll restoration
description:
# Keep stable anchors across faces with alias redirects, outline, and scroll restoration

**Epic:** `am-ep-reader-k0z` · **Batch:** batch-b · **Priority:** P0 · **Plan sections:** §6.8, §6.9, §11.2, §11.3, §15.4, §22.5 (traceability only)

## Background

A reader should be able to share a link to one sentence of the relativity paper, open it in the German face, switch to the English face, and still be looking at that sentence. The plan makes this a structural rule: every section, paragraph, sentence, equation, result, argument node, and instrument has a **stable anchor derived from the printed structure**, anchors are **identical across faces**, and anchors are **content ids, never array positions**. Once published, a source-block id never changes because a paragraph is inserted into an explanation or split for translation; retired or split nodes keep explicit aliases.

The donor keyed parallel readings by block index, so inserting a paragraph shifted every annotation after it. This bead makes navigation robust to editing, face switching, split view, and history.

## Scope

In scope: anchor emission on every face; place-keeping on face switches; nearest-ancestor mapping when a face lacks the exact target; alias anchors for retired and split ids; the section outline; hash navigation with focus management; scroll restoration across back and forward; unique DOM ids in split view.

Out of scope: the id grammar and alias registry (`am-cm-id-scheme-8bn`); recursive clarification history (`am-read-return-stack-oxa`); page layout of the outline (`am-read-page-anatomy-l0b`); face contents (face beads).

## Requirements

- **Anchor grammar** (from the naming conventions): `#s<n>`, `#s<n>-p<m>`, `#s<n>-p<m>-s<k>`, `#eq-<printed number>` or `#eq-s<n>-d<j>` for an unnumbered display equation, `#result-<slug>`, `#arg-<id>`, `#lab-<id>`. Paper 4 has no sections and uses `s0`.
- **Same anchors on every face.** The German, English, gloss, parallel, reading, and results faces emit the same content ids for the same units. Where a face does not contain a unit (the results face has no sentences), navigation maps to the **nearest ancestor or linked unit** present (sentence to paragraph to section; a section to the results derived in it).
- **Place-keeping.** Before a face change, the shell records the topmost substantially visible anchor; after the new face renders, it scrolls that anchor (or its mapped ancestor) into the same relative viewport position.
- **Split view uniqueness.** DOM ids must be unique. The primary pane uses bare ids; the secondary pane uses a pane prefix (for example `pane-b--s3-p2`) plus `data-anchor="s3-p2"`, and hash navigation resolves through `data-anchor` in the focused pane.
- **Aliases.** For each retired or split id, emit a static alias anchor element at the new location so old links work without JavaScript; with JavaScript, rewrite `location.hash` to the current id with `history.replaceState` and record the rewrite for diagnostics.
- **Outline.** A narrow section outline lists sections with the current section indicated, is keyboard operable, and never consumes a third full column on desktop (it collapses into a menu on phones).
- **Hash navigation and focus.** Navigating to an anchor moves keyboard focus to the target's heading or container (with `tabindex="-1"` where needed), accounts for sticky headers with `scroll-margin-top`, and briefly marks the target with an outline and a text cue, never color alone.
- **Scroll restoration.** Back and forward restore the face, the anchor, and the relative scroll position.
- **No-JavaScript.** Anchors, alias anchors, and outline links work as plain HTML.

## Technical Approach

- `src/reader/anchors/emitAnchor.ts` (used by every face renderer), `mapToFace.ts` (nearest-ancestor mapping from the compiler's structure index), `placeKeeper.ts`, `aliases.ts` (reads the alias registry at build time and emits static alias anchors), and `Outline.tsx`.
- The compiler provides a per-paper structure index (section, paragraph, sentence, equation, result, argument, lab ids with parent links and cross-links to results).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every face emits anchors from the grammar for the fixture corpus; a DOM uniqueness test passes in single and split views.
- [ ] Deep link `#s4-p2-s1` on the English face, then a switch to German, shows the same sentence in place; a switch to results shows the section's results.
- [ ] A retired id from the alias fixture lands on its new location with JavaScript disabled and is rewritten with JavaScript enabled.
- [ ] Back and forward restore face, anchor, and position; focus lands on navigation targets.
- [ ] The outline tracks the current section and is keyboard operable at desktop and 320 px.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests

- `emitAnchor.test.ts`: grammar for sections, paragraphs, sentences, numbered and unnumbered equations, results, arguments, labs; paper 4 `s0`.
- `mapToFace.test.ts`: nearest-ancestor and result mapping over the fixture structure index.
- `aliases.test.ts`: alias anchors emitted at new locations; split ids map to the first successor with a note.
- `domIds.integration.test.ts`: rendered static HTML for single and split views has no duplicate ids.

### End-to-end tests

Through `am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh`: deep-link and face-switch journeys on desktop, tablet, and 320 px; split-view hash navigation within the secondary pane; alias link with JavaScript disabled and enabled; back and forward restoration; keyboard-only focus landing; reduced-motion lane (no smooth-scroll animation).

### Structured logging

JSON lines with `paper`, `fromFace`, `toFace`, `anchorBefore`, `anchorAfter`, `mappedTo`, `aliasRewrite`, `scrollDeltaPx`, `focusTarget`, `jsEnabled`, `viewport`, `outcome`. Path: `artifacts/test-logs/reader-anchors/<run-id>.jsonl`.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- Never derive ids from array positions or rendering order.
- A sentence split in translation keeps its source id with suffixes on the English side; English sentences must map back to the German source id when switching faces.
- Smooth scrolling is disabled under reduced motion.

## Dependencies

Blocked by: `am-read-shell-routes-3ua` (faces and routes that emit anchors); `am-cm-id-scheme-8bn` (the grammar and alias registry).

Unblocks: `am-read-return-stack-oxa` (frames are anchored by content id); `am-tours-infra-g518` (tours are ordered anchor lists).

title: Build the German, English, and parallel faces with sentence-alignment highlighting, notes, and footnotes
description:
# Build the German, English, and parallel faces with sentence-alignment highlighting, notes, and footnotes

**Epic:** `am-ep-reader-k0z` · **Batch:** batch-b · **Priority:** P0 · **Plan sections:** §1.2, §1.4 items 1–2, §3.2, §4.3–§4.5, §6.9, §11.2, §11.3, §17.3, §17.4, §19.1 (traceability only)

## Background

No existing English translation of these papers sits next to the German, sentence by sentence. The site publishes its own translation made from the public-domain German and presents it as a **bilingual archival edition**. Three faces carry it:

| `view` | Face | Content |
|---|---|---|
| `german` | Source face | The German edition, term annotations, numbered equations as printed, continuous reading with no scan-page furniture |
| `english` | Translation face | The aligned English; focusing a sentence highlights its German source on the other face |
| `parallel` | Bilingual face | German and English side by side (stacked at narrow widths), sentence-aligned, with the current paragraph's reading in a companion column |

The separation of layers is strict. The reviewed German ledger with page markers is research evidence, not the source face. Explanations may reorganize and modernize but never masquerade as source text. **Notation is not translated**: every symbol stays as printed on both faces. Machine-drafted material is never marked reviewed because a schema or renderer accepted it, and Batch A's exit evidence explicitly requires that **drafts are visibly distinguished from reviewed translations**.

## Scope

In scope: rendering source blocks (masthead, headings, paragraphs, equations, footnotes and footnote marks, closing) and translation units; many-to-many sentence alignment highlighting; term annotations; editorial notes and correction markers; source locators linking to the facsimile; review-state display; language metadata; footnote navigation; static output.

Out of scope: alignment data and edition tests (`am-edn-alignment-tooling-do1`); German edition and translation content (editions beads); the gloss face (`am-read-gloss-face-lp2`); the facsimile viewer (`am-read-facsimile-face-er0`); the result weave (`am-read-result-weave-jex`); readings rendering in the companion column (`am-read-detail-axis-sfc`).

## Requirements

### Source face (`german`)

- Render blocks in order with their anchors: masthead (title and author line as printed, "von A. Einstein"), headings, paragraphs, display equations with printed equation numbers, footnote marks and footnotes, acknowledgments, and the closing date-line exactly as printed (for example "Bern, den 17. März 1905").
- Continuous reading: no ledger page markers, running heads, or other scan furniture; a build-time scan rejects `--- REVIEWED TRANSCRIPTION PAGE` and similar markers in face HTML.
- Original spelling and typography are retained as transcribed (for example `daß`); letter-spaced emphasis (Sperrsatz) is rendered as semantic emphasis with a style echoing the print.
- Term annotations mark period words with authored, occurrence-specific definitions longer than 80 characters (for example *Lichtkomplex*, *molekularkinetische Theorie der Wärme*, *ruhendes System*, *Elementarquantum*, *Kathodenstrahlen*, *Lichtäther*, *Beobachter*, *Trägheit*, *Energieinhalt*); annotations open on activation with keyboard and touch, never as tooltip-only content.

### Translation face (`english`)

- Render translation units in source order with suffixed sentence ids where a German sentence was split.
- Display equations reuse the same equation component and markup as the German face (the compiler already enforces byte-identical equation blocks).
- Unresolved alternative readings appear in internal review builds; where editors publish them, they render as an editorial note.

### Parallel face (`parallel`)

- German and English side by side on wide screens, stacked per paragraph at narrow widths, aligned by sentence groups rather than by paragraph counts; the current paragraph's reading appears in the companion column at the reader's Detail.

### Alignment highlighting

- Focusing, hovering, or tapping a sentence highlights all aligned sentences in the other language (one to many and many to one), with an outline and a text marker, never color alone.
- Keyboard users navigate sentences inside a paragraph with a roving focus mode entered from the paragraph, not by tabbing through every sentence; an action "Show the German source of this sentence" announces the aligned text on demand.

### Notes, corrections, and locators

- Editorial notes of kinds historian's margin, correction, typographical, dispute, and side note render as marked margin items linked to their blocks.
- A suspected historical typographical error keeps the original reading in the source view; a corrected reading may be offered only with an explicit marker; translation corrections keep their own history.
- Each block can reveal its source locator (printed *Annalen* page and PDF page) linking to that page on the facsimile face.

### Review state

- Every translation unit carries its review state (machine draft, edited draft, reviewed with reviewer and date). Drafts carry a visible, non-alarming marker; a paper whose translation is not yet reviewed shows a banner on the English and parallel faces.

### Language and access

- `lang="de"` on German content and `lang="en"` on English content, with language-appropriate hyphenation; direction metadata is honored when later editions need it.
- Footnote marks link to footnotes and back; locators are reachable by keyboard.
- Everything renders statically; highlighting hydrates.

## Technical Approach

- `src/reader/faces/GermanFace.tsx`, `EnglishFace.tsx`, `ParallelFace.tsx`, sharing `SourceBlock.tsx`, `TranslationUnit.tsx`, `TermAnnotation.tsx`, `EditorialNoteMarker.tsx`, `Footnote.tsx`; `alignmentHighlight.ts` island reading the compiled alignment index for the paper.
- Route-local payloads from the compiler contain blocks, units, alignment edges, notes, locators, and review states for one paper.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The Brownian §§4–5 fixture renders on all three faces with anchors, printed equation numbers, footnotes, term annotations, and the date-line.
- [ ] No scan furniture appears in any face's HTML (build scan passes; a seeded marker fails).
- [ ] Alignment highlighting works for one-to-one, one-to-two, and two-to-one fixtures in both directions, with keyboard access.
- [ ] Machine drafts and reviewed units are visibly distinguished; the unreviewed-paper banner appears when applicable.
- [ ] Equations render identically on German and English faces; footnotes round-trip; locators open the facsimile page.
- [ ] 320 px stacked parallel layout and JavaScript-disabled reading pass.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests

- `SourceBlock.render.test.tsx` and `TranslationUnit.render.test.tsx`: every block kind with fixture payloads; `lang` attributes; review-state markers.
- `alignmentHighlight.test.ts`: highlight sets for many-to-many fixtures; stable snapshots.
- `noScanFurniture.integration.test.ts`: scans compiled face HTML for ledger markers and running heads.
- `footnotes.test.tsx`: mark-to-note-to-mark navigation.

### End-to-end tests

In `am-bm-slice-e2e-sbqu` and a reader lane: focus an English §4 sentence and assert the German source highlight; split-sentence fixture; open a term annotation by keyboard and touch; follow a locator to the facsimile page; parallel face at 320 px; JavaScript-disabled lane; screen-reader smoke check of the "Show the German source" action.

### Structured logging

JSON lines with `paper`, `face`, `sentenceId`, `alignedIds`, `highlightCount`, `reviewState`, `annotationId`, `footnoteRoundTrip`, `viewport`, `jsEnabled`, `outcome`. Path: `artifacts/test-logs/reader-bilingual/<run-id>.jsonl`.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- Never silently replace printed symbols (for example $V$ with $c$) in either face; notation modernization belongs only to explanation faces.
- Alignment is many-to-many; never rely on matching paragraph or sentence counts.
- A reviewed state requires a named reviewer and date recorded in the provenance receipt; the renderer must not infer "reviewed" from the absence of a draft flag.

## Dependencies

Blocked by: `am-read-shell-routes-3ua` (the faces live in the shell); `am-edn-alignment-tooling-do1` (alignment data, segmentation, and edition checks).

Unblocks: `am-read-gloss-face-lp2` (reuses source rendering); `am-read-result-weave-jex` (lights these sentences); `am-found-reading-german-u8oc` (links into the source face); `am-bm-slice-e2e-sbqu` (the slice journey reads the source).

title: Render all four readings statically with the pre-paint detail script, budget check, and JSON-fragment fallback
description:
# Render all four readings statically with the pre-paint detail script, budget check, and JSON-fragment fallback

**Epic:** `am-ep-reader-k0z` · **Batch:** batch-b · **Priority:** P0 · **Plan sections:** §6.1, §6.2, §16.2, §16.4, §16.5, §19.7 (traceability only)

## Background

Every paragraph, equation, and instrument caption has four authored readings:

| Reading | Name | Assumes | Style |
|---|---|---|---|
| R0 | Overview ("in one breath") | Nothing | One or two sentences; true and complete at its resolution |
| R1 | Full explanation (default) | Calculus, basic linear algebra, basic probability, the ideal gas law | The site's main voice |
| R2 | Show every step | High-school algebra and willingness to read slowly (with the zero-algebra layer embedded where needed) | Every symbol defined, every step shown, every "it follows that" expanded |
| R3 | Historian's margin (modern lens) | R1 | What Einstein wrote, where the argument is heuristic, later changes, priority, cited |

R0 to R2 form the **Detail** axis; R3 is the **Perspective** axis's annotation layer. The site is statically generated, so the Detail choice cannot be a server-read cookie. The plan specifies the mechanism exactly: **all readings are rendered into the static HTML of every paragraph, with R1 visible and the others carrying `data-detail` and `hidden`; a two-line inline script in `<head>` reads `localStorage` and the `?detail=` parameter and sets `data-detail` on `<html>` before first paint (the same trick the theme toggle uses); CSS shows the matching reading.** Consequences: the axis works with JavaScript disabled (R1), search engines index every reading, switching is instant and offline, and `?detail=2` permalinks open at that reading with `rel=canonical` omitting the parameter.

The cost is HTML that grows three to four times. **The budget is 250 kB gzipped for the largest paper's reading face, checked in CI.** If a paper exceeds it, that section's R2 and R3 texts are fetched from a static JSON fragment on first expansion, with **real links, not inert buttons,** for readers without JavaScript.

## Scope

In scope: static emission of R0 to R3 for paragraphs, equations, and captions; the pre-paint script and CSS; the reader control for Detail; per-paragraph deeper reading; URL and storage synchronization; the budget measurement script and CI gate; the JSON-fragment fallback; static fallback pages for readers without JavaScript; canonical handling.

Out of scope: authoring readings (paper readings beads); the Perspective toggle's UI and R3 presentation choices (`am-read-perspective-toggle-abd`, which reuses this mechanism with `data-perspective`); the reading-only setting (`am-a11y-reading-only-6wwd`); site-wide performance budgets beyond this check (`am-plat-perf-budgets-s3ww`).

## Requirements

### Static emission

- For each readable unit, emit one container with anchor id and child blocks `data-reading="0|1|2|3"`. R1 is visible by default; R0, R2, and R3 carry `hidden`.
- Exactly one of R0, R1, or R2 is visible per unit under a Detail setting; R3 visibility follows the Perspective setting.
- Equations and instrument captions follow the same structure.

### Pre-paint script and CSS

- The inline head script reads `?detail=` (accepting `0`, `1`, `2`), then `localStorage` (wrapped in try and catch, so blocked or full storage falls back to R1), and sets `data-detail` on `<html>`.
