It is tiny, dependency-free, and allowed by the Content-Security-Policy through a hash, never through broad `unsafe-inline` (`am-plat-security-f644` owns the policy; this bead supplies the hash in a build artifact).
- CSS reveals the matching reading and hides the default R1 when another level is chosen (author CSS overrides the `hidden` attribute's user-agent `display: none`).
- A `?detail=` parameter wins for the visit; a reader's explicit change persists to storage when available and updates the URL with `history.replaceState` so the address stays shareable without new history entries.

### Per-paragraph deeper reading

- A reader can open a single unit at a deeper reading without changing the global choice ("show me every step for this one"). With JavaScript, this sets a local attribute on the unit.
- Without JavaScript, the control is a real link to a statically generated section page rendered at that Detail (see fallback pages below), anchored to the unit.

### Budget and fragment fallback

- `scripts/measure-reading-face.ts` builds each paper's reading face HTML with all readings and reports raw and gzipped bytes per paper and per section; CI fails when any paper exceeds 250 kB gzipped unless that paper uses fragments.
- When a paper exceeds budget, the compiler moves R2 and R3 for its largest sections into static JSON fragments (for example `/_content/<paper>/<section>/readings.json`), keeps R0 and R1 inline, and marks each affected unit so the first expansion fetches the fragment once and caches it for the session.
- Fragment loading failures show the R1 text with a short retry notice, never an empty box.

### Static fallback pages and canonical URLs

- Generate static section pages at R0 and R2 (and with margins shown) for readers without JavaScript; they declare the section route as canonical and are excluded from sitemap duplication. Their content also guarantees that fragment-held readings remain indexable.
- `rel=canonical` on paper and section routes omits `?detail=`.

## Technical Approach

- Compiler projection that emits the unit structure; `src/reader/detail/preflight.inline.ts` compiled to a minified inline string with its hash recorded; `DetailControl.tsx` island; `detail.css`; `scripts/measure-reading-face.ts`; fragment writer in the compiler.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] With JavaScript disabled, every unit shows R1 and no hidden reading is visible.
- [ ] `?detail=0` and `?detail=2` show R0 or R2 before first paint (no flash of R1), verified by a first-paint check.
- [ ] Blocked storage falls back to R1 without errors; explicit changes persist when storage works and update the URL by replacement.
- [ ] Per-paragraph deeper reading works with JavaScript and via a real link without it.
- [ ] The budget script reports per-paper gzipped sizes, the CI gate fails a fixture paper forced over 250 kB, and the fragment fallback then passes with working expansion and indexable fallback pages.
- [ ] Canonical tags omit `?detail=`; the inline script's hash is present for the CSP.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests

- `preflight.test.ts`: parameter parsing, storage fallback under thrown exceptions, attribute setting (pure function extracted from the inline script and tested directly).
- `emitReadings.integration.test.ts`: compiled HTML contains exactly four readings per unit with correct attributes.
- `measureReadingFace.test.ts`: gzip sizes computed on fixtures; gate behavior over and under budget.
- `fragments.integration.test.ts`: over-budget fixture paper produces fragments and fallback pages; units reference them.

### End-to-end tests

Through `am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh`: JavaScript-disabled lane (R1 only, fallback links reach static section pages at R0 and R2); first-paint lane for `?detail=0` and `?detail=2` (assert computed visibility at `DOMContentLoaded` and a first-paint screenshot); storage-blocked context; per-paragraph override; fragment expansion with network failure injected (R1 plus retry notice); 320 px; canonical tag check.

### Structured logging

JSON lines with `paper`, `section`, `detailParam`, `storageState`, `effectiveDetail`, `firstPaintReading`, `perUnitOverride`, `fragmentFetched`, `htmlBytes`, `gzipBytes`, `budgetBytes`, `jsEnabled`, `outcome`. Path: `artifacts/test-logs/reader-detail/<run-id>.jsonl`; budget reports also written as `artifacts/budgets/reading-face-<run-id>.json`.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- Readings never contradict one another (R0 compresses R1, R2 expands R1, R3 annotates R1); rendering must not reorder or merge them.
- Detail changes the amount of scaffolding, never the truth conditions: the same equation ids, results, and instruments appear at every Detail.
- Do not implement per-paragraph expansion by duplicating R2 text inside `<details>` elements; that doubles the budget cost.
- Without JavaScript the pre-paint script cannot run, so `?detail=` alone cannot change a static page; the static fallback pages are what make "real links" real.

## Dependencies

Blocked by: `am-read-shell-routes-3ua` (the routes and shell that host readings).

Unblocks: `am-read-passage-actions-vbe` (actions sit beside readings); `am-a11y-reading-only-6wwd` (the reading-only setting builds on this rendering); `am-bm-readings-s4-s5-uqbb` (the first authored readings render through it); `am-plat-print-3orn` (print policy for readings); `am-plat-perf-budgets-s3ww` (includes this budget); `am-plat-clarity-signal-nlwr` (records the detail level with each signal).

title: Build the lazy facsimile face with a page map to sections and equations
description:
# Build the lazy facsimile face with a page map to sections and equations

**Epic:** `am-ep-reader-k0z` · **Batch:** batch-b · **Priority:** P1 · **Plan sections:** §2.3, §3.2, §4.1–§4.3, §6.9, §16.4, §16.5 (traceability only)

## Background

The pinned facsimile is the first and most basic source layer: the *Annalen der Physik* pages, pinned by SHA-256, from which the reviewed ledger, the German edition, and everything else derive. The `facsimile` face shows **the Annalen pages via pdf.js with a page map to sections and equations**. The donor already has a solid viewer: `src/components/patents/PinnedPdfFacsimile.tsx` with `usePinnedPdfFacsimile.ts` and a vendored `public/pdfjs`. It shows a page-one preview image rendered from the same pinned bytes while pdf.js loads, and provides previous, next, and go-to-page controls with screen-reader labels and explicit render states.

Rights matter here: **scans are not the text**. A particular scan can carry its institution's terms, and only assets admitted for redistribution are published under `public/papers/pdfs/`.

## Scope

In scope: adapting the donor viewer; loading pdf.js lazily; the page map display and deep links in both directions; handling assets not admitted for redistribution; resource cleanup; the no-JavaScript fallback; accessibility of controls and the text alternative.

Out of scope: pinning scans and writing receipts (facsimile beads such as `am-src-facsimile-brownian-mox`); page-map data in the provenance receipt and source manifest (`am-cm-source-manifest-6qa`); CSP policy (`am-plat-security-f644`).

## Requirements

- **Viewer.** Port `PinnedPdfFacsimile` and its hook with license notices; keep the preview-while-loading behavior and page controls; add zoom and fit-width controls.
- **Page map.** For the current PDF page, show the printed *Annalen* page number, the sections and paragraphs that begin or continue on it, and the numbered and unnumbered display equations it contains, each linking to its anchor on the source or reading face. PDF page indices and printed journal page numbers are always labeled distinctly because they can differ.
- **Deep links.** Block locators on other faces open the facsimile at the right page (for example `?view=facsimile&page=7`, validated and bounded); the facsimile's map links back to anchors.
- **Admitted assets only.** When an asset's recorded publication decision does not permit redistribution, the face shows bibliographic identity, the rights statement, the SHA-256 recorded in the receipt, and a link to the holding institution instead of embedding the scan. Publisher PDFs served under subscription terms are never pinned or shown.
- **Integrity.** A build check confirms every published PDF's bytes match the SHA-256 in its receipt.
- **Lazy loading.** pdf.js, its worker, and the document load only when the facsimile face opens; nothing from pdf.js enters the initial reading route.
- **Cleanup.** Leaving the face destroys the document and terminates the pdf.js worker; repeated open and close cycles do not grow memory or worker counts.
- **Security.** Configure pdf.js without `eval` support and with the worker served from the site's origin under the CSP.
- **Access.** Controls are keyboard operable with visible focus and labels; the preview image has alt text; the accessible text of the page is the German edition, reached through the page-map links.
- **No-JavaScript.** The face fallback page shows the preview image, the full page-map table for the document, and a link to open the pinned PDF directly.

## Technical Approach

- `src/reader/faces/FacsimileFace.tsx` (static shell and page-map table), `FacsimileViewer.tsx` (dynamic import of the ported viewer), `pageMap.ts` (lookups from the compiled receipt data), `public/pdfjs` vendored per the pinned version.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The Brownian fixture document opens on the facsimile face with preview, navigation, zoom, and a page map listing sections and equations per page with working links.
- [ ] A locator link from the German face opens the correct page; the map links back to the anchor.
- [ ] A non-redistributable fixture asset shows metadata and the institution link without embedding.
- [ ] The initial reading route bundle contains no pdf.js code; opening and closing the face ten times leaves no extra workers.
- [ ] The build fails if a published PDF's digest does not match its receipt.
- [ ] Keyboard, 320 px, and JavaScript-disabled lanes pass.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests

- `pageMap.test.ts`: page-to-section and page-to-equation lookups, distinct PDF and printed page labels, bounds.
- `pdfDigest.integration.test.ts`: digest check on fixture PDFs, including a mismatched fixture.
- `FacsimileFace.render.test.tsx`: admitted and non-admitted assets; no-JavaScript table.

### End-to-end tests

Through `am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh`: open from a locator; navigate pages; follow map links both ways; confirm lazy loading by inspecting network requests and bundle manifests; open and close repeatedly while counting workers; non-admitted fixture; keyboard only; 320 px; JavaScript disabled.

### Structured logging

JSON lines with `paper`, `assetKey`, `admitted`, `pdfPage`, `printedPage`, `mappedAnchors`, `renderState`, `workerCount`, `initialRouteHasPdfjs`, `jsEnabled`, `outcome`. Path: `artifacts/test-logs/reader-facsimile/<run-id>.jsonl`.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- A host's possession of a scan is not a rights determination; the recorded publication decision governs.
- Never replace a pinned PDF because a rendering looks wrong; diagnose the viewer instead.
- Page maps come from the receipt; do not compute them from PDF text layers, which are unreliable for these sources.

## Dependencies

Blocked by: `am-read-shell-routes-3ua` (the face lives in the shell); `am-scaf-extract-ui-components-c31` (the donor viewer, hook, and pdf.js assets extracted with license notices).

Unblocks: no manifest rows depend on this bead directly; source locators across faces link to it.

title: Render the interlinear gloss face
description:
# Render the interlinear gloss face

**Epic:** `am-ep-reader-k0z` · **Batch:** batch-d · **Priority:** P1 · **Plan sections:** §1.3 item 1, §4.5, §4.8, §6.9, §7.5, §7.11, §11.2, §19.7 (traceability only)

## Background

The `gloss` face renders **each German sentence with a word-by-word English gloss beneath it**. Glosses are authored at word level for **paper 4 first** (a three-page physics paper is a fine first text for a German learner) and then for the introductions and key sections of the other papers. The face serves three audiences at once: readers who want to read Einstein in his own language with support; German learners; and readers whose first language is neither German nor English, for whom the gloss plus the R0 overview is the most direct route. The same alignment infrastructure later admits reviewed editions of the readings in other languages.

In the innovation sequence, "the gloss face for paper 4" is a P1 delivery that expands only after it resolves an observed misunderstanding in testing.

## Scope

In scope: interlinear rendering of `GlossUnit` records aligned to German sentences; multiword units (separable verbs, fixed phrases); treatment of mathematics tokens; attribution and review state; coverage notices for sections without glosses; links to term annotations and the reading-German foundation; accessible structure and actions; print and narrow-screen layout.

Out of scope: authoring glosses (`am-edn-gloss-mass-energy-g0y`, `am-edn-gloss-introductions-rdq`); German and English faces (`am-read-bilingual-faces-pao`); the foundation on reading a German physics sentence (`am-found-reading-german-u8oc`).

## Requirements

- **Pairs.** Each German token or multiword unit appears with its authored English gloss directly beneath; pairs never split across lines; separable verbs and fixed phrases are glossed as one unit with both parts marked (for example the two halves of a separated prefix verb).
- **Grammar cues.** Authored grammatical notes (for example the subjunctive in hypotheses: *sei*; formulaic *es gilt*, *man erhält*) appear as small markers that open short explanations.
- **Mathematics.** Symbols and inline equations appear once, unglossed and as printed; notation is never translated.
- **Attribution and review.** Each gloss unit shows its author and review state; machine drafts are visibly marked and never presented as reviewed.
- **Coverage.** Sentences or sections without glosses show the German with a notice ("gloss not yet available for this section") and a link to the parallel face.
- **Links.** Period words link to their term annotations; a persistent link opens the reading-German foundation.
- **Access.** Each sentence is a semantic group with actions "Read the German sentence," "Read the word glosses," and "Read the aligned English translation," so screen readers do not interleave German and English token by token; `lang` attributes are set per token language.
- **Layout.** At 320 CSS px pairs wrap cleanly with legible gloss text and adequate line height; print keeps pairs together.
- **Static.** The face is fully static and needs no JavaScript.

## Technical Approach

- `src/reader/faces/GlossFace.tsx` reusing `SourceBlock` structure from `am-read-bilingual-faces-pao`; `GlossPair.tsx`; CSS using inline-grid pairs rather than `<ruby>` (whose assistive-technology support is inconsistent), with the chosen structure verified on the assistive-technology matrix.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Paper 4 fixture sentences render as interlinear pairs with multiword units, grammar cues, unglossed mathematics, attribution, and review state.
- [ ] Unglossed sections show the coverage notice and link to the parallel face.
- [ ] Screen-reader actions read German, glosses, and English separately; `lang` attributes are correct.
- [ ] 320 px, print emulation, and JavaScript-disabled lanes pass.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests

- `GlossPair.render.test.tsx`: single tokens, multiword units, math tokens, grammar cue markers, `lang` attributes.
- `GlossFace.render.test.tsx`: coverage notices, attribution, review markers from fixture payloads.

### End-to-end tests

In `am-me-e2e-qbbm` (which depends on this face) and a reader lane: open `?view=gloss` for paper 4; verify wrapping at 320 px; trigger the three sentence actions with keyboard; follow a term annotation and the foundation link and return; print emulation; JavaScript disabled.

### Structured logging

JSON lines with `paper`, `sentenceId`, `glossUnitCount`, `multiwordUnits`, `reviewState`, `coverage`, `viewport`, `jsEnabled`, `outcome`. Path: `artifacts/test-logs/reader-gloss/<run-id>.jsonl`.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- A gloss is not a translation; the face links to the reviewed English for meaning.
- Interface localization is separate from scientific translation: a translated menu never implies a reviewed gloss or edition in that language.

## Dependencies

Blocked by: `am-read-bilingual-faces-pao` (source rendering, alignment, and term annotations the gloss reuses).

Unblocks: `am-me-e2e-qbbm` (the mass–energy browser journey includes the gloss face).

title: Surface misconceptions inline as common wrong turns and collect them on the results face
description:
# Surface misconceptions inline as common wrong turns and collect them on the results face

**Epic:** `am-ep-reader-k0z` · **Batch:** batch-c · **Priority:** P1 · **Plan sections:** §5.4, §7.6, §11.2, §11.7, §19.7 (traceability only)

## Background

"The fastest way to help someone understand a famous result is to name the wrong version they already carry." Each paper ships a typed `Misconception` list, surfaced inline as a **"common wrong turn" callout at the anchor where it usually arises** and **collected on the results face under the result it concerns**. Each entry has the tempting claim in the words people use, why it is tempting, what is true at every reading (R0 to R3), the instrument that shows it, and sources. The launch ledger has at least five entries per paper; examples include "brighter light means faster electrons," "halving the diffusivity halves the displacement" (it scales by $1/\sqrt{2}$), "length contraction is an optical illusion" and its opposite "the rod is physically squashed," and "$E = mc^2$ is in the paper" (it is not).

Reasonable alternatives deserve a fair hearing, and nobody is mocked. A misconception callout is a respectful correction, never a red "WRONG" stamp.

## Scope

In scope: the callout component; inline placement at authored anchors; detail-aware "what is true" text; instrument links with presets; the results-face collection; accessible and printable presentation; rendering checks.

Out of scope: authoring entries (`am-bm-misconceptions-2hk1`, `am-me-misconceptions-tr18`, `am-sr-misconceptions-cyci`, `am-lq-misconceptions-jenx`); the five-entry minimum compiler rule (`am-cm-checks-epistemic-o7n`); result cards (`am-read-results-face-uzh`).

## Requirements

- **Content shown.** The tempting claim as people say it (quoted), why it is tempting, what is true at the reader's current Detail (R0, R1, or R2 text; R3 margin under the modern lens), an "See it in the instrument" link that opens the named instrument with its preset, and sources.
- **Placement.** Each entry lists one or more anchors; the callout appears collapsed at each anchor as a single summary line ("A common wrong turn: …") and expands in place. By default at most one callout per paragraph is expanded.
- **Collection.** On the results face, each result card lists the misconceptions linked to it with the same content; a paper-level list is available from the results face.
- **Tone.** Headings and copy follow the editorial voice: no mockery, no "obviously," no red-only warning styling; red never simply means bad.
- **Access.** Each callout is an `aside` with a heading and an expand control reachable by keyboard; state changes are announced once; no tooltip-only content.
- **Static and print.** Without JavaScript callouts render with native disclosure elements; print expands essential content per the print policy.

## Technical Approach

- `src/reader/misconceptions/MisconceptionCallout.tsx` (static structure with `<details>`), `collectForResults.ts` (compiler projection grouping by result), integration in faces through anchor placement data from the compiler.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Fixture entries ("halving the diffusivity halves the displacement" linked to BM-01; "length contraction is an optical illusion" linked to SR-03) render inline at their anchors and under their result cards.
- [ ] "What is true" text follows the Detail setting and the modern lens shows R3.
- [ ] Instrument links open the named instrument with the preset.
- [ ] Copy passes the editorial voice lint; styling never relies on red alone.
- [ ] Keyboard, 320 px, print, and JavaScript-disabled lanes pass.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests

- `MisconceptionCallout.render.test.tsx`: collapsed and expanded states, detail variants, sources, link targets.
- `collectForResults.test.ts`: grouping by result; entries without a result appear only inline and in the paper list.

### End-to-end tests

Through `am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh`: expand a Brownian callout at its anchor; switch Detail and observe text changes; follow the instrument link and return through the return stack; verify the results-face collection; keyboard only; 320 px; print emulation; JavaScript disabled.

### Structured logging

JSON lines with `paper`, `misconceptionId`, `anchor`, `expanded`, `detail`, `lens`, `instrumentLink`, `resultIds`, `jsEnabled`, `outcome`. Path: `artifacts/test-logs/reader-misconceptions/<run-id>.jsonl`.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- The instrument link must open a preset that actually exposes the misconception (for example the $1/\sqrt{2}$ comparison), not a generic default.
- Some entries have two tempting opposites (optical illusion versus physical squashing); the callout must present both fairly when the entry says so.

## Dependencies

Blocked by: `am-read-results-face-uzh` (collection under result cards).

Unblocks: `am-bm-misconceptions-2hk1`, `am-me-misconceptions-tr18`, `am-sr-misconceptions-cyci`, `am-lq-misconceptions-jenx` (per-paper ledgers render through this component).

title: Build the local reading notebook and the interrupted-reader recap
description:
# Build the local reading notebook and the interrupted-reader recap

**Epic:** `am-ep-reader-k0z` · **Batch:** batch-h · **Priority:** P2 · **Plan sections:** §6.8, §7.7, §7.10, §14.3, §14.5, §16.3, §16.6, §19.7 (traceability only)

## Background

Readers of four difficult papers get interrupted. The plan asks for a returnable, interruptible reader without surveillance or gamification. A small **local reading notebook** holds optional pinned questions, selected examples, predictions, and the next suggested step. **Saving may fail when storage is blocked or full; reading continues, and important notes have an explicit local export rather than an assumption of permanent browser storage. Nothing is uploaded; competence is never inferred from the notebook.** An interrupted reader resumes with **a short authored recap of the current argument, not a demand to redo anything**. No timers, streaks, punitive red crosses, surprise audio, or forced full screen.

In the innovation sequence, explanation replay, revisit cards, paired worksheets, and capstones (all built on this notebook) are P2 and expand only if "they help explanation and transfer without becoming required navigation."

## Scope

In scope: notebook entry types and local schema; the notebook panel; pinning from passages, examples, and predictions; export and clear; the "last place" record and the authored recap card on return; failure-tolerant storage behavior; privacy guarantees.

Out of scope: the storage layer itself (`am-plat-local-storage-km8f`); predict mode (`am-inst-predict-mode-ti7m`); explanation replay (`am-reason-explanation-replay-35ds`); teach-back and revisit cards (`am-disc-ppe-teachback-wnp7`); capstone worksheets (`am-disc-capstones-infra-3352`); authoring recap text (paper readings beads add a `recap` field to argument nodes).

## Requirements

- **Entry kinds**: `question` (a pinned authored question or the reader's own), `example` (a reference to an authored example), `prediction` (a reference to a prediction event with its instrument, `instanceId`, `runId`, `snapshotVersion`, seed as a decimal string, and stream version), `nextStep` (a suggested anchor), and `note` (free text). Each entry stores the anchor, paper, and a local timestamp.
- **Schema**: versioned, with forward migrations; unknown versions are preserved and flagged rather than discarded.
- **Panel**: opens from the reader chrome; lists entries by paper and argument; each entry links back through the return stack to its exact frame.
- **Failure tolerance**: when storage is blocked, full, or evicted, the panel explains that notes cannot be saved on this device right now, reading continues unaffected, and export of the current session's entries remains available.
- **Export and clear**: explicit export as JSON (machine-readable) and as a readable HTML or Markdown document; clear-all with confirmation in page (not a browser dialog). Exports are created locally and never include notes in shareable URLs.
- **Privacy**: no network requests carry notebook content; free-text answers are never sent anywhere; no analytics derive from the notebook; notes are never cached into shareable URLs or exports by default.
- **Recap on return**: the site records the last frame locally; on a later visit it offers a dismissible recap card with the authored recap of that argument node and a "continue where you were" link; no quiz, no redo requirement, no streak or time display.

## Technical Approach

- `src/reader/notebook/schema.ts`, `notebookStore.ts` (on top of `am-plat-local-storage-km8f`), `NotebookPanel.tsx`, `export.ts`, `RecapCard.tsx`, `lastFrame.ts`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Readers can pin a question, an example, and a prediction, see them in the panel, and return to their exact frames.
- [ ] Blocked storage and quota-exceeded conditions produce the explanatory message and never break reading.
- [ ] JSON and readable exports contain all entries; clear-all removes them.
- [ ] A network assertion in tests shows no request carries notebook content.
- [ ] The recap card appears on return with authored text and a continue link, and never demands a redo.
- [ ] Copy contains no streak, timer, score, or competence language (lint of notebook strings).

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests

- `schema.test.ts`: validation and migrations, preserved unknown versions.
- `notebookStore.test.ts`: add, list, remove, export, clear against the real storage layer in blocked, quota-exceeded, and working modes.
- `export.test.ts`: JSON and readable outputs for fixtures.
- `RecapCard.render.test.tsx`: authored recap and continue link.

### End-to-end tests

Through `am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh`: pin entries on a Brownian passage and a prediction on BM-01, reload, reopen the panel, follow links back; run with storage blocked; export and clear; revisit and use the recap card; record all network requests and assert none contain notebook payloads; keyboard only and 320 px.

### Structured logging

JSON lines with `entryKind`, `paper`, `anchor`, `storageState`, `schemaVersion`, `exportFormat`, `recapShown`, `networkLeak` (boolean), `outcome`. Path: `artifacts/test-logs/reader-notebook/<run-id>.jsonl`; logs never include note text.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- Browser storage is not permanent; do not promise it is.
- Keyword matching must never be used to call a free-text note "correct."
- The notebook is optional; no reading path may require it.

## Dependencies

Blocked by: `am-read-return-stack-oxa` (entries link to frames); `am-plat-local-storage-km8f` (failure-tolerant local persistence).

Unblocks: `am-disc-capstones-infra-3352`, `am-disc-ppe-teachback-wnp7`, `am-reason-explanation-replay-35ds` (all store local reader work in the notebook).

title: Implement responsive page anatomy with companion column, bottom sheet, pinned equations, and bounded sticky labs
description:
# Implement responsive page anatomy with companion column, bottom sheet, pinned equations, and bounded sticky labs

**Epic:** `am-ep-reader-k0z` · **Batch:** batch-b · **Priority:** P0 · **Plan sections:** §1.5 item 6, §15.4, §16.2, §16.4, §17.4, §19.3 (traceability only)

## Background

The rich interface must never compromise the book. The plan's risk register names the failure: "large bundles, tiny panes, endless controls, slow hydration," and prescribes "restrained companions" and real narrow-screen testing. The page anatomy is specified in detail:

- Desktop reading has a **main text column and an optional companion column** showing the original, an explanation, a selected equation, or a laboratory; a narrow section outline remains available without consuming a third full column.
- On phones, **one primary column and a bottom-sheet or full-width companion**; switching context preserves the paragraph and selected term; German, English, commentary, equations, and a 3D scene are **never squeezed into simultaneous narrow columns**.
- The reader can **pin an equation while scrolling its derivation**.
- A laboratory may stay visible within a **bounded sticky region that never traps the scroll or hides text behind fixed controls**.
- Long equations get **authored line breaks or a local horizontal scroll region, never page-wide overflow**.
- Sticky controls **relinquish space before they obscure content**; at high zoom companions move below the passage.
- The first encounter uses a single question, one useful interaction, and a clear next step; the full paper can be long and demanding. Keeping these two scales connected matters more than making every screen equally dense.

## Scope

In scope: layout tiers and breakpoints; the companion column and its content switching; the phone bottom sheet; the outline placement; equation pinning; the bounded sticky laboratory region; local overflow regions for equations and tables; zoom and reflow behavior; reduced-motion behavior of layout transitions.

Out of scope: themes, fonts, and color tokens (`am-design-themes-typography-288q`); print layout (`am-plat-print-3orn`); reading-only adjustments to line length, size, and spacing (`am-a11y-reading-only-6wwd`); face contents (face beads); the outline's navigation logic (`am-read-anchors-navigation-a6o`).

## Requirements

- **Tiers** expressed in `em`-based or container-query breakpoints so browser zoom triggers reflow: a wide tier with main column plus companion plus collapsible outline; a medium tier with main column and a collapsible companion; a narrow tier with one column and a bottom-sheet or full-width companion.
- **Reading measure**: the main column holds a comfortable line length (about 60 to 75 characters for body text by default), adjustable within tested limits by `am-a11y-reading-only-6wwd`.
- **Companion**: shows one of original text, explanation, pinned equation, or laboratory; switching companions preserves the main passage's anchor and selected term; the companion never forces two languages plus commentary plus equations into narrow columns.
- **Bottom sheet** (narrow tier): non-modal by default, keyboard closable, focus moves into it when opened by the reader and returns on close, respects safe-area insets, never covers the passage it explains without a way to see both (collapse to a peek height).
- **Pinned equation**: a reader can pin the current equation card; it stays visible in the companion or as a compact sticky strip while the derivation scrolls, and unpins with one action.
- **Sticky laboratory**: bounded maximum height (a fraction of the viewport) that yields when the passage needs space; it never overlaps text (verified by bounding-box checks) and never traps scroll.
- **Overflow**: page-level horizontal overflow never occurs at 320 CSS px; wide equations and tables live in local scroll regions with visible affordances and keyboard scrolling, or use authored line breaks.
- **High zoom**: at 200 and 400 percent zoom, companions move below the passage and sticky elements release.
- **Reduced motion**: sheet and companion transitions do not animate.
- **No-JavaScript**: the main column renders complete; companions degrade to inline sections or links.

## Technical Approach

- `src/reader/layout/ReaderLayout.tsx` (server layout with CSS grid and container queries), `Companion.tsx` and `BottomSheet.tsx` islands, `pinnedEquationStore.ts`, `StickyLabRegion.tsx`, `overflow.css` utilities for local scroll regions.
- Layout tokens (widths, gaps, maximum sticky heights) live with the design tokens from `am-design-themes-typography-288q`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] At 320, 375, 768, 1024, and 1440 CSS px, and at 200 and 400 percent zoom, no page-level horizontal overflow occurs on fixture pages.
- [ ] The companion switches between original, explanation, equation, and laboratory while preserving the anchor and selected term.
- [ ] On narrow screens the companion is a bottom sheet or full-width view, and no more than one reading surface plus one companion is visible at once.
- [ ] A pinned equation stays visible while its derivation scrolls; unpinning restores the layout.
- [ ] The sticky laboratory never overlaps text and yields at high zoom.
- [ ] Reduced-motion and JavaScript-disabled lanes pass.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests

- `pinnedEquationStore.test.ts`: pin, unpin, and persistence across companion switches.
- `BottomSheet.test.tsx`: focus movement, Escape close, non-modal behavior, peek state.
- `layoutTokens.test.ts`: sticky maximum heights and breakpoints consistent with tokens.

### End-to-end tests

Through `am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh`: viewport matrix screenshots; `scrollWidth <= clientWidth` assertions; bounding-box intersection checks between the sticky laboratory and text nodes; pinned equation visibility while scrolling a derivation; companion switching with anchor and selection assertions; 200 and 400 percent zoom lanes; reduced motion; JavaScript disabled; touch emulation on the bottom sheet.

### Structured logging

JSON lines with `route`, `viewport`, `zoom`, `tier`, `companion`, `pinnedEquationId`, `overflowPx`, `stickyOverlapPx`, `anchorPreserved`, `selectionPreserved`, `reducedMotion`, `jsEnabled`, `outcome`. Path: `artifacts/test-logs/reader-layout/<run-id>.jsonl`; failures retain full-page screenshots per viewport.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- A fixed control that hides text under it at some zoom level is a failure even if the default viewport looks fine; test zoom explicitly.
- Do not let the companion become a second reading column that competes with the main text on phones.
- The first-encounter layout is intentionally sparse; do not reuse the dense paper layout for it.

## Dependencies

Blocked by: `am-read-shell-routes-3ua` (the shell whose layout this defines); `am-design-themes-typography-288q` (tokens, measures, and fonts).

Unblocks: `am-plat-print-3orn` (print policy builds on the layout's structure).

title: Add the local passage actions and the "What is getting in the way?" menu
description:
# Add the local passage actions and the "What is getting in the way?" menu

**Epic:** `am-ep-reader-k0z` · **Batch:** batch-b · **Priority:** P0 · **Plan sections:** §6.1, §6.3, §6.4, §6.7, §7.1, §9.1, §10.4 (traceability only)

## Background

The interface refuses to become a wall of switches. Instead of exposing every combination of detail, formalism, and guidance as modes, the default reading carries **local actions on every passage**: **"Why?"**, **"Show the missing step,"** **"Show me one example first,"** **"Try it,"** and **"Read the original."** Beside every hard passage sits a compact **"What is getting in the way?"** action with concrete choices: an unfamiliar word or symbol; an algebraic move; the physical reason for a step; the connection to the picture; the purpose of the calculation; or simply too much at once. Each choice opens an **authored response for this exact argument**. The reader is never asked to diagnose a learning disability or reveal a personal history.

"Show me one example first" exists because concrete numerical examples often resolve confusion more efficiently than another layer of terminology. Guided discovery is never compulsory rediscovery: a reader may move directly to the explanation at every point.

Editors write these responses through five invisible review lenses (the programmer, the physician, the engineer, the student, the reader with no algebra) so they address real obstacles. Readers never see or choose a persona.

## Scope

In scope: the data contract for passage actions and obstacle responses; the action bar and obstacle menu components; opening behavior in context; static fallbacks; compiler coverage reporting for hard passages without responses.

Out of scope: the navigation stack for descending and returning (`am-read-return-stack-oxa`); authoring responses (paper readings beads); derivation-chain contents (`am-eq-derivation-chains-r4c`); the missing-step explorer as a reasoning instrument (`am-reason-missing-step-explorer-rsl4`); instruments and their presets (instrument beads); first encounters (paper first-encounter beads).

## Requirements

### Actions

- **Why?** opens the authored justification for the passage's claim at the current Detail, with links to the premises it uses.
- **Show the missing step** opens the derivation-chain step or authored bridge for a step the paper skips; when `am-reason-missing-step-explorer-rsl4` covers the step, it opens there.
- **Show me one example first** opens an authored concrete numerical or geometric instance; it sits beside every abstract derivation.
- **Try it** opens the instrument for this step with its preset scenario (embedded in place or in the companion column); when no instrument applies, it opens a static worked example.
- **Read the original** jumps to the aligned German and English sentences for the passage with the alignment highlight.
- An action appears only when its content exists; missing content is a coverage gap reported by the compiler, never filled with generated text.

### Obstacle menu

- Present on passages flagged hard by authors (or implied by the presence of obstacle responses).
- Six choices exactly as listed above, each opening its authored response; responses may point to a foundation, an example, a derivation step, or an instrument state.
- Copy never asks about disabilities, history, credentials, or level, and never judges.

### Behavior

- Opening an action keeps the reader's place and hands control to the return stack API (`openClarification`) once `am-read-return-stack-oxa` lands; until then it opens inline with a working close control.
- Keyboard operable, touch targets sized properly, accessible names that describe the action and the passage, no tooltip-only content.
- Without JavaScript, every action is a real link: examples and justifications to static anchors or `<details>` content already on the page, "Read the original" to the German face fallback page at the passage anchor, "Try it" to the laboratory route or a static worked example.

### Content contract and coverage

- `PassageActions` on argument nodes and paragraphs: `why`, `missingStep`, `example`, `tryIt` (instrument id and scenario id or static example id), `original` (source anchors), `hard` flag, and `obstacleResponses` keyed by the six obstacle kinds.
- The compiler emits a coverage report listing hard passages missing any obstacle response and abstract derivations missing an example, feeding `am-cm-coverage-ledger-0ip`.

## Technical Approach

- Schema additions in `am-cm-schemas-argument-llm`; `src/reader/actions/PassageActions.tsx` (static structure plus island), `ObstacleMenu.tsx`, `openInContext.ts`; compiler coverage pass `passageActionsCoverage.ts`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] On the Brownian §4 fixture passage, all five actions and all six obstacle choices open authored content.
- [ ] Actions without content do not render; the coverage report lists the gaps.
- [ ] No copy asks the reader to self-diagnose or declare a level (reviewed string list plus a lint of banned phrasings).
- [ ] Keyboard, touch, 320 px, and JavaScript-disabled lanes pass.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests

- `passageActions.schema.test.ts`: valid records; unknown instrument or scenario ids rejected; obstacle kinds restricted to the six.
- `passageActionsCoverage.test.ts`: gaps reported for fixture passages.
- `PassageActions.render.test.tsx`: availability, accessible names, static links.

### End-to-end tests

In `am-bm-slice-e2e-sbqu` and a reader lane: open each action and obstacle response on a Brownian §4 passage; confirm "Read the original" lands on the aligned sentence; confirm "Try it" opens BM-06 with its preset; repeat keyboard only, at 320 px, and with JavaScript disabled following real links.

### Structured logging

JSON lines with `paper`, `anchor`, `action`, `obstacleKind`, `contentId`, `available`, `jsEnabled`, `viewport`, `outcome`. Path: `artifacts/test-logs/reader-actions/<run-id>.jsonl`.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- Formalism and guidance stay behind tested presets; do not add them as new switches beside these actions.
- Do not let actions crowd short passages; keep the bar compact and contextual.
- Scientific difficulty comes from the ideas, not from navigating the site: no timers, streaks, or punitive marks.

## Dependencies

Blocked by: `am-read-detail-axis-sfc` (actions render beside readings at the current Detail); `am-cm-schemas-argument-llm` (the content contract for actions and obstacle responses).

Unblocks: `am-read-return-stack-oxa` (descending from actions); `am-bm-first-encounter-fjvh`, `am-me-first-encounter-kejt`, `am-srk-first-encounter-471z`, `am-lq-first-encounter-hhr8` (first encounters use these actions and bridges).

title: Implement the perspective axis and the notation toggle as independent choices
description:
# Implement the perspective axis and the notation toggle as independent choices

**Epic:** `am-ep-reader-k0z` · **Batch:** batch-b · **Priority:** P1 · **Plan sections:** §4.7, §5.1, §6.1, §6.2, §11.4, §15.5 (traceability only)

## Background

The **Perspective** axis chooses which knowledge, notation, and later interpretations may be used: "Paper and contemporary context" (the default) or "Explicit modern lens." Its annotation layer is **R3, the historian's margin**: what Einstein wrote and in what notation, where the argument is heuristic, where later physics changed the reading, who had the same result earlier or at the same time, and what the primary literature says, cited.

Separately, the explanation faces show Einstein's **printed notation** by default with a toggle to **modern notation**. The toggle re-renders every equation from its semantic expression tree, never by string substitution, and updates the colorized sentence and the legend, so a reader can learn to read Einstein's own symbols and then switch.

The plan insists these are different choices: **"Modern notation" and "modern knowledge" are modeled independently.** Renaming $V$ to $c$ does not authorize importing a later proof. The interface may offer a sensible preset, but the underlying state keeps two independent values.

## Scope

In scope: the Perspective control and its effect on R3 margins and modern-lens content; the Notation control and its effect on explanation-face equations, sentences, legends, and notation strips; persistence and URL parameters; pre-paint application; loading modern-notation markup within budget; markers for unit conversions and modernizations; first-use collision callouts.

Out of scope: rendering readings (`am-read-detail-axis-sfc`, whose pre-paint mechanism this bead reuses); LaTeX generation (`am-eq-latex-generation-hc3`); the colorized component (`am-eq-colorized-component-1z8`); concordance entries (`am-not-concordance-model-uag`); discovery shelf rules (`am-disc-knowledge-cards-iw8j`).

## Requirements

- **Two independent states**: `perspective` (`paper`, `modern`) and `notation` (`printed`, `modern`). Any combination is valid. A preset "Modern lens with modern notation" may set both, but each remains separately changeable and separately persisted.
- **Perspective effects**: under `modern`, R3 margins and modern-lens content blocks (for example later formal explanations such as invariant mass of two opposite pulses, or spacetime diagrams labeled as Minkowski's 1908 aid) become visible, each labeled with its historical status and date. Under `paper`, they stay hidden (R3 remains available per paragraph through an explicit "historian's margin" action).
- **Perspective never changes discovery**: the 1904 shelf and discovery steps obey the knowledge boundary regardless of the lens.
- **Notation effects**: only on explanation faces (`reading`, `results`, companion explanations). Source and translation faces always show printed notation. Switching swaps each equation's markup to the modern variant generated from its tree, updates the colorized sentence, legend, and notation strip, and keeps term and operation ids unchanged so selection persists.
- **Structural modern forms**: when an equation's modern form is a unit conversion (paper 3 §6, Gaussian to SI) or a modernization (the modern transverse-mass treatment), the modern view shows a visible marker ("converted from Gaussian units" or "modern argument, later lens") and links to the derivation.
- **Collision callouts**: the first appearance in each section of $\beta$ as the modern $\gamma$ (papers 3 and 4) and of $k$ as viscosity (paper 2) is called out prominently in both notations, linking to the concordance.
- **Persistence and URLs**: `?lens=modern` and `?notation=modern` (validated) apply before first paint through the same inline script pattern as the Detail axis (`data-perspective` and `data-notation` on `<html>`); reader changes persist to storage when available and update the URL by replacement; canonical URLs omit these parameters.
- **Budget**: printed-notation markup is inline; modern-notation markup for a paper loads from a static route-local fragment on first use unless inlining both stays within the 250 kB gzipped reading-face budget.
- **No-JavaScript**: printed notation and paper perspective render; each equation's notation strip and a link to `/notation` provide the modern symbols; R3 margins are reachable through real links to static margin views.

## Technical Approach

- `src/reader/perspective/state.ts` (two independent values), `PerspectiveControl.tsx` and `NotationControl.tsx` islands, extension of the Detail pre-paint script with the two attributes, `modernNotationFragment.ts` loader, CSS for `data-perspective` visibility of R3 and modern-lens blocks.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All four combinations of perspective and notation render correctly on a fixture page: modern notation with paper perspective shows modern symbols but no modern-knowledge blocks; modern perspective with printed notation shows margins and modern-lens blocks with printed symbols.
- [ ] Source and translation faces are unaffected by the notation toggle.
- [ ] Term selection persists across notation switches (same ids); legends and sentences update.
- [ ] Unit-conversion and modernization markers appear on the relevant fixture equations.
- [ ] URL parameters apply before first paint; storage failures fall back to defaults; canonical URLs omit parameters.
- [ ] Reading-face budget remains within 250 kB gzipped per paper with the chosen loading strategy.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests

- `state.test.ts`: independence of the two values; presets set both without coupling later changes.
- `prepaint.test.ts`: parameter parsing and storage fallback for `lens` and `notation`.
- `modernNotationFragment.integration.test.ts`: fragment contents match compiled modern variants; ids unchanged.
- `collisionCallout.test.tsx`: first-use detection per section.

### End-to-end tests

Through `am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh` on a Brownian and a relativity fixture page: the four combinations; toggling with a selected term; the §6 unit-conversion marker; first-use callouts; first-paint check with parameters; JavaScript-disabled lane (printed notation, links to margin views and `/notation`); 320 px.

### Structured logging

JSON lines with `paper`, `face`, `perspective`, `notation`, `preset`, `selectedTermId`, `selectionPreserved`, `fragmentLoaded`, `markersShown`, `firstPaintState`, `jsEnabled`, `outcome`. Path: `artifacts/test-logs/reader-perspective/<run-id>.jsonl`.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- Coupling the two controls would quietly teach that modern symbols imply modern knowledge; keep them visibly separate.
- Modern-lens content must never leak into historical routes or discovery steps, even when the lens is on.
- Notation strips must still show the printed symbol beside the modern one so readers can learn Einstein's notation.

## Dependencies

Blocked by: `am-read-shell-routes-3ua` (the faces the controls act on); `am-eq-latex-generation-hc3` (printed and modern variants generated from trees); `am-not-concordance-model-uag` (scoped mappings and collision metadata).

Unblocks: no manifest rows depend on this bead directly; the paper reading beads rely on it for margin and notation presentation.

title: Generalize the result weave so instruments light the sentences they demonstrate
description:
# Generalize the result weave so instruments light the sentences they demonstrate

**Epic:** `am-ep-reader-k0z` · **Batch:** batch-b · **Priority:** P1 · **Plan sections:** §2.3, §6.9, §10.1, §12.5, §15.5 (traceability only)

## Background

The donor's spec-clause weave (`src/physics/specClauses.ts`, exporting `SpecClause` and `specClausesFor(patentId, params)`) lights exact phrases on a patent's specification face when a kernel predicate holds. Here the same idea lights the **German and English sentences that state what an instrument is currently demonstrating**:

- dragging the boost past $0.5c$ lights the paper 3 §4 sentence about the slowed clock;
- entering the Wien regime lights the paper 1 §4 limiting-law sentence;
- making the ensemble histogram and the Gaussian overlay agree lights the paper 2 §5 formula for $\lambda_x$.

The plan's caution is essential: **the highlight is a pointer, not a claim that truth has been achieved.** The donor's implementation imports patent kernels into one large module keyed by patent id; here predicates belong to instruments, are evaluated by the owner side on accepted snapshots, and target content ids.

## Scope

In scope: the weave predicate data contract; predicate evaluation on accepted snapshots in the runtime; hysteresis for noisy statistical predicates; highlighting of target sentences on source, translation, and parallel faces and of linked explanation paragraphs; accessible presentation; compiler validation of targets.

Out of scope: instruments and their kernels (instrument beads); snapshot store internals (`am-rt-snapshot-store-aft`); face rendering (`am-read-bilingual-faces-pao`); statistical tolerances policy (`am-ver-statistical-policy-grj`, consulted for agreement predicates).

## Requirements

### Data contract

`WeavePredicate` records live with experiment manifests: `id`; `instrumentId`; `kind` (`threshold` on a quantity id with direction; `regime` on a classification output; `agreement` between two outputs within a stated tolerance and sample requirement); parameters; `hysteresis` (enter and exit bounds); `targets` (source sentence ids; aligned translation sentences are derived from alignment); `pointerText` (ordinary-language description such as "The instrument is now showing what this sentence states").

### Evaluation

- Predicates are pure functions evaluated alongside the owner's accepted snapshot (in the worker or the runtime's host path), and the snapshot publishes `weave` flags with the snapshot version. React components only read flags.
- Threshold and regime predicates use enter and exit bounds to avoid flicker at the boundary; agreement predicates require the stated sample size and tolerance before lighting and use hysteresis on exit.
- Flags from different input revisions are never mixed.

### Presentation

- Target sentences show an outline plus a text marker ("shown by the instrument now") on German, English, and parallel faces, and the linked explanation paragraph shows a small pointer; no glow and no "proved" language.
- Only the current paper and argument context are affected.
- Changes are announced politely once per committed interaction (for example on slider release), never on every frame; a "What the instrument shows now" list is available on demand.
- Reduced motion disables any transition.

### Validation

The compiler rejects predicates whose targets do not resolve to sentence ids or whose quantity ids are not outputs of the instrument.

## Technical Approach

- `src/experiments/weave/types.ts`, `evaluate.ts` (pure, shared by worker and host paths), `hysteresis.ts`; `src/reader/weave/WeaveHighlighter.tsx` island subscribing to the instance's snapshot flags; compiler validation pass.
- Port the donor concept, not its module: no aggregate import of kernels.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Fixture predicates for the three plan examples evaluate correctly on scripted snapshots (boost at $0.49c$ versus $0.51c$ with hysteresis; Wien regime entry by $h\nu/(k_BT)$ threshold; histogram and Gaussian agreement within tolerance at the required sample size).
- [ ] Highlights appear on both languages and the parallel face, and the pointer copy never claims truth.
- [ ] No flicker occurs when a noisy agreement metric hovers near its threshold in a seeded run.
- [ ] Announcements occur once per committed interaction; reduced motion is respected.
- [ ] Invalid targets fail the compiler.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests

- `evaluate.test.ts`: threshold, regime, and agreement predicates on fixture snapshots; revision isolation.
- `hysteresis.test.ts`: enter and exit bounds; seeded noisy sequences produce stable states.
- `weaveValidation.integration.test.ts`: unresolved targets and non-output quantity ids rejected.
- `WeaveHighlighter.render.test.tsx`: markers on target sentences from flags.

### End-to-end tests

In `am-bm-slice-e2e-sbqu`: run BM-06 until the histogram and Gaussian agree and assert the §5 $\lambda_x$ sentence lights on German and English faces with a matching `snapshotVersion`; move away and assert exit without flicker; keyboard-only operation and a screen-reader announcement check; reduced-motion lane.

### Structured logging

JSON lines with `instrumentId`, `instanceId`, `snapshotVersion`, `predicateId`, `metric`, `threshold`, `state` (`enter`, `hold`, `exit`), `targets`, `announced`, `outcome`. Path: `artifacts/test-logs/reader-weave/<run-id>.jsonl`.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- A lit sentence says "this is what the instrument now shows," not "this is now true"; a simulator makes consequences of assumptions legible and is never evidence that nature obeys them.
- Agreement between a histogram and a curve depends on sample size and seed; predicates must state both.

## Dependencies

Blocked by: `am-read-bilingual-faces-pao` (the sentences being lit); `am-rt-snapshot-store-aft` (flags published with accepted snapshots); `am-scaf-extract-runtime-utilities-99y` (the donor weave concept extracted with its license notice).

Unblocks: no manifest rows depend on this bead directly; paper instruments declare weave predicates once it exists.

title: Build the results face with printed, modern, one-sentence, probe, misconception, and used-later layers
description:
# Build the results face with printed, modern, one-sentence, probe, misconception, and used-later layers

**Epic:** `am-ep-reader-k0z` · **Batch:** batch-c · **Priority:** P1 · **Plan sections:** §3.3–§3.6 (results and printed checks), §6.9, §7.6, §10.2, §11.4, §13.3, §15.6 (traceability only)

## Background

Each paper states a set of results that later physics, the other papers, and popular accounts all lean on. The `results` face presents **the paper's numbered results as cards: as printed, in modern notation, in one sentence, with the live probe, the misconceptions that cluster around it, and "where this is used later."** The results face is also where the equation genealogy is drawn and where misconception ledgers are collected under the results they concern.

Results carry the four kinds of meaning, and printed numerical checks carry their provenance: Einstein's printed numbers (for example $N = 6.17\times10^{23}$ from Planck's constants, about 4.3 V for $\nu = 1.03\times10^{15}\,\mathrm{s^{-1}}$, about $0.8\,\mu\mathrm{m}$ in one second and $6\,\mu\mathrm{m}$ in a minute) are historical fixtures reproduced from his stated inputs, labeled separately from modern golden values and from measurements.

## Scope

In scope: the result card component and layout; the result data contract consumed from the compiler; printed-check display with provenance labels; on-demand live probes; links to misconceptions, used-later results (including cross-paper), source anchors, and reading-face explanations; the slot for the genealogy; static and print output.

Out of scope: authoring result cards per paper (`am-bm-results-cards-ft8k`, `am-me-results-cards-c6mf`, `am-sr-results-cards-k9ck`, `am-lq-results-cards-c8w7`); the genealogy itself (`am-eq-genealogy-hmm`); misconception callouts (`am-read-misconception-callouts-a3o`); instruments (instrument beads).

## Requirements

### Card contract

`ResultCard`: `resultId` (anchor `#result-<slug>`), paper, section anchor(s); `printedEquationId` (rendered in printed notation); modern form (generated from the tree, with unit-conversion or modernization markers when applicable); `oneSentence` (authored, true at its resolution); `printedChecks[]` (value as printed, the inputs Einstein stated, a scenario id for the historical fixture, and a label "historical, as printed"); `probe` (instrument id, preset scenario id, the question the probe answers, for example "intensity changes the electron count but not the maximum kinetic energy"); `misconceptionIds[]`; `usedBy[]` (result ids in this or other papers, with relation labels); the four kinds of meaning; `sources[]`.

### Behavior

- Cards appear in paper order with a section filter; each card's anchor works across faces.
- **Probes load on demand.** A card shows the probe's question and a "Run the probe" action; the instrument loads lazily and all displayed values come from its accepted snapshot with the instrument's execution label. When the instrument is unavailable on the device, the card shows its static worked example.
- **Printed checks** show the printed value, the stated inputs, and the reproduced value from the historical scenario; modern golden values, where shown, are labeled "modern constants" and kept visually distinct.
- **Links**: "Read where the paper states this" to the source anchor, "Explanation" to the reading face, misconceptions to their callouts, and used-later results (with cross-paper edges labeled, such as paper 3 §8 feeding paper 4).
- **Genealogy slot**: the results face reserves a section for the equation genealogy supplied by `am-eq-genealogy-hmm`.
- **Static and print**: without JavaScript, cards render fully except the live probe, which becomes a link to the laboratory route with the preset; cards print cleanly.

## Technical Approach

- `src/reader/faces/ResultsFace.tsx`, `ResultCard.tsx` (reusing the semantic equation component), `ProbeLauncher.tsx` (dynamic import of the registered instrument through the dispatcher), compiler projection `resultsProjection.ts`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A Brownian fixture results face renders cards for the diffusion coefficient, the displacement law $\lambda_x = \sqrt{2Dt}$ with its printed checks, and the molecular-number formula, each with printed and modern forms, one sentence, misconception links, and used-later links.
- [ ] A probe loads only on request and shows values whose `snapshotVersion` matches the instrument; unavailable instruments show static worked examples.
- [ ] Historical printed checks and modern values are labeled and styled distinctly.
- [ ] JavaScript-disabled, print, 320 px, and keyboard lanes pass.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests

- `resultsProjection.test.ts`: compiled cards contain all layers; unresolved probe, misconception, or usedBy ids fail compilation.
- `ResultCard.render.test.tsx`: printed and modern forms, markers, labels for historical versus modern values.
- `ProbeLauncher.test.tsx`: lazy loading and unavailable fallback using the real dispatcher with a fixture instrument.

### End-to-end tests

Through `am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh` on the Brownian fixture: filter by section; run a probe and compare snapshot ids with the instrument view; follow source, explanation, misconception, and used-later links and return; print emulation; JavaScript disabled; 320 px; keyboard only.

### Structured logging

JSON lines with `paper`, `resultId`, `probeInstrumentId`, `probeLoaded`, `snapshotVersion`, `executionLabel`, `printedCheckScenario`, `reproducedValue`, `linkTargets`, `jsEnabled`, `viewport`, `outcome`. Path: `artifacts/test-logs/reader-results/<run-id>.jsonl`.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- Never present a probe's output as evidence that nature behaves that way; the card states the probe's question and the model's execution label.
- Paper 4's card must state that the paper shows the mass falls by $L/V^2$; the familiar $E = mc^2$ form belongs to 1907 and later.
- Keep the results face light: heavy instruments load only when asked.

## Dependencies

Blocked by: `am-read-shell-routes-3ua` (the face lives in the shell); `am-eq-colorized-component-1z8` (cards render semantic equations).

Unblocks: `am-read-misconception-callouts-a3o` (collected under cards); `am-eq-genealogy-hmm` (drawn on this face); `am-bm-results-cards-ft8k`, `am-me-results-cards-c6mf`, `am-sr-results-cards-k9ck`, `am-lq-results-cards-c8w7` (per-paper card content).

Added during graph review (blocked by):
- `am-eq-live-bindings-2se`: result cards show live probe values bound to accepted snapshots.
- `am-inst-registry-dispatcher-66l0`: result-card probes resolve registered instruments.

title: Build recursive clarification with the return stack and compass
description:
# Build recursive clarification with the return stack and compass

**Epic:** `am-ep-reader-k0z` · **Batch:** batch-b · **Priority:** P0 · **Plan sections:** §6.4, §6.8, §7.5, §12.8, §12.11, §16.2, §19.4 (traceability only)

## Background

Recursive explanation easily becomes a maze: each definition opens more undefined terms until the reader has lost the argument. The plan's response has three parts. The prerequisite graph is **finite and curated**, and every basic node has a stated stopping point (multiplication as repeated scaling, a graph as a record of paired quantities, a rate as change per unit of something). A selected term opens a **compact explanation in context**, from which the reader can descend to a worked example, a prerequisite, and ultimately ordinary arithmetic or a concrete counting or measuring operation. And a **return stack retains the original paragraph, the selected expression, the laboratory state, and the scroll position.**

The stack has a persistent, unobtrusive **compass**: the question we were answering, the idea we just opened, and return to the exact step. It supports back and forward history, a direct link to the current clarification, and one action to close all side explanations without losing the main passage. The plan's closure condition for the reader shell is that **a deep-linked passage survives face switching and foundation return**.

## Scope

In scope: the clarification stack model; the `openClarification` API used by passage actions, equation terms, foundation drawers, and discovery steps; the compass; history and URL integration; restoration of selection, scroll, and laboratory state; close-all; focus management; static fallbacks.

Out of scope: foundation lesson content and the drawer UI (`am-found-library-infra-002t`); passage actions (`am-read-passage-actions-vbe`); anchors and face switching (`am-read-anchors-navigation-a6o`); the reading notebook and interrupted-reader recap (`am-read-notebook-tde`); experiment runtime internals (`am-rt-snapshot-store-aft`, `am-rt-control-tapes-0gc`).

## Requirements

### Frames

A frame records: the anchor (content id) and face; Detail and Perspective; the selected term or operation id; the opened clarification (`kind` of foundation, example, obstacle response, derivation step, or instrument view, plus its id); the authored question being answered; the scroll offset relative to the anchor; references to mounted laboratory instances (`instanceId`, `runId`, and the latest tape checkpoint digest).

### Descend and return

- `openClarification({ kind, id, question, returnTo })` pushes a frame and one history entry.
- Back pops to the previous frame and restores face, anchor, relative scroll, selection, and the opened state; forward re-opens.
- Returning must never restart an experiment: if the instance is still mounted, it is reused; if it was unmounted, it is restored from its tape checkpoint only when model, schema, parameters, seed, and stream semantics validate, otherwise the laboratory shows a visibly new run.
- Close-all clears side explanations and returns to the root frame with the main passage in place.

### Compass

- A persistent, compact navigation landmark showing the question being answered, the idea just opened, and "return to the exact step."
- Hidden when no clarification is open; never obscures content (it relinquishes space before hiding text, and moves below the passage at high zoom).

### URLs

- The current clarification is linkable through a compact, validated parameter (for example `?open=foundation:mean-variance-rms`) plus the anchor; a direct link opens the clarification with its compass.
- State parameters never enter canonical URLs; the parameter's size is bounded and invalid values are ignored.

### Access

- Focus moves to the opened clarification's heading and returns to the originating control or term on return.
- Frame changes produce a single polite announcement, never a stream.
- Without JavaScript, clarifications are real links to static anchors and foundation pages, and the browser's own back button returns the reader.

## Technical Approach

- `src/reader/stack/stackStore.ts` (external store with stable snapshots), `history.ts` (push, pop, and state serialization in `history.state` plus the URL parameter), `Compass.tsx`, `restoreLab.ts` (coordinates with the runtime by instance id and tape checkpoint), `focus.ts`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] From a deep link to a Brownian §4 sentence, a reader selects $\langle x^2\rangle$, opens the mean-variance foundation, descends to its prerequisite and a worked example, then presses back twice and returns to the exact sentence, selection, and scroll position, with the linked instrument's `runId` unchanged.
- [ ] Face switching during a clarification and then returning keeps the passage in place.
- [ ] A direct clarification link opens the clarification with the compass; close-all returns to the main passage.
- [ ] Focus management and single announcements pass keyboard and screen-reader smoke checks.
- [ ] Without JavaScript, the same journey works through real links and the browser back button.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests

- `stackStore.test.ts`: push, pop, close-all, restore, stable snapshots, bounded depth with a clear message if exceeded.
- `history.test.ts`: serialization of frames, URL parameter validation and size bounds, ignored invalid values.
- `restoreLab.integration.test.ts`: with the real runtime and a fixture experiment, return reuses the instance or restores from a validated checkpoint; an invalid checkpoint produces a visibly new run.

### End-to-end tests

In `am-bm-slice-e2e-sbqu` and a reader lane: the journey in the first acceptance criterion; the face-switch variant; a direct clarification link; close-all; keyboard-only focus assertions; 320 px with a bottom-sheet companion; JavaScript-disabled variant.

### Structured logging

JSON lines with `action` (`push`, `pop`, `forward`, `closeAll`, `directOpen`), `frameDepth`, `anchor`, `face`, `clarificationKind`, `clarificationId`, `selectionId`, `scrollDeltaPx`, `instanceId`, `runIdBefore`, `runIdAfter`, `restoredFromCheckpoint`, `focusTarget`, `outcome`. Path: `artifacts/test-logs/reader-return-stack/<run-id>.jsonl`.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- A glossary link is not a logical premise; the stack is navigation, not a proof route.
- Deep stacks signal a curation problem: log depth so editors can see where readers descend far.
- Never block reading on laboratory restoration; the book stays usable if a laboratory must pause.

## Dependencies

Blocked by: `am-read-anchors-navigation-a6o` (frames are anchored by content ids); `am-read-passage-actions-vbe` (the main entry points that descend).

Unblocks: `am-found-library-infra-002t` (foundations open through this stack); `am-read-notebook-tde` (the notebook links to frames); `am-reason-missing-step-explorer-rsl4` (opens and returns through the stack); `am-bm-slice-e2e-sbqu` (the slice journey depends on return).

title: Build the reader shell and paper routes with ?view= faces and canonical URLs
description:
# Build the reader shell and paper routes with ?view= faces and canonical URLs

**Epic:** `am-ep-reader-k0z` · **Batch:** batch-b · **Priority:** P0 · **Plan sections:** §1.5 item 6, §2.2, §2.3, §6.1, §6.9, §15.1, §16.1, §16.4, §19.4 (traceability only)

## Background

The reader shell is the frame in which a visitor moves between the German source, the English translation, the explanation, the results, the gloss, and the facsimile. The donor's `DualProjectionViewer.tsx` and `patentViewMode.ts` established the right interaction idea: every face is a URL through a `?view=` parameter, so deep links work and the browser back button behaves. The donor helpers parse the parameter (`viewModeFromSearch`), and compute the next URL without double-pushing history while preserving other query keys and the hash (`applyPatentViewToUrl`). The monolithic viewer is not ported. The shell here loads independent panels, each with route-local data, so the German edition, the translation, explanations, discovery, and laboratories never arrive as one aggregate bundle.

Routes are App Router only, under the single `src/app/` root.

## Scope

In scope: `/papers/[paper]` and `/papers/[paper]/[section]`; static generation from compiler outputs; the face registry and `?view=` parsing and application; split view; independent, code-split face panels; canonical URLs and metadata; not-found handling; the no-JavaScript fallback for face links; the decision record for static generation versus query parameters.

Out of scope: anchors and alias redirects (`am-read-anchors-navigation-a6o`); the Detail axis (`am-read-detail-axis-sfc`); face contents (`am-read-bilingual-faces-pao`, `am-read-gloss-face-lp2`, `am-read-results-face-uzh`, `am-read-facsimile-face-er0`); page anatomy (`am-read-page-anatomy-l0b`); `/discover` and `/lab` routes (`am-disc-journey-framework-umbg`, `am-inst-lab-route-f8f3`); share images (`am-design-og-images-pwok`).

## Requirements

### Routes and data

- Paper slugs: `light-quanta`, `brownian-motion`, `special-relativity`, `mass-energy`, and the companion `molecular-dimensions` when its record exists. Bibliographic keys (`ap-17-132` and so on) never appear in URLs.
- `generateStaticParams` comes from the compiler's paper and section projections; unknown papers or sections return the App Router not-found page.
- `/papers/[paper]/[section]` is a shareable section-first entry that keeps paper context: the section content, the paper outline, previous and next section navigation, and a link to the same anchor in the full paper.
- Each route receives only its route-local payload from `am-cm-compiler-core-oa7`; no client component imports an aggregate content module.

### Faces

| `view` | Face |
|---|---|
| `german` | Source face: German edition, term annotations, numbered equations as printed, no scan-page furniture |
| `english` | Translation face: aligned English; focusing a sentence highlights its German source |
| `gloss` | Interlinear face: German sentences with word-by-word English glosses |
| `parallel` | Bilingual face: German and English side by side (stacked when narrow) with the current paragraph's reading in a companion column |
| `reading` | Explanation face (default): the paper in the site's voice at the chosen Detail, with equations, derivation chains, and instruments in place |
| `results` | Results face: numbered results as cards |
| `facsimile` | Pinned scan via pdf.js with a page map |
| `split` | Any two faces side by side; default `parallel` on the left and `reading` on the right |

- `?view=` values outside this set fall back to `reading` without an error message and without writing an invalid value back to the URL.
- `split` accepts a validated pane pair (for example `?view=split&panes=german,reading`); invalid pairs fall back to the default pair.
- Face changes push history once (no double push), preserve other query keys and the hash, and never restart a running experiment or mount a second owner.
- Discover and Experiment are routes, not faces.

### Static generation and the no-JavaScript reader

Reading `searchParams` in a page component would force per-request rendering. Keep paper pages static:

- With JavaScript, a small pre-paint script and a client island read `?view=` and show the requested face instantly, loading that face's panel and route-local fragment on demand.
- Without JavaScript, the default reading face is fully present in the HTML, and every face link resolves to a statically generated fallback page that renders that face (for example a build-time face segment), declares the paper URL as canonical, and is excluded from sitemap duplication.
- Record the implemented approach and its trade-offs in `docs/decisions/reader-faces-static.md`.

### Canonical URLs and metadata

- `rel=canonical` for `/papers/[paper]` omits `?view=`, `?detail=`, and other state parameters; section routes are canonical for themselves without parameters.
- Titles and descriptions use the German title and the working English title; metadata comes from the paper record.
- Document URLs never multiply into an index of slider positions.

### Performance

- Faces are code split; pdf.js, Three.js, and WASM never enter the initial route's dependency graph; the initial reading route stays within 200 KiB compressed JavaScript.
- Paragraphs are not virtualized out of the DOM, so browser text search finds whole sections.

## Technical Approach

- `src/app/papers/[paper]/page.tsx` and `src/app/papers/[paper]/[section]/page.tsx` (static), `src/reader/faces/registry.ts`, `src/reader/viewMode.ts` (ported and generalized from the donor helpers with their tests), `src/reader/Shell.tsx` (server layout) and `ShellIsland.tsx` (face switching).
- Face panels in `src/reader/faces/*` loaded with dynamic imports; each receives a typed route-local payload.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All paper and section routes for the fixture corpus build statically with no dynamic rendering reported by the build.
- [ ] Every face in the table is reachable by `?view=`; back and forward buttons return to prior faces; unknown values fall back to `reading`.
- [ ] Split view renders the default pair and a validated custom pair.
- [ ] With JavaScript disabled, the reading face is present and every face link reaches a static page rendering that face with a canonical link to the paper.
- [ ] Canonical tags omit state parameters; the initial route's JavaScript is within budget.
- [ ] Unknown paper or section slugs render not-found.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests

- `viewMode.test.ts`: parsing, fallback, no double push, query and hash preservation, split pane validation (ported donor cases plus new faces).
- `staticParams.integration.test.ts`: generated params match the compiler's paper and section projections for the fixture corpus.
- `canonical.test.ts`: canonical URLs for paper, section, and face fallback pages.

### End-to-end tests

Through `am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh`: visit each face by URL; switch faces and use back and forward; confirm unknown `view` falls back; open split with a custom pair; confirm a running fixture experiment is not restarted by a face change (snapshot `runId` unchanged); JavaScript-disabled lane following face links; 320 px lane; assert the initial route's transferred JavaScript is within budget.

### Structured logging

JSON lines with `route`, `paper`, `section`, `view`, `panes`, `jsEnabled`, `viewport`, `historyLength`, `runIdBefore`, `runIdAfter`, `initialJsBytes`, `outcome`. Path: `artifacts/test-logs/reader-shell/<run-id>.jsonl`; failures retain screenshots and HTML.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- Never create `src/pages` or a second app root (AGENTS.md Rule 2).
- The interface never exposes the Cartesian product of axes as modes; faces are a small, fixed set.
- Machine-drafted translations must be visibly distinguished from reviewed ones on every face that shows them (implemented in `am-read-bilingual-faces-pao`; the shell passes review state through).

## Dependencies

Blocked by: `am-scaf-nextjs-app-bu2` (the App Router application); `am-cm-compiler-core-oa7` (route-local payloads and static params).

Unblocks: `am-read-anchors-navigation-a6o`, `am-read-detail-axis-sfc`, `am-read-bilingual-faces-pao`, `am-read-page-anatomy-l0b`, `am-read-perspective-toggle-abd`, `am-read-results-face-uzh`, `am-read-facsimile-face-er0` (all live inside the shell); `am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh` (needs real routes); `am-found-library-infra-002t`, `am-disc-journey-framework-umbg`, `am-inst-lab-route-f8f3`, `am-design-home-page-0s7s`, `am-design-papers-index-afnu`, `am-design-sources-about-zumd`, `am-design-og-images-pwok`, `am-disc-timeline-xzef`, `am-disc-bern-bridge-6euz`, `am-not-notation-page-2us`, `am-bm-kitchen-page-ny2o` (routes and layouts built on the shell).

title: Build the countermodel workbench with fair candidate models and explicit constraints
description:
# Build the countermodel workbench with fair candidate models and explicit constraints

**Epic:** `am-ep-discovery-33u` · **Batch:** batch-e · **Priority:** P1 · **Type:** feature · **Plan sections:** §14.3, §5.4, §10.6, §19.7 (traceability only)

## Background

The site teaches model selection, not retrospective ridicule. The countermodel workbench offers a small set of coherent candidate models and explicit constraints, and lets the reader discover what each explains, where each fails, or why the available information cannot distinguish them. Its three launch cases come straight from the papers: the Galilean map, locked positions, and Lorentz's ether kinematics. The fairness rules are binding: a failed alternative fails on a stated constraint or observation; an empirically equivalent alternative is not declared refuted; no rival is made to fail by programming the test with the favored conclusion; and the site never claims to have searched all conceivable alternatives.

Stop rule (shared with the hold-fixed comparison): expand beyond these cases only after the interface demonstrably distinguishes changed premises from changed representation.

## Scope

In scope: the candidates-by-constraints matrix, computed cell outcomes, drill-down explanations, the three cases, fairness copy rules, accessibility, and tests.

Out of scope: the underlying instruments (SR-04, LQ-05); the hold-fixed machinery (`am-reason-hold-fixed-comparison-xgxw`).
